A longitudinal groove in front of eye. No enlarged osseous scales behind gill opening. Attains 26 cm SL. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: A rare species that occurs in offshore reefs, often seen well above the bottom . Also taken by drive-in nets. Oviparous .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スジハナダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 20 - 150 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea to southern Japan south to Great Barrier Reef. Recently reported from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16 - 17; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7. Juveniles of this species lack the red lateral stripe . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found in or near caves and ledges of seaward reefs . Adults swim upside-down . Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

entries.name: スジハナビラウオ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 20 - 550 m . Deep-water; 49°N - 43°S, 180°W - 180°E
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: tropical and warmer temperate waters. Western Atlantic: Massachusetts, USA and northern Gulf of Mexico to South America . Reported from southern Africa .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9 - 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 23 - 28; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 23 - 28; Vertebrae : 31. Dark horizontal lines laterally . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Inhabits the open ocean . Found under floating weeds or debris. Adults were found under large weed-rafts at a depth of about 20 meters, using the shade as cover. They also form schools . Associated with Sargassum  and jellyfish .

entries.name: スジブダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 30 m . Tropical; 30°N - 32°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Thailand to New Caledonia, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Perth and New South Wales in Australia. Recently recorded from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. This species is distinguished by the following features: 5-7 (usually 6) median predorsal scales; 3 scale rows on cheek 1(5-7), 2(5-7), 3(1-4); pectoral-fin rays 13-15 (usually 14); conical teeth on side of dental plate, none in female and usually 2 on upper and 0-1 on lower of dental plates for terminal male; lips nearly covering dental plates; caudal fin slightly rounded to truncate in female and emarg
entries.biology: Found in silty coastal and offshore areas to 20 m deep . Inhabits rocky and coral reefs from tidal pools to at least 10 m deep. Form schools with 30 to 40 individuals. Grazes on benthic algae and corals . Reproductively active terminal males become bicolored .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スジブチスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 5 m . Tropical; 30°N - 23°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marshall and Gilbert islands and Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 13 - 14. Bluish or purplish spots at the posterior base of the dorsal fin. Juveniles with large ocellus that reduces with size and lacks completely in adults. The white band in young reduces to a small white saddle in large adults . Body depth 2.2-2.5 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults occur in protected inner reef flats and shallow lagoons and channels, over rubble and rocky outcrops. Feed primarily on filamentous algae . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are deposited inside empty shells or under stones or shells (Ref. 36479 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スジベラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 40 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Sagami Bay, Honshu south to Victoria, Australia and New Caledonia and east to Tonga.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 12. Body greenish with pink longitudinal lines and white barring . Body greenish with several red stripes breaking into spots posteriorly and about 8 thin vertical pale bars. A black spot rimmed with yellow on posterior margin of opercle. A black spot at posterior basal portion of dorsal fin. First 2 dorsal-fin spines with flexible tips slightly longer than other dorsal-fin spines (Ref 9823). Body shape ( s
entries.biology: Found in coastal to outer reef habitats in deep gutters or along reef margins . Inhabits rocky and coral reefs, in areas with rubble, weed and sand . Found solitary .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スジミゾイサキ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range ? - 30 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: East Asian Shelf , including Taiwan and Okinawa Island and Miyazaki Prefecture (southern Japan).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6 - 7. Five separate and goldish-yellow stripes on the body with the third stripe not meeting the fourth stripe. No dark blotch on the upper opercle but with a yellow stripe when alive. Pored lateral line scales 52 - 54 and 5 - 6 on the scaly sheath of the caudal fin. Body depth in SL, 2.84 - 3.16; suborbital depth in eye diameter 2/3. Pectoral fin tip when vented, do not usually reach to the pelvic f
entries.biology: A rare species collected from depths less than 30 meters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ススキハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 412 - 1537 m . Deep-water; 42°N - 52°S, 112°E - 117°W
entries.distribution: Circumglobal  in all tropical and subtropical waters . Eastern Atlantic: Morocco to South Africa (as expatriates in Agulhas water pockets). Western Atlantic: between about 42°N and 34°S. Indian Ocean: between 7°N and 24°S. Pacific Ocean: between 32°N and 31°S, but extends northward to 40°N in the Kuroshio Current. South China Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 18 - 21; Vertebrae : 36 - 39. Branchiostegal rays: 9-10 . Anal organs 14; male supracaudal gland has 5-8, female infracaudal gland with 2-6 small, round to oblong spots, respectively; may be distinguished from all other Myctophum possessing cycloid scales by its angulate, non-serrate, posterodorsal margin of the operculum . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: High-oceanic, nyctoepipelagic at the surface and to 950 m and generally found between 475-850 m during the day . Neustonic to mesopelagic . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae . Lipid content is 3.8 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 10.6 % in total lipids . Females reach sexual maturity at 4.8 cm, males at 3.5 cm .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 31442 ).

entries.name: スズメダイモドキ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 20 m . Tropical; 32°N - 25°S, 92°E - 171°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Thailand (Phuket), China, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea, Timor Sea (Ashmore Reef), Western Australia, Great Barrier Reef, New Britain and Solomon Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 15; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 15. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Adults occur in protected lagoon and coastal reefs around branching corals , usually with lots of algae on coral bases on the substrate . Feed on algae . Large species, to at least 18 cm . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スソウミヘビ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 134 - 139. This moderately elongate species of Ophichthus , subgenus Coecilophis is distinguished by the following characters: tail 53-58%, head 11-13% of total length and depth at gill opening 4.0-4.8% of TL; origin of dorsal-fin slightly behind pectoral-tips; pectoral fins spatulate, non-elongate and slightly less than length; large eyes, posterior margin of orbit ahead of rictus; posterior nostril a hole in upper lip and covered by a flap; small, inconspicuous head pores, SO 1+3,
entries.biology: Taken from great depths, rarely from shallow muddy bottoms. Feeds on benthic animals .

entries.name: スダレヤライイシモチ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 20 m , usually 2 - 15 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan south to Australia east to Solomon Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6 - 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Differs from C. artus by having darker stripes and fewer gill rakers, and from C. macrodon by having narrower dark stripes . Similar to C. heptazona , but lacking yellow on snout, and C. octolineatus , but without black tip on dorsal fin. Juveniles and sub-adults with large yellow area on caudal peduncle with a small black spot in its center . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: oval
entries.biology: Occurs in reefs over sand or mud bottoms. Solitary in caves to 20 m depth .
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スナエソ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range ? - 60 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan, Taiwan , and China.

entries.name: スナゴチ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 30 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marshall Islands and Fiji . Northwards to Taiwan and Ryukyu Islands, including Mariana, Marshall, and Caroline islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 13; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13. Lips smooth, lacking papillae on edges. Least interorbital width going 3.5 times or less in greatest diameter of orbit. Base of lower opercular spine concealed by scales. Anterior 1-3, usually 2, lateral line scales bearing a small spine. Iris lappet bearing short branches with bifurcate tips. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Taken over sand associated with rocks and coral reefs to about 30 m . Buries itself partially in the sand for camouflage. Feeds mainly on crabs and prawns, also on fishes. Also found in sandy fringe of coral reefs (Ref 90102).

entries.name: スナゴハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: western Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Philippines and southern Japan; west of Lydekker’s Line.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Found in shallow-water estuarine, estuaries of rivers, streams and mangroves, at depths of 0–1 m, especially in mangrove habitats . Adults also found in the sea . Feed on small fishes and invertebrates .
entries.reproduction: The male guards the clutch only as long as the young have not hatched.

entries.name: スナハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; reef-associated; amphidromous . Tropical; 30°N - 6°N
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands and Palau , and Micronesia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 12. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Found burrowing in sandy bottoms along shores and in estuaries . Of no commercial interest but may be taken incidentally .

entries.name: スベスベカスベ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 150 - 1420 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: North Pacific: Sea of Okhotsk off Abashiri, Japan to the Kamchatka Peninsula and the Bering Sea.
entries.description: This species is distinguished from its congeners in Bathyraja in having a whitish area along the inner margin of eyes; dorsal side of disc with minute fine prickles; pointed clasper with a pseudosiphon-like groove; dense, minute prickles covering smaller egg capsule . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Juveniles feed mainly on amphipods, adults feed on crabs and fish . Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsules are 7.6 cm long and 5.5 cm wide .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミクイアカカサゴ
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 180 - 704 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Andaman Sea to Fiji; north to Japan; south to New Caledonia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 4 - 6. This species is distinguished by the following set of characters: scale rows between 6th dorsal-fn spine and lateral line 8-10 (usually 9); scale rows between last dorsal-fn spine and lateral line 10-13 (11); middle postorbital scale rows 3-4 (3); caudal-peduncle depth 8.2-9.6% (moderately 9.9%) of SL; interorbital width at vertical midline of eye 19.8-24.2% (22.3%) of HL, maxillary depth 1
entries.biology: Found on the continental shelf and continental slope. Benthic . The dorsal spine contains poison glands which can inflict painful wounds .

entries.name: スミゾメスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 8 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: including Indo-Malayan Archipelago, Taiwan, and the Ryukyu Islands.

entries.biology: Adults occur solitarily or in small groups in lagoons, harbors, coastal reefs and outer reef slopes, frequently among branching alcyonarians. Also found in mangrove creeks (sometimes in freshwater), brackish lagoons and shallow reefs exposed to freshwater runoff; found well upstream in pure freshwater . Feed primarily on benthic algae. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミツキアカタチ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 15 - 149 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: central Honshu in Japan southward to Taiwan. Also found in Indonesia which is a new record for the northeastern Indian Ocean .
entries.biology: Found usually occurs in small loose groups, on muddy bottoms of fairly deep water down to 100 m, and rises vertically up to 15 m, to feed on plankton drifting over .

entries.name: スミツキアトヒキテンジクダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Vietnam, Hong Kong, eastern Philippines, Taiwan, Japan.
entries.description: Distinguished by its color pattern, dentition, gill raker counts (18-20 developed gill rakers  and flanges on the sixth and seventh ribs . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Observed from shallow coastal reef crests, among corals and in caves, often in less than 10 m depth .

entries.name: スミツキアマダイ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 51 - 65 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: East and South China seas.

entries.name: スミツキイタチウオ
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 110 - 567 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan to the Philippines, off New Caledonia and the Arafura Sea.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 90 - 92; Anal soft rays : 74 - 75; Vertebrae : 53 - 54. Distinct ocellus on dorsal fin situated immediately behind vertical line through anus, two sharp spines on posterior margin of preoperculum, ventral fins reaching halfway to anus and no vertical bars on body. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope . Uncommon species . Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass .

entries.name: スミツキカノコ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 6 - 40 m . Tropical; 20°N - 25°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Indonesia (including Mentawai Islands), Philippines, Solomon Islands, and Great Barrier Reef. Also reported from Malaysia , Tosa Bay, Japan , and Viet Nam .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 4; Anal soft rays : 9. This species is distinguished by the following characters: 3rd or 4th dorsal spines longest, 1.8-2.0 HL; pectoral rays 13-14 (usually 13); lateral line scales 33-38, scale rows above 2.5; oblique scale rows on cheek 4; gill rakers of first gill arch 5-7 + 9-11; body depth 2.7-3.0 in SL; posterior edge of nasal fossa with 1-6 spinules, 0-1 at anterior edge; upper edge of first suborbital bone with a
entries.biology: Inhabits coral-rich areas of outer reef slopes and drop-offs to depths greater than 40 m . Hides in caves or beneath ledges by day; forage for food at night, mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps. Spine of preopercle venomous.

entries.name: スミツキカミナリベラ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 13. Initial phase brownish above, paler underside marked with a series of dark spots following scale rows, often appearing as a cross-hatched pattern. Below eye with distinct yellow line. Terminal phase with olivaceous dorsally, pale ventrally, with a series of 4 large vertically elongate blackish bars on side of body from beneath pectoral fins to above first 3 anal-fin rays. A bright yellow spot posterior to upper gill opening (Ref 9823).
entries.biology: Retires in the sand at night.
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミツキゴンベ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ogasawara Islands to Oceania excluding the Hawaiian Islands.
entries.biology: A shallow water carnivore occurring around rocky and coral reefs.
entries.reproduction: Further histological evidence is needed to establish protogyny (Ref. 103751 ).

entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 30 m . Tropical; 28°N - 25°S, 94°E - 128°W
entries.distribution: Western Pacific. Eastern Indonesia (throughout the Lesser Sunda Is., the Banda Arch., Moluccan Arch., Sulawesi, and west Papua); Philippines, Palau; north to the Okinawa Is. Western and southwestern Pacific: Bismarck Arch., the Solomon Is., the Caroline Is., the Marshall Is., the Northern Mariana Is., Ogasawara, the Great Barrier Reef in northeastern Australia, the Coral Sea, New Caledonia, and Va
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 10; Vertebrae : 25. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D IX,11; A III,10; pectoral-fin rays 13; upper procurrent caudal-fin rays 6-7, lower 7-8; principal caudal-fin rays 8 + 7 (BPBM 15838 with 8 + 8); circumpeduncular scales 18-20; body depth 3.6-4.2 in SL; head length 2.5-3.1 in SL; snout length 2.9-4.0 in HL; orbit diameter 3.9-5.3 in HL; orbit diameter 1.0-1.7 in snout length; ca
entries.biology: Inhabits coral-rich areas of seaward and clear lagoon reefs . Occur solitarily or in pairs. Creates 'cleaning ' stations to which fishes come to have crustacean ectoparasites and mucus removed ; client fish Myripristis violacea .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミツキハタ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 30 m . Tropical; 29°N - 34°S, 28°E - 157°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Natal, South Africa to the central Pacific. Not known from the Red Sea nor Persian Gulf.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. A single large black blotch along middle of dorsal fin base , which can be turned off ; further characterized by head, body and fins having numerous close-set polygon shaped dark brown spots; broad zone along side of body with ctenoid scales, cycloid scales elsewhere; body with auxiliary scales; greatest depth of body 2.9-3.4 in SL; rounded caudal fin; short pelvic fins, 2.0-2.6 in head length ; he
entries.biology: Occur in outer reef flats and shallow lagoon . Reported to be taken in a trawl, thus presumably caught somewhat deeper than 7 m. Also reported to occur in reefs at a depth of about 30 m . Because of its small size and apparent rarity, it is of little or no commercial importance. Solitary (Ref 90102).

entries.name: スミツキハナダイ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 129 - 204 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Japan to Taiwan, and northwestern Australia.
entries.biology: Inhabits offshore trawling grounds .

entries.name: スミツキベラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 100 m , usually 2 - 40 m . Tropical; 24°C - 27°C ; 32°N - 32°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea to South Africa , east to the Marshall, Marquesan and Tuamoto islands, north to Japan .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 12 - 13. Juveniles and females easily recognized by the generally black body with large white spots; males have large black spots on the soft parts of the dorsal and anal fins . Juveniles resemble the juveniles of B. mesothorax but have white rather than yellow spots. Undergoes a dramatic color change with growth. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs ; common in clear shallow waters at 1-8 m; large individuals occasionally at greater depths below 27 m . Juveniles occur solitary in caves or under ledges and act as cleaners by picking at bodies of other fishes (adults occasionally do this) ; occurring regularly at depths of 14-26 m . Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled, invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Not commonly marketed. Occasionally seen in the aquarium trade.
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミツキメダマウオ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 65 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Kuril Islands and Tartar Strait to Peter the Great Bay, Japan Sea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 2; Dorsal soft rays (total): 39 - 40; Anal spines : 1 - 2; Anal soft rays : 29 - 31. Resemble B. leurolepis but easily distinguished by a distinct dark (blue when fresh) blotch on the operculum, and a smaller number of lateral line scales. Attains about 15 cm SL. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Inhabits rocky shore areas.
entries.reproduction: Pairing observed during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: スミレエビス
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 100 m , usually 1 - 15 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Aldabra and the Laccadive Islands  to the Society Islands , north to Ryukyu Islands, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef; Palau to the eastern Caroline and Marshall Islands in Micronesia.

Body color brownish to purplish red; head primarily red; upper part of opercular membrane blackish; each scale with vertical silvery white line. Four to five oblique scale rows on cheek; body depth 2.3-2.7 in SL; head length (HL) 2.4-2.85 in SL; snout length 3.75-4.35 in HL; maxilla extending posteriorly from below front of pupil to below center of the eye, upper jaw length 2.7-2.85 in HL; premaxil
entries.biology: Uncommon in atoll reef flats, lagoon patch reefs, and steep outer reef slopes. Solitary and secretive species, occasionally seen in small crevices in clear water habitats . Strictly nocturnal, feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps. Spine of preopercle is venomous. Usually among rich coral growth (Ref 90102).

entries.name: スミレガレイ
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 253 - 580 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: New Caledonia, southern Japan, and the Hawaiian Islands ; including the Norfolk Ridge and Isle of Matthew .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 106 - 117; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 87 - 95; Vertebrae : 32 - 33. Body elliptical, its depth contained more than 2.4 times in SL. Tip of isthmus below posterior margin of lower eye. Eyes separated by a broad and concave space. Interorbital in male broader than that in female. Ctenoid scales on ocular side armed with a row of hairlike spines. Small dark blotches on origin of straight part of lateral line. Small dark dots along upper mar
entries.biology: Inhabits mud and sand bottoms . Benthic . Feeds on small benthic animals. Marketed fresh, sometimes dried-salted .

entries.name: スミレスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 30 m . Tropical; 25°N - 21°S
entries.distribution: Western Central Pacific: Indonesia to Solomon Islands, north to Japan, south to northern Australia and Vanuatu.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 10 - 11. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Adults are found in lagoons, harbors, and coastal reefs, shallow habitats, deep sand or mud slopes with outcrops of debris or coral rubble pieces, or on rocky substrates in sheltered bays. This species is distinguished by having teeth in jaws; scales on central part of body of equal length and height; when fresh caudal fin colouration dusky with black-edged yellow inner margin . Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Schools in shallow waters on sandy bottom, diving into the sand when threatened . Probably taken by trawl net and handnet .

entries.name: タイワンカマス
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 25 m . Tropical; 31°N - 31°S, 31°E - 169°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf ; Red Sea to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef. The exact range is uncertain because of confusion of this species with Sphyraena obtusata . Lessepsian migrant to the Mediterranean .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 9. Body with two brown or brownish yellow longitudinal stripes which may disappear in old specimens; caudal fin yellowish . S. flavicauda is more elongate than S. obtusata and differs in dorsal fin height pectoral fin length . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits lagoon and sheltered seaward reefs ; also found in bays . Often schools on coastal reefs .

entries.name: タイワンスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 12 - 70 m . Tropical; 25°N - 25°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Maldive Island and east to Fiji and Island of Micronesia (except Marshall Is,); north to Taiwan; south to the Philippines and Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 10 - 11. Color of body grayish brown; edges of scales orangish or bluish; dorsal and anal fins with whitish spot on its posterior half; anus region blackish; upper base of pectoral with a blackish spot. Opercular margin serrate. 15-17 tubed lateral line scales. Eyes large . Body depth 1.8-1.9 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit cave openings and crevices of steep outer reef slopes in small aggregations . May also be seen singly with black corals, large sponges or gorgonian fans. Diurnal species . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 48636 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タイワンソコダラ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; non-migratory; depth range 200 - 300 m . Deep-water; 42°N - 17°N, 109°E - 146°E
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: East China Sea, off southern Japan, Taiwan, and Korea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Anal spines : 0. Snout moderately long and sharply pointed. Head ridges well developed but not especially coarse. Light organ long, extending as a black streak from the anus to just behind the isthmus. Grayish dorsally, silvery ventrally, with irregular blotches on trunk and tail. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.

entries.name: タイワンタマガシラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: from southern Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, southern China and Vietnam, south to n. and nw. Australia; also Singapore, Gulf of Thailand, South China Sea, East Malaysia, w. Indonesia, and the Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7; Vertebrae : 22. This species is distinguished by the following set of characters: head scaly except for subopercle (naked) with numerous small pores; scales on top of head reaching forward to between the anterior nostrils and snout tip; lower margin of eye tangent to a line from snout tip to upper pectoral-fin base; suborbital with a large retrorse spine (a small antrorse spine also sometimes present on
entries.biology: Usually found on sand or mud bottoms near reefs in depths up to about 30 m .

entries.name: タイワンダイ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal; depth range 50 - 200 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10 - 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8 - 9. This species is distinguished from all its congeners by the following set of characters: body deep and compressed; D XI,10 (rarely X,11); first dorsal-fin spine rudimentary (one dorsal-fin spine on first dorsal pterygiophore), the second to sixth spines (usually 5, rarely 4) are much elongated and flattened in juveniles 15-25 cm SL (second spine often reaching beyond level of last dorsal so
entries.biology: Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms . Important food fish. In Okinawa (Japan), according to local fishermen, this species usually reches more thatn 50 cm SL and a buyer from Ryukyu Is. reported that some individuals occasionally attain 65 cm SL .

entries.name: タイワンヒイラギ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal; amphidromous ; depth range 10 - 100 m . Tropical; 30°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: from India to Papua New Guinea; north to Japan; south to Australia,
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 14; Vertebrae : 24. This species of the Leiognathus splendens complex is distinguished by the following characters: no scales on cheek; anterior dorsolateral body surface almost completely scaled without a semicircular naked area on nape; lower margin of inner preopercular ridge is smooth or weakly serrated (including the neotype); interspace of pelvic keels without scales; second spines of dorsal and anal
entries.biology: This schooling species inhabits coastal waters. It feeds on fish, crustaceans, foraminiferans, and bivalves . The annotated bibliography of Leiognathidae by Pauly and Wade-Pauly  includes 172 references pertaining explicitly to Leiognathus splendens .
entries.reproduction: Lipid stored in muscles, liver and intestine decreased during gonadal maturation and following spawning (Ref. 3655 ).

entries.name: タイワンブダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 72 m . Tropical; 30°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Kenya to at least Delagoa Bay in Mozambique, and east to the Marshall and Tonga Islands. Presence in Somalia to be confirmed .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 25. General body color when fresh is greenish brown with scales finely flecked with pale; shade of white ventrally (belly sometimes dull rose or yellowish). Across the chin, 2 irregular dull reddish bars interspaced by white or yellow; upper opercular margin with a diffused dark spot. Hyaline pectorals with a yellowish flush; pelvic fins hyaline except for numerous small white spots and some
entries.biology: Found in coastal bays and deep lagoons . Inhabits seagrass beds or dense beds of algae. Well-camouflaged and easily overlooked . Feeds on these or the associated epiphytes. Caught nets and other types of artisanal gear.
entries.reproduction: Spawning at Aldabra occurs above grassflats on falling tides; protogynous hermaphroditism with both primary & secondary males occurring in the atoll's population has also been reported (Ref. 1875 ).

entries.name: タイワンメナダ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; reef-associated; catadromous ; depth range 0 - 3 m . Tropical; 35°N - 32°S, 28°E - 135°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea, south to Transkei, South Africa  and east to the Hawaiian and Marquesan islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia and Norfolk Island  and Tuamotu Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Diagnosis: Characterized by having membranous, digitate posterior margin on scales; snout shorter than eye diameter; slender maxilla and weakly curved ventrally at posterior tip, partially or completely concealed; poorly developed adipose eyelid as rim around eye; preorbital weakly concave on anteroventral edge . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Found in coastal waters but enters estuaries and rivers where they feed on microalgae, filamentous algae, forams, diatoms, and detritus associated with sand and mud . Form schools. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive . Also caught using stakenets, barrier nets, and pouch nets during spawning; also taken as bycatch . Marketed fresh and perhaps salted, boiled (Thailand), canned or frozen (Australia); roe salted .

entries.name: タイワンヤモリザメ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 60 - 90 m . Deep-water; 25°N - 21°N
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Anal spines : 0. Dorsal and sometimes upper and lower caudal-fin lobes with prominent black tips . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: A little-known bottom-dwelling shark found on the continental shelves . Possibly at depths greater than 90 m .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ).

entries.name: タウエガジ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 5 - 120 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: southern Kuril Islands and Sea of Okhotsk, Hokkaido, Japan Sea from Tatar Strait to Peter the Great Bay and central Honshu.

entries.name: タカクラタツ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 100 m , usually ? - 20 m . Tropical; 42°N - 42°S, 65°E - 132°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: India to Tahiti; north to Japan, south to Indonesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 22; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 4. Body shape ( shape guide ): other; Cross section: angular.
entries.biology: Inhabits gravel or sand bottoms around shallow reefs ; muddy estuaries and near mangroves, tolerating brackish waters . Occur singly or in pairs . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail .
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タカサゴ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 2 - 25 m . Tropical; 30°N - 27°S, 40°E - 157°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to eastern Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10 - 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13. Body light blue to brownish dorsally, white to pinkish ventrally. Broad yellow stripe just under lateral line . 4-5 cheek scales; 21-27 predorsal scales; scaled dorsal and anal fins. Upper peduncular scale rows usually 11 (11-13); lower peduncular scale rows usually 15 (14-17). Ventrolateral surface of basioccipital with a broad process for insertion of Baudelot's ligament. Post maxillar
entries.biology: Ranges widely around coral reefs. Found in schools. Feeds on zooplankton in large midwater aggregations. Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs . Also caught by drive-in nets. Valuable tuna baitfish.

entries.name: タカサゴ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 100 m . Tropical; 30°N - 32°S, 32°E - 178°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa (excluding the Red Sea and Arabian (Persian) Gulf) eastward to Fiji. Reported from the Ryukyu Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10 - 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13. Variable body coloration, dark red to silvery, paler ventrally with lateral line darker; often yellowish snout and eyes. Caudal fin tips distinctly black or reddish black . 4-5 scales on cheek; 21-29 predorsal scales; scaled dorsal and anal fins. Upper peduncular scale rows usually 11 (10-12); lower peduncular scale rows usually 15 (13-17). ventrolateral surface of basioccipital with a b
entries.biology: Ranges widely around coral reefs , sometimes forming schools with other Pterocaesio species. Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations. Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs . Also caught mostly by drive-in nets. Important tuna baitfish.

entries.name: タカサゴイシモチ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Philippines, Fiji and Carolines, north to Sagami Bay, Japan .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9 - 10. Body all silvery and translucent with a dusky midlateral band. Back margin evenly dark. Membrane between 2nd and 3rd dorsal spine blackish. Mouth strongly oblique. Margin almost straight from the origin of the 1st dorsal snout. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Common in brackish waters near river mouths where it occurs in schools; sometimes found in upper streams . Mainly marine but enters rivers .

entries.name: タカサゴスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 3 - 40 m . Tropical; 32°N - 23°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Line Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults occur singly or in small to large aggregations in passes and steep outer reef slopes . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タカサゴヒメジ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 12 - 350 m , usually ? - 60 m . Tropical; 35°N - 33°S, 29°E - 173°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Transkei, South Africa, Red Sea, Persian Gulf north to South Korea, and east to Tonga.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 7. Diagnosis: Pectoral rays 16 (rarely 15 or 17). Gill rakers 6-7 + 29-23 (total 26-30). Body depth 2.95-3.55 in SL; head length (HL) 2.9-3.25 in SL; snout length 1.75-2.1 in HL; barbel length 1.15-1.35 in HL; posterior end of maxilla evenly convex; longest dorsal spine 1.45-1.75 in HL; penultimate dorsal ray 1.05-1.25 in length of last dorsal ray; pectoral-fin length 1.25-1.4 in HL; pelvic-fin length 1.4-1.
entries.biology: Occurs singly or in small groups, over muddy, sandy, rubble, or seagrass bottoms of lagoon and seaward reefs, usually below 20 m. Flesh is fairly good for human consumption .

entries.name: タカノハハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 4 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa to the Mariana Islands, north to southern Japan; Belau, Ifaluk, and Guam in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 9. Resembles C. koumansi , but differs by having numerous small iridescent blue spots over a dark background with at least 8 transverse bars and 3 to 4 dark round spots longitudinally along the sides. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Common in fine sand or silt bottoms of shallow lagoons and coastal bays subject to terrestrial runoff at depths of 0.3 to 4 m. Uses the burrow of an alpheid species.

entries.name: タカハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 100 - 1400 m . Subtropical; 46°N - 18°N, 119°E - 153°W
entries.distribution: Widespread in the tropical and subtropical Pacific Ocean.
entries.biology: Meso- and benthopelagic at 15-100 m at night, 490-625 m during day .

entries.name: タキフグ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: South Africa to Indonesia, north to Japan, south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 10 - 12. Body covered with prickles . Brownish above with pale spots, yellowish white below; narrow dark bars on sides . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Lives in shallow coastal waters, but enters brackish waters .

entries.name: タケギンポ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 5 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan, the Korean Peninsula, and Yellow Sea to the Gulf of Po-Hai (Bo Hai, Chihli), China.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 73 - 81; Dorsal soft rays (total): 0; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 34 - 41; Vertebrae : 80 - 88. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Ranges from the intertidal zone to 5 m depth, on seaweed beds with pebble bottoms .

entries.name: タケノコメバル
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan and South Korea.
entries.description: Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Occur along rocky coasts. Viviparous .

entries.name: タコベラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 120 m . Tropical; 32°N - 21°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian and Marquesan islands, north to southern Japan, south to Vanuatu.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Body variable from brown to yellow or green mixed with various color shades or spots. Males develop long filaments on the caudal fin . Young with a broad, dark lateral stripe which breaks into dark blotches in adults, the largest above distal pectoral fins. A small dark spot behind eye. Mouth terminal or lower jaw slightly projecting. Caudal fin of terminal males rhomboid, with central rays longest,
entries.biology: Inhabits outer reef slopes or deep clear lagoons among rubble or clumps of algae; also in seagrass beds . Often in sheltered estuaries and harbors . Benthic and benthopelagic . Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タスジイシモチ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 4 m . Tropical; 35°N - 24°S, 92°E - 157°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean to the Line Islands, north to the Izu Islands, south to Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Characterized by alternating dark brown and whitish stripes, dark stripes narrower than pale ones; dark midlateral stripe extending onto caudal fin; greatest depth of body 2.7-3.1 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Common in reef flats and shallow lagoons to a depth of about 4 m. Also found in rocky reefs . Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes . Nocturnal species . Usually in pairs swimming close to shelter .
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タスジウミシダウバウオ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 8 - 25 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Japan and Indonesia.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal soft rays : 9 - 10. This species is distinguished by the following characters: body slender, its depth 12.7-16.1 (mean 14.4) % SL; adhesive disc is circular, its length 15.0-18.7 (16.8) and with 12.9-15.9 (14.4) % SL, ratio of length to width 1.03-1.25; anus posteriorly positioned, pre-anus length and disc to anus length 66.7-72.0 (68.9) and 25.7-31.6 (28.9) % SL, respectively; snout tip directed upward, usually horizontally level with lower margin of eye
entries.biology: This species is usually commensal with crinoids, rarely associated with rocky substrate near sea urchins .

entries.name: タスジコバンハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory ; depth range 8 - 66 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands  and the South China Sea. Recently recorded from the Chesterfield Islands .
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Found among Acropora spp. Monogamous .
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both obigate and social (Ref. 52884 ).

entries.name: タスジフグ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range 2 - 40 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Japan (Ryukyu Is.); photographed from Mozambique and literature record from the Phlippines..
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal soft rays : 9 - 11; Vertebrae : 18. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D 9 (10-11); A 10 (9-11); pectoral-fin rays 18 (19); vertebrae 9 + 9 = 18; colour of lateral and dorsal surfaces of head and body dark greenish-brown covered with many longitudinal white lines while the ventral surface of head and body white with light yellowish tinge; many spinules on head and body except on the lateral surface of the caudal peduncle, around mou
entries.biology: This species has been observed by SCUBA divers from 10 m to 25 m on the sandy bottom along the south coast of Amami-oshima Island of the Ryukyu Islands . Feeds on corals, mollusks, and other sand-dwelling invertebrates (2935).

entries.name: タツウミヘビ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 30 m , usually 0 - 2 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa in Tanzania, Seychelles and Mauritius , to the Society Islands (but not the Hawaiian Archipelago), north to Japan, south to Australia .
entries.description: Vertebrae : 116 - 124. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin arising well behind pectoral tips; pectoral fins teardrop-shaped; snout very short; jaws elongate; anterior nostril in a very short tube in upper lip, closely followed by an ethmoidal pore, a barbel, and the posterior nostril which is in outer lip and entirely covered by a flap; labial cirri numerous, unbranched and slender in anterior half of lip of mandible, those posterior and along lower lip branched at tips; flesh above and behind eye laterally e
entries.biology: Generally found in shallow lagoon sand, rock and broken coral substrates at depths of 0-2 m . Benthic , occurs in sandy bottoms from intertidal to over 12 m.; remains buried in sand with only the eyes protruding where it waits to ambush fish  and octopuses . Used in Chinese medicine .

entries.name: タツノオトシゴ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 20 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan and South Korea. This name has been misapplied to Hippocampus sindonis .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14. Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Inhabits Sargassum belts near shore. Used in Chinese medicine . Length type OT refers to height (= TL - head length). Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail .
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タテカブトウオ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 0 - 4740 m , usually 500 - ? m . Deep-water; 63°N - 50°S, 180°W - 180°E
entries.distribution: Circumglobal: In tropical to temperate waters; except Arctic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea. Eastern Atlantic: Gulf of Guinea and west of the Canary Islands. Eastern Pacific: California Current region . Western Pacific: Kuril Island . South China Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 2 - 3; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 13; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 7 - 9; Vertebrae : 24. Dark brown body; black head, mouth, and branchial cavity; pigmented fins. Transverse rows of scales, 28 . Gill rakers on the first arch, 14-17 . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Mesopelagic and bathypelagic at 340-1200 m depth . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae . Significant morphological variation between Indo-Pacific and other populations.
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 36655 ).

entries.name: タテガミカエルウオ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 32 m , usually 0 - 10 m . Tropical; 35°N - 35°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea to Tonga, north to southern Japan; south to Lord Howe Island; Palau, Ifaluk, and Kapingamarangi in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 15; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16; Vertebrae : 29 - 31. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XII, 14, membrane attached to caudal fin, with deep notch above last spine, first spine almost same or slightly higher than second; anal fin II, 15; pectoral rays 15; pelvic fin I, 4; caudal fin procurrent rays 10-14. Vertebrae 11 + 20. Body depth at anal-fin origin 3.2-3.5 in SL. Body depth at anal-fin origin 3.2-3.7 in SL. LL, without scales a
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing ; Adults occur in wave-swept algal ridge (Porolithon ridge) of outer reef flats. Usually found on rocky and coralline substrates at depths less than 10 m. Usually seen in small loose groups spread over sections of reef . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Have been collected as deep as 30 m in the Red Sea, 32 m at Rowley Shoals off Western Australia .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ). Urogenital orifice of male genital papilla located basally between 2 widely separated slender filaments on a fleshy swelling behind anus; testes bulbous with length equal to its width (Ref. 529 ).

entries.name: タテガミギンポ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Atlantic: Bermuda, Florida (USA), and northern Gulf of Mexico to Brazil. Eastern Atlantic: Mauritania and the Canary Islands to about South Africa. Also known in the southern parts of Mediterranean, including the following most southern localities of the northern coast: Torremolinos and Taramay near Motril (Spain), Sicily, Kyra Island (Gulf of Aigina) and near Palaea Epidavros, Peloponnes
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 15; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 17. Resembles P. yatabei but easily distinguished by a median series of cirri on nape. A short supraorbital cirrus present . Dull green or olive with dark bars on body which extend into lower part of dorsal fin . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit shallow rocky areas and tide pools. They hide in empty Strombus gigas shells , holes or troughs of rocks, or between algae . Herbivorous . Feed on invertebrates as juveniles and shift to diet of algae as adults . Unusual erectile nuchal crest . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: タテジマヤッコ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 10 - 50 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Indo-Malayan region, eastward to Vanuatu, north to southern Japan, southward to the Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 15; Dorsal soft rays (total): 15 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 16 - 17. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Inhabit shallow reef crests and deep reefs adjacent to steep slopes. Form aggregations to feed in midwater well above the bottom; harems of 3-7 individuals. Feeds on plankton. Frequently exported through the aquarium trade .

entries.name: タテスジハタ

entries.description: This large, rhomboidal skates (to at least 157 cm TL) have a triangularly shaped disc (width 44.2-63.7% TL), long head length (19.7-27.8% TL), and with rounded pectoral apices; claspers are very long and slender, the tips conspicuously bulbous, large and wide pseudosiphon present, length 20.0% of clasper, with a distinct, curved pseudorhipidion, the inner surface with a defined V-shaped cleft; ventral lobe with a rounded projection; teeth in 27-39 rows on upper jaw, 24-34 rows on lower jaw; pect
entries.biology: This species lives in deep waters, on the upper continental slope and often over fine sediment; reported to have a preference for colder temperatures than its congeners. The size at maturity for males is from 109 to 120 cm TL, for females 145 cm TL; size at birth uncertain, with the smallest free-swimming specimen measured 19 cm TL. Feeds on annelids, cephalopods, crabs, shrimps, and bony fishes, the smaller individuals consume more invertebrates . Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . The light golden brown egg cases are larg
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ).

entries.biology: Benthopelagic species found in reefs ; in coral bottoms of channels and over reef slopes ; also in areas with rubble bottom . Often in small loose groups on inner reefs in low patches of brittle corals and coralline algae mix that is shared by damselfishes and small wrasses . Herbivorous . Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade .
entries.reproduction: Bi-directional sex change has been confirmed for this species (Ref. 103751 ).

Frequently exported through the aquarium trade . Very close to Chaetodontoplus poliourus Randall & Rocha, 2009 with different colors on pelvic, dorsal and caudal fins. The two species coexist in several islands of Indonesia  including Lesser Sunda Islands, Molucca Islands, Halmahera, and Bird's Head Peninsula of West Papua .
entries.reproduction: Protogyny has been proposed for this species awaiting confirmation (Ref. 103751 ).

Capable of living out of the water for considerable time by taking air into the bronchial chambers . Feeds on crustaceans and other invertebrates and probably small fishes . Not seen in markets .

Live specimens' head and trunk sides olive-green above, becoming silvery below; snout region blackish dorsally; dorsal fin membrane with faint black blotches or small spots at each spine and ray, just above edge of scaly basal sheath, silvery anteriorly on 1st-5th dorsal spine, grading to hyaline on spinous and soft dorsal fin; anal fin scaly basal sheath silver; distal part of pelvic fin between 1st-5th
entries.biology: Adults often in clear coastal waters up to about 50 m depth; juveniles often in estuaries or lagoons influenced by fresh water ; they prefer shallow waters over sandy bottoms, from coral reefs to brackish waters . Fry about 10 cm in length enter the estuaries and stay until they reach maturity . Occur singly or in groups . Feed on small bottom invertebrates . In the Gilberts, the species forms spawning aggregations for a few days around the new moon . Sold fresh in markets; processed into fishmeal. Also taken with stake-nets .

It is further distinguished from B. parmifera by its narrower interdorsal space 0.5-1.0% TL (vs. 1.0-3.9% TL), number of precaudal and caudal vertebrae 41 and 90 (vs. 32-40 and 82-89), tail thorns 22-28 (vs. 15-23), larger orbit 4.3-5.3% TL (vs. 2.6-4.8% TL), 3 postdorsal foramina slightly smaller

entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205 ).

They feed on a wide variety of invertebrates. Also taken by drive-in nets . Oviparous . Monogamous . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .

On the day prior to spawning, female pushes her snout into the sandy bottom repeatedly and removes small stones and pieces of coral at several sites. Adhesive eggs are deposited on the sandy bottoms or in a small cavity of the reef covered with sand. Female fans the eggs and defends the nest, while male patrols around female (Ref. 86

This species is distinguished by the following characters: head 9.7% TL; tail 61% TL; mandibular pores 7; preopercular pores 4; teeth on maxilla biserial, vomer uniserial; dorsal-fin origin is slightly behind pectoral-fin tip; body without blotches or bars, melanophores gathering along lower lip; predorsal 12, preanal 46 and total vertebrae 121 . entries.name: ツマリギンポ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 15 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ryukyu and Ogasawara islands and the southern Great Barrier Reef and Lord Howe Island. Reported from Tonga  and the Marquesan Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 13; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 12 - 13. Distinguished from Entomacrodus by scalelike flaps on anterior portion of lateral line, fewer dorsal and anal fins, and more pectoral fin elements. Nasal, supraorbital and nuchal cirri simple and short. Both sexes without occipital crest. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Adults are found in the surge channel zone of exposed outer reefs. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ツマリダルマハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 90 - 1485 m . Deep-water; 55°N - 46°S
entries.distribution: Eastern Atlantic: British Isles to Namibia, also the Mediterranean (gap across region of cyclonic gyre between the South Equatorial Countercurrent and western branch of Benguela Current (5°S-13°S). Larvae, however, are not found among the cruise collections in the Agulhas Current Region . Western Atlantic: off Suriname to Brazil . Northwest Atlantic: Canada . Indian Ocean: 0°-40°S. Western Pacific
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 15; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 18 - 20; Vertebrae : 32 - 34. Branchiostegal rays: 7-9 . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Oceanic, found between 225-750 m during the day and between 90-375 m (juveniles) and 450-550 m (adults) at night. Epipelagic to mesopelagic . Widespread distribution in all oceans, limited by 10° and 15°C isotherms at 200 m and by a productivity greater than 50g Carbon per square meter per year. Sexually mature from about 5.9 cm. Spawn mainly during summer to autumn in the Mediterranean . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae . Also Ref. 58302 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 31442 ), determinate fecundity (Ref. 104737 ).

entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 67 - 76; Anal soft rays : 52 - 59; Vertebrae : 38 - 39. Upper jaw reaching to below anterior quarter of lower eye, length 2.8 to 3.3 times in head length. Head length 4.4 to 5.2 times in SL (Ref 12933). Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Feeds on small benthic animals.

Adipose very slender; pectorals small; pelvic fins large and expanded . Brown dorsally, lighter below . Brown dorsally, lighter below . Branchiostegal rays: 8 . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Synchronous hermaphrodites . Oviparous, with planktonic larvae .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 35929 ).

entries.name: ツマリトビウオ

Eastern Atlantic: Guinea to Angola . Indo-Pacific: widespread from East Africa, including the Red Sea  to southern Japan, Hawaii, the Marquesas, and Queensland (Australia); separate population in
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 12 - 14. Body iridescent greenish blue dorsally, silvery white ventrally; dorsal black except for base and posterior rays which are pale; pelvic fins greyish, other fins transparent . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Occurs in coastal waters , rare in the open ocean . Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for considerable distances above the surface. 3-4 individuals aggregate during breeding . Carnivorous . Not important as food fish, but occasionally taken by fisheries.
entries.reproduction: During breeding, a spawning aggregation composed at least of 3-4 individuals, probably 2-3 males to 1 female, were observed jumping and flying over the water surface, exuding ripe eggs and sperm in the process. Spawning on surface substrate (e.g. flotsam) when present is the usual reproductive mode but other modes may be employed if this substrate is not available. The fertilised eggs may remain s

entries.name: ツマリドクウロコイボダイ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 800 m , usually 0 - 91 m . Subtropical; 47°N - 8°N
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: in tropical and subtropical waters. Western Atlantic: Nova Scotia in Canada to Panama .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 14 - 17; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 13; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 9 - 12; Vertebrae : 44 - 51. Light brown to nearly black in color.
entries.biology: Oceanic, mostly in the upper 91 m but adults probably deeper . Occasionally strays close to shore . Young commonly inquiline in pelagic tunicates, especially Salpa and Pyrosoma . Feeds on soft-bodied medusae, ctenophores and especially salps; will also take plankton . The flesh may be poisonous .

entries.name: ツマリドングリハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 1000 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indian and Pacific: widespread in the tropical and subtropical waters. South China Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 17 - 21. Anal organs 12; mature males with large, single, black-edged supracaudal gland, about 3/4 or more of the supracaudal space; mature females with 2 infracaudal glands; has a larger supracaudal gland than any other species of the genus . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Oceanic and mesopelagic. Nyctoepipelagic at the surface . Neustonic at 0-150 m at night, 500-700 m during day . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 31442 ).

entries.name: ツマリヒメスミクイウオ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 176 - 600 m , usually 300 - 600 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: from Taiwan and the Philippines to northwestern Australia and Vanuatu where it is common but rare off Japan.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 13 - 16. This small deep-bodied species is distinguished by the following characters: convex dorsal head profile; second spine of first dorsal fin, spine of second dorsal fin, second spine of anal fin and spine of pelvic fin are serrated; A II + 7; pectoral-fin rays 14-16, pectoral length 20.3-26.5% SL; gill rakers 13-16; pseudobranchial filaments (13) 16-21; first anal-fin pterygiophore is long and straight, with broad tip and hollow; palatines and ectopterygoids are moderately wide
entries.biology: Found on the continental slope .

Dark dorsally, silvery finish on translucent flanks; fin rays colorless; black pigment at base of each dorsal and anal ray . Branchiostegal rays: 11-12 . Longer trunk and shorter tail . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Mesopelagic . Exhibit diel vertical migrations, juveniles and adults mainly at 300-600 by day and at 50-200 by night . Feed on copepods and euphausiids . Photophores developing in fishes over 12-20 mm SL . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 35800 ).

entries.name: ツムギハゼ

entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 9. Diagnosis: Characterized by pale grey body colour with three large dark brown blotches on side; head and body with faint brown scribbling; elongate and filamentous second and third dorsal spines; rounded caudal fin, slightly shorter than head; longitudinal scale series 26-30; head without scales; ctenoid body scales except cycloid on breast, base of pectoral fin and anterior part of abdomen; midline of na
entries.biology: Solitary . Found over silty  and muddy bottoms around inner reefs. Common in mangroves, entering estuaries and rivers . Toxin concentrated in the skin; contains 28.7 µg/g tetrodotoxin in the internal organs while the flesh holds 1.7 µg/g .

entries.name: ツムラカスベ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 200 - 400 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: north of Tôhoku, Japan to the Sea of Okhotsk.
entries.description: This species is distinguished from its congeners in Bathyraja in having a dark purplish brown color on both sides of the body; the spiracle is longer than eyeball and with deep concavity at their anterior part; clasper with a deep cleft; dense silky fibers cover the egg capsule . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Oviparous . Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ツラナガソコカナガシラ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: southern Japan and the East China Sea.

entries.name: ツラナガハギ

entries.distribution: Western Pacific: off Kochi Prefecture, Japan and the East China Sea. Also known from the Philippines .
entries.biology: Inhabits deep muddy substrates from about 30 meters depth, but some individuals were found drifting with large Sargassum rafts over deep water, well away from the shore .

entries.name: ツルウバウオ

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan to Taiwan.
entries.biology: Found in tide pools and under boulders in the subtidal zone.

Body shap

entries.name: テナガカクレウオ

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and the east coast of Africa  to the Society Islands , as far north as Taiwan, but not Hawaii, and probably south to Tasmania.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 33 - 38; Anal soft rays : 53 - 61; Vertebrae : 116 - 128. Eel-like, moderate to shallow body depth; maxilla free and movable; cardiform teeth present; branchiostegal membranes partly or completely united; swim bladder with thin terminal membrane or bulb; lacking enlarged dentary or premaxillary fangs, dentary diastema, pelvic fins, and swim bladder rocker bone . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: This uncommon  pearlfish inhabits the coelom and respiratory trees of some holothurians, especially Stichopus chloronotus and Holothuria argus . It is apparently in competition with Jordanicus gracilis [= Encheliophis gracilis ] for its preferred host H. argus . Although most occur singly, there is a tendency towards sexual pairing inside the host. Found to depths over 30 m . Stomach contents which include amphipod, shrimp and fish indicate non-parasitic, foraging habits . Leaves host at night to prey on small fishes and shrimps (Ref 90102).

entries.name: テナガダラ

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan (Okinawa Trough, Pacific coast southward from Hokkaido), East China Sea (off Kagoshima Prefecture), Sea of Okhotsk and Korea (off Ulsan, Gyeongsangnam-do).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Anal spines : 0. Head large; the eyes also large; head ridges well developed; the snout tipped with a blunt tubercular scute. Scales covered with short, rather broad spinules, arranged in 4 to 9 widely divergent rows. Overall color brownish, bluish ventrally on belly; the mouth and gill cavities blackish, but the latter with whitish hyoid area along its posterior margin; the fins dusky or blackish. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Feeds mainly on euphausiids, prawns, and small fishes (e.g. myctophids).

Description. D 85-94, A 64-69, pectoral-fin rays on ocular side 10-12, on blind-side 9-11, caudal-fin rays 3 + 11 + 3; pelvic-fin rays on ocular-side 6, on blind-side 6, lateral line scales

entries.biology: A little-known inshore shark . Viviparous . Taken in fisheries where it occurs .

entries.name: テンガンムネエソ

entries.biology: Oceanic  and mesopelagic, mainly at 250-650 m . Depth range from 100-700 m  and from 460-1082 m in the eastern Ionian Sea . Adults make marked vertical migrations . Found singly or in small groups . An opportunistic feeder at dusk on calanoid copepods, small fishes, etc . Sexual dimorphism with regard to body size , the males being slightly smaller than the females . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae . Occurs between 200 and 700 m depth during the day, concentrated between 350 and 550 m, and between 100 and 650 m at night, preferring a depth between 150 and 380 m Ref. 47377 ). Also Ref. 58302 .
entries.reproduction: Spawns more than once per season with egg batches about 50-500 egg/ovary pair, the number increasing with increased animal size (Ref. 4739 ).

entries.name: テンクロスジギンポ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 45 m . Tropical; 30°N - 50°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa (to False Bay, South Africa, Ref. 4404 ) to the Line, Marquesan, and Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Zealand and Rapa. Replaced Plagiotremus goslinei in the Hawaiian Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7 - 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 34 - 39; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 28 - 33. About 20 oblong segments form the dark midlateral body stripe . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs , usually the lower surge zone to deeper areas. They hide in deserted worm tubes when alarmed . They feed by attacking other fishes and removing dermal tissue, mucus and sometimes scales; occasionally makes harmless 'attacks' on divers . Some individuals usually strike from behind and quickly dive in the reef for cover to avoid punishment . Their wriggling swimming mode possibly mimics other non-scale eating species. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsules are 8.5-10.0 cm long and 5.5-6.4 cm wide .

Juveniles expatriate to tropical regions; adults mainly found in muddy estuaries where they pair. Sometimes they are seen partly buried but also feed during the day. Sometimes found floating on the surface . Sometimes occurs in seagrass areas (Ref 90102). Feeds on small benthic organisms .

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Sri Lanka and Indonesia, north to southern Japan. Reported occurrence of this species from Niue  should be verified.
