entries.name: ホシモンガラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 8 - 150 m , usually 24 - 147 m . Tropical; 30°N - 23°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Mauritius eastward through northern Australia to the Hawaiian and Society islands, north to southern Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 3; Dorsal soft rays (total): 27 - 30; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 25 - 27. Females lack the blue chins of males and yellow margins on fins. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Occur in upper margins of current-swept seaward drop-offs and ledges . Current-prone and with rich invertebrate growth such as seawhips. Usually found at moderate depths over 20 meters and occuring in small loose groups . Benthopelagic . Form loose aggregations a few meters above the bottom where it feeds on zooplankton, particularly copepods. Oviparous . Also taken by drive-in nets .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ホシヤマトミズン
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 10 - 75 m . Tropical; 35°N - 28°S, 31°E - 178°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and Mozambique to the Philippines, north to Taiwan and Okinawa (Japan), south to New Guinea, the Arafura Sea , northern Australia, and Fiji.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 21; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 12 - 23. Diagnosis: Body slender, belly rather rounded, scutes not prominent . It is distinguished from Amblygaster clupeoides and A. leiogaster by the presence of a series of 10-20 gold, in life, or black, on preservation, spots down the flank, but sometimes missing; also, lower gillrakers 33-43, while 26-33 in the other two species . Sardinops species are also round-bodied and have spots on the flank
entries.biology: A pelagic, schooling species occurring in coastal waters and lagoons , at depths of 1-75m . In Panggang Island, Indonesia it was recorded in temperatures of 28.5-29.8°C and salinities of 31.6-32.3 ppt . It feeds mainly on copepods, nauplii and zoea larvae, larval bivalves and gastropods, as well as Peridinium and Ceratium ; juveniles also on phytoplankton . Used as bait in the tuna fishery.
entries.reproduction: Spawn in school (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ホシヤリガレイ

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific, South Africa (Natal), Japan, Saya de Malha Bank, New Caledonia and Solomon Islands

This species is distinguished by the following characters: head length 4.5-5.9, body depth 2.6-3.2 in SL; upper profile steep with distinct concavity anterodorsal to eyes; snout tip pointed; pectoral-fin lenght of ocular side 6.9-12.4 in SL and shorter than head; upper jaw as long as lower eye diameter; teeth on lower jaw of the blind side in 1 or 2 rows; dorsal fin beginning above anterior nostril of blind side,
entries.biology: Feeds on benthic animals .

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Arabian Sea to southern Japan, New Guinea and New South Wales, Australia.
entries.biology: Inhabits surface neritic waters. Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

entries.name: ホソイトヒキサギ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal; depth range 1 - 22 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Indonesia and New Guinea.
entries.description: Similar to G. filamentosus with the long filament on the dorsal fin but instead of spots, it has bars along the sides .
entries.biology: Occurs in shallow inshore coastal waters on sandy bottoms and in estuaries. Maintain discrete, single species' schools .

entries.name: ホソウバウオ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 6 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific.
entries.biology: Inhabits rocky shores and coral reefs and sometimes associated with Stomopneustes variolaris  and also Heterocentrus trigonarius .

entries.name: ホソウミヤッコ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 5 - 25 m . Tropical; 32°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea to the Solomon Islands, north to southern Japan, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef; Belau [=Palau] and Pohnpei in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16 - 20; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 2 - 3. Brownish to near black in color; tip of snout pale, often with irregular pale bars on dorsum of body . Snout short with rounded dorsal ridge, and large eyes . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Collected from sand, rubble, or reef habitats to a depth of at least 14 m. Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Also found in coastal algal-rubble slopes in 5-25 m (Ref 90102).
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ホソエビス
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 20 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marquesan Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to northern Australia, New Caledonia and Rapa. Throughout Micronesia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 13; Anal spines : 4; Anal soft rays : 7 - 9. Head and body silvery, scales often with blackish spot in centre . LL scales with pale red spot and black edges . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found mainly around oceanic islands . It is an uncommon inhabitant of reef flats, lagoon and semi-sheltered seaward reefs to depths over 20 m. Occurs with N. sammara in coral-rich areas with large staghorn Acropora corals. Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates .

entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: circumtropical.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 15 - 17; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16; Vertebrae : 30 - 31. Light tan to brown in color; caudal fin dusky, other fins clear . Teeth patches on midline of roof of mouth and tongue large, broad and granular (sometimes partly obscured by mucous) (Ref 9834). Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Occurs from the border of the continental shelf to about 1,000 m depth . Found near the surface at night . Adults feed mainly on salps .

entries.name: ホソオビヤクシマイワシ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, widely distributed from East Africa to northern Australia and north to southern Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5 - 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 11; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 12 - 16; Vertebrae : 39 - 43. entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: widely distributed; Madagascar and the Maldives to Hawaii and Easter Island; north to Japan; south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. This species is distinguished by the following characters: first gill arch with one gill raker; pelvic-fin insertion is located slightly before vertical through first dorsal-fin origin; pored lateral-line scales 134-141 (modally 137), total lateral-line scales 139-148 (146); scales above 15-17 (15) and below 4-16 (15) the lateral; snout is comparatively short, its length 13.6-15.8 (mean 14.4) % SL; upper

entries.name: ホソカワインドカエルウオ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 10 - 20 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan to Papua New Guinea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 20 - 21; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 20 - 21; Vertebrae : 34 - 36. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit coral reefs . Found among the branches of both living and dead corals on a shallow coral reef . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ホソギンガエソ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 100 - 3000 m . Deep-water; 36°N - 34°S, 98°W - 154°W
entries.distribution: Eastern Atlantic: scattered records from Morocco to Mauritania, Cameroon to Gabon. Southwest Atlantic: off Brazil (27°S, 37°W). Also, Indian and Pacific Oceans.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal soft rays : 15 - 16. Body long and slender. Mouth large, gape straight . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Meso- and bathypelagic at 40-1500 m .

entries.name: ホソクロタチ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 50 - 1000 m . Deep-water; 42°N - 38°S, 180°W - 180°E
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: in central water masses. Rather rare, but relatively abundant in the northwest and southeast Atlantic and southeast Pacific Ref. 6181 ).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 30 - 36; Dorsal soft rays (total): 35 - 44; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 28 - 35; Vertebrae : 57 - 64. Body is extremely elongate and compressed. Lower jaw extends anterior to upper jaw with a small conical dermal process. Upper jaw with 3 immovable and 3 or 4 movable fang-like teeth anteriorly. Lateral line situated closer to the ventral profile than the dorsal profile posteriorly. Color is silvery with narrow dark dotted lines along the body; the gill membranes are
entries.biology: Oceanic, migrating upward at night to 100 to 200 m . Probably forming schools during daytime . Feed on crustaceans and small fish . Females mature at about 16 cm . Eggs and larvae are pelagic .

entries.name: ホソタチモドキ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 100 - 1000 m . Deep-water; 50°N - 21°N, 127°E - 117°W
entries.distribution: North Pacific: off Japan, Ryukyu Islands, Kyushu-Palau Ridge, British Columbia, Canada and California, USA.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 44 - 46; Dorsal soft rays (total): 99 - 104; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 90 - 94; Vertebrae : 149 - 153. Body silvery, jaws and opercle blackish. The inside of the mouth and gill cavities black. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Occurs from 305 m (depth of specimens hooked off Manazuru, Japan) and deeper, sometimes migrating to the surface. Juveniles mesopelagic from 100 to 500 (1000) m depth.

entries.name: ホソトビウオ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range 0 - ? m. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan  and South Korea .
entries.biology: Feeds on zooplankton.

entries.name: ホソトンガリハダカ

entries.distribution: Circumglobal. Eastern Atlantic: Mauritania to Angola. Western Atlantic: isolated individuals to 42°N in the Gulf Stream but generally from 23°N to Brazil. Indian Ocean: between 10°S and 18°S. Western Pacific: Japan , Taiwan , Australia , and New Zealand . Eastern Central Pacific: near Hawaii, and at western margin of the California Current region . South China Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 15; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 17 - 19; Vertebrae : 37 - 39. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic . Found between 475 to over 900 m during the day and between 100-500 m at night . Maximum abundance found between 300-500 m at night. Sexually mature from about 11.2 cm . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae .  Also Ref. 58302 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 31442 ).

entries.name: ホソヒゲホシエソ

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Papua New Guinea  and Indonesia . Reported from the Hawaiian Islands .
entries.biology: Mesopelagic species .  Also Ref. 58302 .

entries.name: ホソマメハダカ

entries.distribution: North Pacific.
entries.biology: Mesopelagic species .

entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 25 - 26 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.

entries.name: ホソミカズキハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 50 - 1021 m . Deep-water; 30°N - 20°S
entries.distribution: Indian Ocean: 20°N-18°S. Pacific Ocean: 30°N-20°S. South China Sea .

entries.biology: Adults occur in intertidal zones in large rock pools or coastal bays . Found near-shore ; common in tide pools . They feed on algae scraped from rubble or rock surfaces. Sometimes numerous individuals can be seen clinging to rocks out of the water when the level drops on the low of the swell. When disturbed in rock pools during low tide, they may jump out of the water to get to other rock pools or safer deeper water nearby . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .

entries.description: A large stingray with a circular disc, no thorns, a black and white mottled upper surface, and a deep and prominent ventral skin fold that extends to the tail tip . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Occurs in a wide range of habitats, from shallow lagoons to outer reef slopes . Feeds on bottom fish, bivalves, crabs and shrimp . Ovoviviparous . Smallest free-swimming specimen recorded was 33 cm WD. Caught commonly by demersal tangle net fisheries, and occasionally by longline and bottom trawl fisheries. Utilized for its meat and cartilage . Found singly or in aggregates and usually with jacks and cobia swimming near them . Not normally aggressive, but it has been responsible for at least one human fatality. entries.biology: Found in sheltered bays, harbors and lagoons . Inhabits seagrass areas or areas with hard substrates heavy with algal cover. Usually occur in small groups. entries.biology: Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs at depths of 1 to over 30 m, and relatively common along shallow reef margins with good coral cover . Usually solitary . Feed mainly on shelled benthic invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans, but occasionally take fishes . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Difficult to approach . Juveniles secretive on algae reefs and usually around stinging hydrozoans .

entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 4; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 7. Unbranched infraorbital canal, very short upward and downward branches of lateral line. Anal fin dark with many darker spots . First dorsal spine is extended with a filament in males. This species has double series of small pearly spots along lower sides .
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal bays and estuaries , over sand, mud, or dead coral rubble of lagoons and outer reef slopes. Feeds mainly on small benthic invertebrates. Usually buried in substrate. Occurs in small groups . May also be solitary .

entries.name: ミナミゴンベ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 5 - 40 m , usually 12 - 20 m . Tropical; 24°C - 27°C
entries.distribution: Western Indian Ocean: Maldives . Western Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6. Resemble C. oxycephalus but lacks spots on the tail and has a conspicuous opercular ocellus . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: A common species found in rocky and coral areas of subtidal coastal reefs . Enters shallow harbors and estuaries . Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).
entries.reproduction: Pelagic spawner (Ref. 31569 ). Spawning ascents into the water column occurred over a distance of 0.3 to 0.6 m (Ref. 26305 ).

entries.name: ミナミサルハゼ
entries.environment: Brackish; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Amamiôshima to Iriomotejima and the Philippines.

entries.name: ミナミシマウシノシタ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; anadromous ; depth range 15 - 20 m . Tropical; 31°N - 23°S, 33°E - 149°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and Persian Gulf, then off the west coast of India and Sri Lanka, eastward through the Malay Peninsula and Archipelago to China and northern Australia. Recorded from the mouth of Vivany River in Madagascar .
entries.biology: Inhabits shallow sand and mud bottoms in coastal waters. Enters brackish waters . Reported to enter fresh waters . Feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling invertebrates, especially small crustaceans . Marketed fresh, frozen and dried salted.

entries.name: ミナミシラヌイハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: offshore islands in the western Indian Ocean and from Bazaruto, Mozambique northward. Also known from Western Australia  and Japan .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 13. Yellowish in color, with white saddles and faint brown spots above; anal fin with dusky tips; chin black . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Sand-dweller, occurs in areas where freshwater streams ran dead in beach sand . Generally found with Kraemeria samoensis Steindachner, 1906. Rarely in brackish water .

entries.name: ミナミダテハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 20 - 35 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Wakayama Prefecture, Chichijima, Okinawajima, the Amami Islands, Ryukyu Islands and along the east coast of northern Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 14; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 13 - 14. Characterized by yellowish color on back grading to white on lower half; head and body with five broad brown bars; numerous blue spots on head, in pale spaces between brown bars; caudal fin with broad white upper margin; dorsal fin with blue and yellow basal stripes; pelvic fins united by low membrane at base of fins; absence of median predorsal scales; side of nape with scales extending forwa
entries.biology: Inhabits clear coastal sand slopes, but appears to be uncommon in Indonesia . Found in sand bottoms in 20-35 m .

entries.name: ミナミトビギンポ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 4 - 20 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from east Africa and Red Sea to western Australia, Taiwan, Ryukyu Is. and Ogasawara Is., Micronesia, the Hawaiian Is., the Cook Is., and the Pitcairn group.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 22 - 25; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 26 - 28. Body pale, with 8-12 narrow, short bars across dorsal surface . Dorsal saddles not reaching, even if present, a lateral band. Combined number of soft rays in dorsal and anal fins usually 44 to 51 (Ref 12874). Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Benthic in surge-swept sand patches and shorelines . Found in sea bottoms with coarse sand and fine gravel 4-20 m deep . Occurs in small groups that bury themselves in coarse sand patches on reef corners subject to currents .

entries.name: ミナミニベ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: China seas.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 26 - 29; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 7. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal waters . An important foodfish.

entries.name: ミナミハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous ; depth range 0 - 5 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Asia: India to the Philippines and north to Japan. Oceania: Fiji ; French Polynesia ; and, New Caledonia and Vanuatu .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 10; Vertebrae : 26. A black ocellus on the posterior part of the first dorsal fin. Upper jaw thick and slightly extended. The cheek and upper portion of operculum scaled. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Found on fine gravel bottoms from estuaries to fresh water of rivers.

entries.name: ミナミハタ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 10 - 120 m , usually 25 - 120 m . Tropical; 28°N - 24°S, 46°E - 156°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: scattered insular localities from the Comoros to the Line Islands. Unknown from the Red Sea, coast of East Africa, Sri Lanka, Australia, New Guinea, and the larger islands of Indonesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8 - 9. Characterized by yellow to greenish yellow color; head, body and fins with bright blue stripes; body scales ctenoid, including abdomen; pelvic fins, 1.5-1.9 in head length; greatest depth of body 2.7-3.1 in SL; truncate caudal fin to slightly emarginate ; eye diameter subequal to interorbital width and about twice the depth of the preorbital; rounded preopercle, finely serrate, lower edge with 1
entries.biology: Sporadic distribution . Occurs only at oceanic islands. Inhabits clear waters of steep drop-offs; rarely seen in less than 30 m. It has been taken in depths of 120 m and may occur deeper. Also found in caves and crevices. Often swims upside-down against the roofs of caves or archways . Feeds on fishes and crustaceans . Solitary (Ref 90102).

entries.name: ミナミハタンポ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.
entries.biology: Nocturnal species. Juveniles form large schools. Tasty food fish.

entries.name: ミナミハリダシエビス
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 143 - 274 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indian Ocean: Saya de Malha ; off Somalia . Mediterranean Sea: Nazareth Banks . Northwest Pacific: Kyushu-Palau Ridge .

entries.name: ミナミハリダシエビス
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic. Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: from the Kyushu-Palau Ridge, North Pacifc Seamount Chain; probably more widespread.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8; Vertebrae : 27. This species is distinguished from its congeners by the following set of characters: D V,13; A III,8; ventral scutes 10; scale rows in longitudinal series 72; pored lateral-line scales 31; scale rows between last dorsal fin spine and lateral line 11; a striated area ending near mid-point of caudal peduncle, its length on caudal peduncle 43.2% of caudal peduncle length; posterior interorbi

entries.name: ミナミヒメコダイ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; non-migratory; depth range ? - 118 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan  to Australia.
entries.biology: Occurs in the continental shelf over soft bottom .

entries.name: ミナミヒメジ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 5 - 100 m . Tropical; 26°C - 29°C; 32°N - 33°S, 28°E - 137°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Persian Gulf ; Red Sea south to East London, South Africa and east to Micronesia and the Hawaiian, Marquesan, and Society islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 7. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D VIII,9; pectoral fins 15-16; gill rakers 7-8 + 19-21 = 27-29; lateral line scales 36-38; body depth at first dorsal fin origin 25-29% SL and at anal-fin origin 21-24% SL; caudal-peduncle depth 9.9-12% SL; maximum head depth 21-26% SL; head depth through eye 18-20% SL; head length 30-31%SL; orbit length 7.0-8.7% SL; upper jaw length 11-13% SL; ba
entries.biology: Euryhaline . Inhabits sandy lagoons and sheltered coastal waters. Also found over muddy bottoms . Benthopelagic . Often in groups . In the north-east coast of India, the male to female ratio was 1:1.5 in most months . Feeds primarily on small crustaceans. Marketed fresh .

entries.name: ミナミヒメハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous ; depth range 0 - 5 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa to the Philippines , north to Japan , south to northern Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 7 - 8. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Usually in small groups . Found over sandy and muddy bottoms, often in weedy areas of intertidal zone; also in mangroves, estuaries, lagoons and rivers .

entries.name: ミナミフエダイ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 80 m . Tropical; 31°N - 30°S, 30°E - 174°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 14; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Dorsal profile of head steeply sloped. Preorbital width equal to eye diameter or larger. Preopercular notch and knob poorly developed. Scale rows on back parallel to lateral line. Center of each scale often with a reddish-brown spot, giving an overall appearance of series of horizontal lines on side of body. Generally yellow with a bronze to silvery sheen, shading to silvery white on belly and unde
entries.biology: Adults probably frequent coral reef areas; juveniles found in mangrove estuaries . Feed on fishes and benthic invertebrates including shrimps, crabs and cephalopods. In Hong Kong live fish markets .

entries.name: ミナミフトスジイシモチ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 50 m . Tropical; 30°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Western Indian Ocean: Mozambique , Red Sea and Christmas Island to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia and Rapa.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Characterized by having dorsal fin rays VII-I, 9; anal fin rays II,8; pectoral fin rays 14; pelvic fin rays I, 5; pored lateral line scales 24; predorsal scales 4; circumpeduncular scales 12; total gill rakers 24, developed gill rakers 18; snout pointed; body white in color . Further characterized by alternating black and yellow stripes, dark stripes wider; greatest depth of body 2.6-3.1 in SL . Body shap
entries.biology: Occurs on reef flats and shallow lagoon reef, usually seen singly or in pairs under ledges or in crevices. Feed on small benthic invertebrates at night .
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ミナミミミズアナゴ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 19 m . Tropical; 30°N - 15°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Persian Gulf , Red Sea  and East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia; Caroline and Marshall islands in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 0; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 0. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Found in reef flats and lagoons to at least 13 m. Burrows in soft bottoms . Benthic . Caught in bags or nets, or by digging . Used as shark bait .

entries.name: ミナミヤリエソ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 300 - 2626 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Bay of Bengal , Solomon Sea , New Zealand , and Japan . Southeast Pacific: Chile . South China Sea
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 12; Anal soft rays : 27; Vertebrae : 46. Body moderately elongate, deep strongly compressed. Body and head naked. Skin smooth, delicate and easily torn. Head and body dark brown with brassy green iridescence in alcohol . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.

entries.name: ミナミワニギス
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 0 - 267 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, and Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 4 - 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 23; Anal soft rays : 16 - 21; Vertebrae : 29 - 33. Distal third of first dorsal fin black. A row of 5 to 7 pairs of sensory papillae on dorsal surface of head from snout to interorbital. Sensory papillae between eyes not arranged in a semicircle (Ref 12850). Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Rarely caught by trawl net .

entries.name: ミノカエルウオ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m , usually ? - 10 m . Tropical; 35°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: South Africa to Kiribati, north to Japan , south to Rowley Shoals and the southern Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 15; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16; Vertebrae : 29 - 31. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XI-XIII (usually XII), 13-15, deeply incised above last spine, first spine almost equal to second; anal fin II, 14-16 (usually 15); pectoral rays 15; pelvic fin I, 3; caudal fin procurrent rays 9-12. Vertebrae 10 + 19-20; last pleural rib on 11th, last epipleural rib on 15-19th vertebral centrum. Without scales and scalelike flaps. LL tubes 2-9
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Occur in algal ridge and ridge crests between surge channels of exposed seaward reefs to a depth of about 3 m . Benthic . Feed on algae and associated minute invertebrates like forams, ostracods, and gastropods. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ). Urogenital orifice of male genital papilla located basally between 2 widely separated slender filaments on a fleshy swelling behind anus; testes bulbous with length equal its width (Ref. 529 ).

entries.name: ミハラハナダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: collected from the Izu and Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan.
entries.biology: Caught by handline from fairly deep water over rocky bottom. Food fish.

entries.name: ミホハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 350 - 1000 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Southeast Atlantic: in Agulhas water pockets. Indo-Pacific and Southeast Pacific. South China Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 12 - 14. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Oceanic and mesopelagic, found below 200 m at night .

entries.name: ミミズアナゴ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 30 m . Tropical; 32°N - 28°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: widespread, from East Africa to Samoa, north to Okinawa-jima Island, Japan, excluding the Red Sea and the coast of Australia.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 118 - 135. This species is distinguished by the following set of characters: 2 infraorbital pores found at the postorbital area; median ventral groove on the snout absent; acute snout; rictus of mouth slightly posterior to a vertical line through the posterior margin of the eye; pointed conical teeth on upper jaw and vomer, arranged biserially on upper jaw, uniserially on vomer; dorsal-fin origin posterior to a vertical line through the anus, horizontal distance between the origin an
entries.biology: Lives in loose sand and fine gravel . Benthic  and burrowing species found in inshore waters . Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans .

entries.name: ミヤケテグリ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 30 m , usually 3 - 30 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: widespread in the area. Replaced by Synchiropus stellatus in the Indian Ocean .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 4; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 10; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 7 - 8; Vertebrae : 20 - 21. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal reef slopes, usually on rubble and sand near large coral formations . Found in small loose groups and usually a large male dominates sections of reef . Small groups occur with one adult male .

entries.name: ミヤケベラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 55 m , usually 7 - 55 m . Tropical; 24°C - 27°C ; 33°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to American Samoa, north to Izu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 10. Scales on lateral line: 46-49 (+2 past hypural) . Juveniles are black with several white pinstripes; females become lighter dorsally, and males develop golden centered scales, blue lines on the face, and a wedge-shaped white area in the center of the tail . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Uncommon inhabitant of coral-rich areas of clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs . May form small groups . Males generally solitary . Juveniles are cleaners while adults feed on coral polyps . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ミヤコイシモチ
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan and the Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Body yellowish-brown with small indistinct milky spots, the coloration varying with habitat. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found among Zostera colonies.
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ミヤコキセンスズメダイ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 12 m . Tropical; 32°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to Marquesan and Society islands, north to Japan, south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13. This species occurs in 2 basic color phases: a blue-backed ( leucopoma ) phase and a gray to black ( amabilis ) phase usually with 2 light bars . Large blue-edged black spot at end of dorsal fin base, and yellow form with black spots at end of dorsal fin and its base . Body depth 2.3-2.5 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Adults occur in rubble-strewn surge channels, the outermost reaches of exposed reef flats, and the upper submarine terrace at 12 meters. Territorial but they generally occur in groups, and remains close to shelter. Feed mainly on benthic algae and small crustaceans . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ミヤコヒゲ
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Kyushu-Palau Ridge.

entries.name: ミヤコベラ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 40 - 80 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and Persian Gulf south to Mozambique and Mauritius; also Indonesia and southern Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 10.
entries.biology: Usually solitary . Found on deeper coral and rocky reefs. Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins . Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: ミヤラビハゼ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated. Tropical; 30°N - 20°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman  to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Indonesia. Recently recorded from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16. Body yellowish brown with a black longitudinal stripe and a bright blue spot between dorsal spines 5 and 6. SL to 25 mm . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits mangrove swamps and inlet waters ; shallow coastal waters with mud, sand, or rock bottoms . Forms aggregations near surface .

entries.name: ムカシデメニギス
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; oceanodromous ; depth range 400 - 800 m . Subtropical; 55°N - 35°N, 140°E - 120°W
entries.distribution: Eastern Atlantic: off Azores Island. Northeast Pacific: British Columbia, Canada  to central California . Northwest Pacific: Kashimanada Sea, Japan .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 16; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 10 - 14; Vertebrae : 78 - 84. Branchiostegal rays: 2.
entries.biology: Oceanic. Eggs and larvae are pelagic . Oviparous . Bathypelagic at about 400-800 m .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 35626 ).

entries.name: ムカシハダカ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 100 - 500 m . Temperate; 48°N - 46°N
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: off Tôhoku in Japan. Northeast Pacific: south of southern California to Washington . Also widespread in the transition region between the subarctic and central water masses of the North Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 13; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 19 - 24; Vertebrae : 36 - 38. Branchiostegal rays: 8-9 . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Epipelagic to mesopelagic . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 31442 ).

entries.name: ムカシヤリエソ
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 400 - 1000 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: in tropical and subtropical waters. Absent in the Mediterranean and in the eastern tropical Pacific. Widespread in the Eastern Central Atlantic but recorded mainly between 5°N and south of the equator. South China Sea .
entries.biology: Mesopelagic at ca. 100-1000 m . Larvae ( 4763 ). Feeds on other midwater fishes. Synchronous hermaphrodites .

entries.name: ムギイワシ
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 3 m . Tropical; 30°N - 18°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Southern Japan in Ryukyu Islands and south to northern Queensland, Australia. Has been collected close to the islands in Micronesia, Melanesia, Fiji and New Guinea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 4 - 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 13; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 13 - 15. Mouth barely protractile and with thin lips. Basihyal and mesopterygoids usually with teeth. No notch present at the anterior border of preopercular bone. Face with Shangreen denticles. Ascending process of premaxilla with no lateral processes present. Distal end of maxilla blunt and truncate. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: oval.
entries.biology: Loose aggregations inhabit tide pools and rocky shorelines and reef margins. Eggs are large.

entries.name: ムグラヒゲ
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; non-migratory; depth range 200 - 600 m . Deep-water; 8°C - 12°C ; 35°N - 28°N, 126°E - 139°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: South China Sea, off Taiwan to Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 2; Anal spines : 0. Snout slightly long and pointed, with broad triangular naked areas on the dorsal surface; the terminal scute small, poorly defined in larger individuals. Overall color is light brown with a large ocellated black blotch above and behind the pectoral fin bases; a fainter saddle just below the anterior end of the second dorsal fin extending 2 to 3 rows below the lateral line. The mouth cavity whitish; the gill cavity blackish; the fins generally dusky exce
entries.biology: Captured at depths from 200 to more than 600 m . Feeds primarily on polychaetes with crustaceans of minor importance .

entries.name: ムサシトミヨ
entries.environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic. Temperate
entries.distribution: Asia: Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7 - 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 12; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 8 - 11; Vertebrae : 31 - 34. This species is distinguished from its congeners by the following set of characters: dorsal-fin rays IX (VII-IX) + 11 (8-12); anal-fin rays I + 10 (8-11); pectoral-fin rays 10 (8-10); pelvic-fin rays I + 1 (1 or 2); procurrent caudal-fin rays 5 (4-6) + 5 (4-6) = 10 (8-11); lateral plates in an incomplete row (0–2 lateral plates on anterior body, 3-8 plates on caudal pedu

entries.name: ムシクイアイゴ
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m , usually 0 - 15 m . Tropical; 19°C - 38°C ; 30°N - 30°S, 77°E - 20°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: India, Sri Lanka, Andaman Islands, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Belau [=Palau], Guam, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Vanuatu, ?New Caledonia, ?Western Australia, ?Pohnpei, Caroline Islands, ?Ebon Island and Marshall Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 7; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 13. Body bluish white; head brown to brownish or golden yellow with irregular blue lines. Preopercular angle 91°-102°; strong overlapping scales cover cheeks; midline of thorax scaled, not pelvic ridges. Anterior nostril with low flange, broadened slightly posteriorly. Spines stout, blunt or pungent, and venomous. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Juveniles live among mangroves then move out to lagoon and coastal reefs as they mature. Forms schools. Feeds on algae growing on seagrasses, mangrove roots and rocks. Adults congregate inshore in groups of several hundreds to spawn in summer. Spawning is by pairs; sticky eggs laid on the bottom. Its very high quality flesh commands premium prices . Adults on coastal reefs, subject to strong currents . This species can tolerate very low salinities (2 ppt) and temperatures up to 38 C .
entries.reproduction: Throughout summer, adults form inshore breeding groups of several hundred individuals on the 7th or 8th days of the lunar month; pairs break from these groups to spawn. The species has a high fecundity of 350,000/spawning season.

entries.name: ムシフグ

Potential predators include Squalus acanthias , Sebastes taczanowskii , and S. trivittatus , sea scorpions Myoxocephalus , and cormorants . Oviparous, eggs are guarded by the male .

Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . entries.biology: Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms; also in sheltered estuaries . Feeds mainly on crustaceans and small fishes. Principal catch in the Taiwanese pair-trawl fishery off the coast of northwestern Australia. Good food fish .

entries.biology: A predominately pelagic schooling species . Occasionally seen in small groups along reef slopes adjacent to deep water in pursuit of zooplankton . Adults feed mainly on small invertebrates . Marketed fresh and salted or dried .

Nests are found in small patches of loose sand under ledges or at the base of slopes . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

Feed on crustaceans, mollusks, worms, heart urchins and foraminiferans. Consumed fresh or dried. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874 .

They enter small holes, with just its head protruding. They feed on algae and associated detritus and small invertebrates. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 90102 .

But the biggest males swim over large areas and move away quickly when approached by divers rather than diving into the bottom .

entries.biology: Common in large schools along sandy shorelines and reef margins. Reported to be mainly a nocturnal species which usually forms schools (from several hundred to more than 100 m long and 20 m wide) . Feeds mostly at night when the school disperse. Feeds on a variety of planktonic crustaceans. Preyed upon by sharks, tunas, long toms, and amberjacks which swim alongside the school. Among its other predators are crested terns, gannets, sea-gulls and herons. Slow moving and not well regarded as bait. Extremely important as forage fish for larger species . Sold fresh, or salted and dried . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178 .

Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans  and benthic invertebrates, primarily polychaetes .

Juveniles from about 2.5 cm length inhabit shallow waters over muddy substrates . Feed on a broad range of prey dominated by fish, and with small amounts of crustaceans, cephalopods and other benthic invertebrates . They forage mostly at night . They are marketed either gilled and gutted, whole as fillets, as fresh chilled or frozen product .

entries.biology: Adults inhabit both coastal and offshore reefs. They tend to be associated with sponge and gorgonian-dominated habitats on the North West Shelf , and hard mud areas of the Arafura Sea. In Australia, they frequently form mixed shoals with L. erythropterus . Juveniles tend to inhabit shallow inshore waters and larger fish live in deeper waters . Juveniles also occur in mangrove areas and seagrass beds . Feed mainly on fishes, with small amounts of benthic crustaceans, cephalopods and other benthic invertebrates . They forage mostly at night . Caught mainly with handlines, bottom longlines, and bottom trawls . Marketed fresh, dried-salted  and frozen .

entries.biology: Sedentary . Inhabit intertidal zone to depths of at least 25 m on both lagoon and seaward reefs. Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' . Voracious carnivore, attracting prey with front of their cavernous mouth by wriggling their baitshaped first dorsal spine (lure) .

entries.biology: Solitary or in pairs . Adults inhabit coastal reefs and lagoons on sand and rubble margins of algal reefs and sometimes near seagrass beds . Feed by sifting mouthfuls of sand and expelling it through the gills, to capture small invertebrates, organic matter, and large quantities of algae. Monogamous . Spawning is synchronous with semilunar periods . Eggs are deposited in burrows which are tended by the male parent . Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115 . Also Ref. 58652 .
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both facultative and social (Ref. 52884 , 58559 ). Although a few pairs changed partners, most pairs remained together over successive rounds of spawnings according to a study (Ref. 84980 ). Spawning cycle is semilunar. entries.summary: ホッキョクガンギエイ (学名：Amblyraja hyperborea) は、ガンギエイ目に分類されるエイの一種。世界中の冷たい海に分布する底魚。
entries.morphology: 体盤は菱形で、吻は少し長く、尾は非常に短い。頭部から尾の先にある背鰭まで、背面の正中線上に棘が並ぶ。背面は灰色から茶色で、小さな丸い斑点が散らばる。腹面は白く、暗色の模様があるか、褐色で、白い模様がある。全長は最大112 cmだが、大型に成長することは稀である。
entries.ecology: 様々な底生生物を捕食する。繁殖様式は卵生で、角に突起のある卵を砂地や泥地に産む。出生時は全長16 - 18 cm。寄生虫は線虫類のAnisakis simplex、Metanisakis tricupola、Schistobrachia ramosaが知られる。
entries.distributionJa: 北極海、カナダ、ヨーロッパ北西部、北太平洋、ニュージーランド、南極大陸周辺等、世界中の冷たい海域に分布する。水深300 - 2925 mの大陸斜面に生息する深海魚で、海底付近に多い。

entries.description: Grey-brown with large dark blotches . Tail very short . Mid-dorsal row of stout thorns which extend from nuchal region to first dorsal fin. Thorns close posterior to the pelvic girdle larger than along the tail . Upper surface dark mouse gray, dark blue gray or dark brown with small rounded spots. Lower surface white and sooty in variable patterns . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Found on the lower continental slope , probably most common on deep slopes and at abyssal depths . Benthic ; meso- to bathybenthic, on muddy substrate . Adults feed on all kinds of bottom animals . Prefer polar temperatures from hatching to maturity and eggs are incubated successfully and regularly in water as cold as 0°C . Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsule measures 81-125 mm long and 50-80 mm wide . Hatching size at 16-18 cm TL  (15 cm long in Ref. 119696 ).
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ).

entries.biology: Adults seek shelter among rocks in subtidal areas  and will occupy the same shelter until driven out by larger wolf-eels or a large octopus . Juveniles are pelagic for up to two years . Feed on hard-shelled invertebrates and fishes . Both male and female wrap their body around the egg mass to keep the eggs in place and to deter predators . Large specimens can inflict a painful bite . Its flesh is tasty .
entries.reproduction: When courting, the male wolf-eel butts his head against the female's abdomen, wraps around her, and fertilizes her eggs as she extrudes them. Eggs are laid and both male and female wrap themselves around the egg mass to protect it . Only one parent at a time leaves the eggs to feed. The female periodically rotates the eggs until they hatch. A male and female may pair for life (Ref. 28499 ).

entries.biology: Adults inhabit freshwater streams and pools, preferring marshy habitats , in rivers and creeks, commonly over rock bottoms and in deeper pools and move as young to estuaries and seas . Seldom found in large rivers . Restricted to lowland (coastal) reaches of river systems . Adults descend to the sea to spawn (Refs. 52331 , 79840 ). They feed on small fishes, crustaceans and mollusks. Reported to breed east of Madagascar; the south equatorial current probably carries the eel larvae and elvers towards the east coast of Africa where local coastal currents guide the elvers to suitable rivers which they invade and they stay there until sexually mature, when they return to their breeding grounds .

entries.biology: Occurs in coral-reef slopes in the protected bays, found solitary on muddy or sandy-mud bottoms with dead-coral rubbles under the heavy growth of corals .

entries.name: Auxis rochei
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; pelagic-neritic; oceanodromous ; depth range 10 - ? m . Tropical; ? - 28°C ; 61°N - 51°S, 180°W - 180°E
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific (Western): including the Mediterranean Sea. The eastern Pacific population is recognized as subspecies Auxis rochei eudorax . Highly migratory species.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9 - 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 13; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 12 - 14. Back bluish, turning to deep purple or almost black on head. Scaleless area with pattern of 15 or more fairly broad, nearly vertical dark bars. Belly white. Pectoral and pelvic fins purple, their inner sides black. Body robust, elongate and rounded. Teeth small and conical, in a single series. Pectoral fins short, not reaching vertical line from anterior margin of scaleless area above cor
entries.biology: Adults are principally caught in coastal waters and around islands . Form schools. Feed on small fishes, particularly anchovies, crustaceans (especially crab and stomatopod larvae) and squids. Eggs and larvae are pelagic . Because of their abundance, they are considered an important element of the food web, particularly as forage for other species of commercial interest. Also caught with encircling nets and troll lines . Marketed fresh and frozen  and also dried or salted, smoked and canned .
entries.reproduction: Fecundity ranges between 31,000 and 103,000 eggs per spawning according to the size of the fish.

entries.name: Banjos banjos
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 50 - 400 m . Tropical

entries.biology: Occurs inshore .

entries.name: Barathronus diaphanus
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 579 - 2030 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Madagascar to Japan and Tonga.

entries.biology: Rare species .

entries.name: Barbatula nuda
entries.environment: Freshwater; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Asia: China, Korea and Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal soft rays : 8; Vertebrae : 40 - 42. Distinguished from all other species of Barbatula from northern Asia by having an upper lip with a marked and deep median indention (vs. slight and shallow) and a nearly scaleless body or scales only on the caudal-fin base (vs. body scaled posterior to the dorsal-fin origin or a fully scaled body). Can be further diagnosed from B. dgebuadzei in having closely-set nostrils (vs. widely separated) and 40-42 vertebrae (vs. 43-45)
entries.biology: Facultative or obligate air-breathing

entries.name: Barbatula toni
entries.environment: Freshwater; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Asia: all rivers flowing to the Arctic and Pacific Oceans between the Ob and the Huang He.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal soft rays : 8; Vertebrae : 42 - 43. Together with Barbatula altayensis and B. sawadai , this species differs from all other congeners from northern Asia by having the body scaled predorsally (vs. body scaled posterior to the dorsal-fin origin, or scales only on the caudal-fin base). It can be distinguished from B. altayensis and B. sawadai in having widely separated nostril (vs. closely-set) and further from B. altayensis in having 42-43 vertebrae (vs. 44-45),
entries.biology: Facultative or obligate air-breathing

entries.name: Bassozetus levistomatus
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 3965 - 5200 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian and Pacific: restricted to abyssal depths globally..
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 114; Anal soft rays : 93; Vertebrae : 65. Snout inflated; eyes much smaller than snout; opercular spine weak or absent; preopercle without spines and posteriorly expanded almost reaching posterior margin of opercle; pseudobranchial filaments 2 .
entries.biology: Specimens were apparently caught on or near the bottom at abyssal depths . Rare species . Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass .

entries.name: Bathyclupea nikparini
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 505 - 515 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwestern Pacific: Japan and possibly to the Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal soft rays : 36; Vertebrae : 31. This species is distinguished by the following characters: lightly colored oral cavity; standard length 4.4 times as great as the maximum body depth and 3.2 times as great as the head length; dentate ventral branch of the praeoperculum; A 36; developed gill rakers 23-24; last pair of pleural ribs reduced . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.

entries.name: Bathycongrus wallacei
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 250 - 500 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: southern Mozambique to Natal, South Africa ; Japan, Philippines and Indonesia .
entries.description: Vertebrae : 168 - 181. Grey dorsally, lighter ventrally, median fins black posteriorly . Dorsal fin origin above first quarter up to first third of length of pectorals. 1-2 enlarged vomerine teeth on elevated base; the largest vomerine tooth larger than intermaxillary teeth. In adults, the posterior nostril is in front of upper part of eye . Predorsal vertebrae 9. Preanal pores 37-43. Dorsal rays before anus 59-67 . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Collected using beam trawl .

entries.name: Bathygobius meggitti
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 8. Characterized by male with yellowish grey color, densely and diffusely mottled with dusky, bluish whit and dull orange spots; female with dark grey brown color dorsally, paler ventrally, with five large yellowish white blotches dorsally from nape to caudal peduncle; broadly yellow outer part of first dorsal fin in both sexes; upper 5-6 pectoral rays free of membrane; rounded caudal fin; longitudinal scale
entries.biology: Inhabits rocky pools of intertidal zone and rocky shores . Specimens collected from tide pools of exposed coasts . Feeds on planktonic crustaceans, polychaetes and algae .

entries.name: Bathyonus caudalis
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 1524 - 4040 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: equatorial Indian Ocean, off Panama and New Caledonia; Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 100; Anal soft rays : 80; Vertebrae : 63. Body depth 9.5 or less in SL; head length about 1/2 preanal length; branchiostegal rays 8-9; no prominent spines on top or side of head; lower pectoral rays free and stronger than upper ones; caudal fin rays 6; precaudal vertebrae 17-19 .
entries.biology: Benthopelagic at bathyal and abyssal depths . Uncommon species . Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass .

entries.name: Bathyraja andriashevi
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 1390 - 2004 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan  and Indonesia .
entries.biology: Oviparous . Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bathyraja fedorovi
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 447 - 2025 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Sea of Okhotsk and Pacific coast of Japan.
entries.biology: Oviparous . Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bathyraja maculata
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 70 - 1200 m , usually 400 - 700 m . Deep-water; 2°C - 6°C ; 59°N - 51°N
entries.distribution: North Pacific: southern Sea of Okhotsk to the eastern Gulf of Alaska, including the Bering Sea, the waters off the Kuril and Aleutian Islands, and eastern Kamchatka.
entries.description: This species is distinguished from its congeners Bathyraja in having a white blotches of different sizes on the dorsal surface of the disk, lateral folds of tail are broad; clasper has a large pseudosiphon; dense silky fibers covering egg capsule . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Exhibited migratory pattern of going toward greater depths during colder months for overwintering, while in the warm period, this species predominantly fed at shallower depths Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsules are 10.19 cm long and 6.28 cm wide .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bathytoshia brevicaudata
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal; non-migratory ; depth range 0 - 476 m , usually 0 - 200 m . Temperate; 15°C - 29°C
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: antitropical; from southern Africa to New Zealand, and off Japan and Peter the Great Bay (eastern Russia).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0. This species is huge, plain-coloured, with a disc broad and rhombic, belly with transverse groove, tail short tapering strongly before caudal sting, thorns when present are confined to tail before sting, pectoral fin with an oblique rows of white spots dorsally; disc width ca. 1.1-1.2 times its length, very thick trunk; narrowly-rounded pectoral-fin apex; short snout, obtuse with tip barely extended and anterior margins weakly convex; small eyes with orbit length and sp
entries.biology: Adults occur offshore, on the outer shelf and uppermost slope; sometimes close inshore , in very shallow ( 0 m) depths . Found on sandy bottoms, in bays, harbors, and near rocky reefs . Often in aggregations . A study on migration shows horizontal movement of less than 25 km but shows a seasonal shift to deeper waters towards winter . Food includes fishes, bivalves, squid, and crustaceans . Ovoviviparous . Reputed to be the largest stingray in the world weighing more than 350,000 g . This species frequently raises its tail in a scorpion-like fashion when approached, but is considered more as inquisitive rather than aggressive . The barbed tail however can inflict a severe or potentially fata
entries.reproduction: Exhibit ovoviparity (aplacental viviparity), with embryos feeding initially on yolk, then receiving additional nourishment from the mother by indirect absorption of uterine fluid enriched with mucus, fat or protein through specialised structures (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace (Ref. 205 ). During courtship, the male will hold onto the pectoral margin of a female (sometimes for hours)

entries.name: Bathytoshia lata
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 1 - 800 m , usually 40 - 200 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Eastern Atlantic: southern France to Angola, including the Mediterranean Sea. Indo-Pacific: widespread, from southern Africa to Hawaii.
entries.description: This species is huge, plain-coloured, with a disc broad and rhombic, has sharp thorns over its disc and tail in adults; it is moderately elongate, with gently tapering tail to caudal sting, a slender ventral tail fold and a minute dorsal fold; disc width ca. 1.2-1.3 times its length, very thick trunk; narrowly-rounded to angular pectoral-fin apex; short snout, broadly triangular with tip extended slightly and anterior margims weakly undulate; small eyes with orbit length and spiracle 2.1-2.5 in
entries.biology: Demersal or benthic on insular and continental shelves ; on on upper slopes to 800 m . Found on sand or mud bottoms, sometimes near coral reefs . Feeds on crabs, prawns and small bony fishes . Ovoviviparous . Males mature at ca. 100 cm WD, and females ca. 110 cm WD; pups born at ca. 35 cm WD; but these data measurements needs confirmation . Caught often by demersal tangle net and longline fisheries operating in shelf waters.Utilized for its meat, cartilage and thorny tail (58048).
entries.reproduction: Exhibit ovoviparity (aplacental viviparity), with embryos feeding initially on yolk, then receiving additional nourishment from the mother by indirect absorption of uterine fluid enriched with mucus, fat or protein through specialised structures (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Benthodesmus vityazi

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 61 - 64; Dorsal soft rays (total): 88 - 93; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 80 - 85; Vertebrae : 137 - 142. Body silvery, jaws and opercle blackish. entries.biology: Adults benthopelagic from 640 to 820 m, juveniles mesopelagic from 170 to 900 m .

entries.name: Blenniella gibbifrons
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 4 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian, Line and Ducie Islands, north to Marcus Island.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 20; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 20 - 21. Body with 6-7 irregular bands . Dark spot present distally on anterior part of dorsal fin; females with dark spots on vertical fins, males more evenly colored . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabit shallow shore line water of intertidal reef flats from 0.5 to 1.5 m depth where the substrate consists of a thin carpet of algal turf and sand . Benthic . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Blenniella paula
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 3 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Sulawesi; Palau to Marquesan and Ducie islands, north to Marcus Islands, south to Great Barrier Reef; throughout Micronesia; replaced by Blenniella periophthalmus in the Indian Ocean and southeast Asia from Ryukyus through Solomons to Santa Cruz Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12 - 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 21; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 20 - 21; Vertebrae : 37 - 39. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XII-XIV, 18-21, notched between spinous and segmented-ray portions; anal fin II, 20-21; pectoral rays 13-15 (usually 14); pelvic fin I, 3; caudal fin, procurrent rays 7, segmented rays 13. Vertebrae 12 + 25-27. Orbital cirrus simple and slender, may have a short lateral branch, less often up to 4 branches; nasal cirri short and palmate, may rare
entries.biology: Adults are common on exposed outer intertidal reef flats, in areas with numerous cracks and holes. They feed on filamentous algae and associated minute invertebrates, e.g., foraminiferans, ostracods, copepods, and gastropods . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bodianus cylindriatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 250 - 510 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan. More recently reported from the Chesterfield Islands . Reported from the Hawaiian Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10. This species has the following characters: D XII, 10; caudal fin rays 10 + 12 + 10; pectoral-fin rays ii, 14-15; lateral line scales 30-31 (rarely 31); scales above lateral line 2-3; scales below lateral line 8½-10½; predorsal scales 25-27; total gill rakers 13-17; upper jaw have prominent anterior canines of similar size; dental ridge is low, 2 consecutive rows of shorter canines, the first with 4 teeth slightly longer than 4-5 in second
entries.biology: Benthopelagic over hard substrates . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bodianus leucosticticus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 50 - 75 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Somalia, Mozambique, Natal (South Africa), Mauritius, Réunion, and southern Japan. Likely at Seychelles  if Lepidaplois luteopunctatus is a synonym of Bodianus leucosticticus .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 12. Adults reddish to purplish brown on head, body dull yellow; longitudinal row of 3 pale yellow spots along back; small black spot centered at base of caudal fin; 2 black spots on soft anal fin; large black spot on pelvic fins; blackish spot anteriorly on dorsal fin . Juveniles reddish brown with rows of white blotches and small spots; black spots on fins . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Adults are usually found at moderate depths (50 m). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bodianus loxozonus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 100 m , usually 3 - 40 m . Tropical; 25°C - 28°C ; 37°N - 35°S, 101°E - 130°W
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: eastward to French Polynesia, north to Japan, south to New Caledonia. Myers & Lieske 1994  list the subspecies loxozonus as occurring from Vietnam to the Marshall Islands and Tonga, north to the Ryukyu and Ogasawara Islands and the subspecies trotteri as occurring in the Line and Cook Islands and French Polynesia. Reports of Bodianus hirsutus (synonym of Bodianus macrourus ) from
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. Adults usually with a large black blotch on the back, extending along the lower lobe of the tail fin to the black ventral fins, but reduced to a small patch in large males . Often misidentified as Bodianus hirsutus (synonym of Bodianus macrourus (Lacepede, 1801) . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs , on slopes or along upper part of drop-offs . Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled, invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bodianus tanyokidus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific, Comoro Islands and Mauritius to southern Japan.
entries.biology: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Bodianus thoracotaeniatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 320 - 395 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Kyushu-Palau Ridge.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11. Distinguished morphologically by the following: D XII, 11; caudal fin rays 10 + 12 + 7-9; pectoral-fin rays ii, 15; lateral-line scales 29; scales above lateral line 2½; scales below lateral line 8-10; predorsal scales about 21-24; total gill rakers 15-16; anterior canines of similar size on upper jaw; dental ridge with 7-12 smaller posterior canines to anterior ones, last few sometimes smaller, coalesced at base and set apart from others;

entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

During daytime minimal catch data indicate that the species is not found in the upper 500 m, but at night, small specimens ( 96467 ).

entries.name: Brachypterois serrulifer
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range 6 - 82 m . Tropical; 35°N - 18°S, 37°E - 143°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East coast of Africa, Madagascar, Red Sea and Persian Gulf, east to the Timor Sea, the Philippines and northern Australia, South and East China seas, and north to Tosa Bay, Kochi, southern Japan.

entries.name: Brachysomophis cirrocheilos
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 38 m . Tropical; 39°N - 20°S, 35°E - 148°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Japan, Taiwan south to Indonesia and Australia.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 135 - 140. Coloration pale, overlain dorsally and along flanks with irregular brown smudges. A moderately elongate species with tail 51-58% and head 11-14% of TL; dorsal fin arising well behind pectoral-fin tips; pectoral fins not elongate; snout moderate, about 3.2 in jaw; jaws elongate; lower jaw extending beyond snout; nostrils in very short tubes in upper lip and closely associated; labial fringe well-developed but cirri not elongate on jaws, with cauliflower-like projections at
entries.biology: Most commonly found in sand and mud, near coastal reefs at depths of 1 up to at least 10 m. Burrows into the sand tail-first until only its eyes and the top of its snout are visible. Sometimes seen with only its head or snout protruding from the sand. More commonly encountered at night but also seen with its head protruding out of the substrate during the day. Observed with cleaner shrimp Periclimenes magnificus on its head. The shrimp would swim off for short periods and then return to this species . Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans .

entries.name: Brachysomophis henshawi
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 35 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 128 - 134. With tail 45-48% and head 13-16% of TL; dorsal fin arising well behind pectoral tips; pectoral fins fan-shaped, not elongate; snout short, about 3.4 in jaw; jaws elongate, about 2.3-3 in head; nostrils in short tubes in upper lip and closely associated; cirri of labial fringe unbranched, short and stubby; flesh above and behind eye laterally elevated as a ridge; dorsal head profile depressed and constricted behind eyes, the flesh forming a lateral eave behind dorsal margin
entries.biology: Found over sandy areas, usually near or within coral or rocky reefs . Feeds on fishes and crtustaceans . Benthic . At night, it is usually encountered with its head and even the anterior portion of its body protruding from the substrate at night . At day time, it often remains buried with only the tip of its snout and the top of its head projecting from the sand or mud .

entries.name: Brotulotaenia nielseni
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 800 - 900 m . Deep-water; 39°N - 15°S, 141°E - 117°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from Japan, east to Mexico and to southeast Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 85 - 91; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 62 - 72; Vertebrae : 68 - 72. Scales small, non-imbricate prickles; opercle with no spine; median basibranchial tooth patch absent; gill rakers are tooth-bearing tubercles; otolith very small and rounded; precaudal vertebrae 12-15 .
entries.biology: Uncommon species . Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass .

entries.name: Bryaninops amplus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 30 m , usually 5 - 20 m . Tropical; 22°C - 26°C ; 32°N - 26°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Natal, South Africa  and Madagascar to the Hawaiian Islands, north to southern Japan, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 6 - 9; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 6 - 9. Characterized by semi-transparent reddish body color, blends in well with host gorgonian; iris with gold inner ring, broad red outer ring; 2-4 lowermost pectoral rays are unbranched; longitudinal scale series 37-79; short and cup-like pelvic fins; thickened and lobed skin surrounding pelvic spines; opening of gill extending ventrally to below pectoral fin base . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongat
entries.biology: Benthic . Live exclusively on, or in close association with gorgonian seawhips Junceella fragilis and Junceela juncea which usually occur in groups in areas exposed to currents at depths of 5 to more than 30 m . May also live on other species like Ellisella maculata , or even on mooring lines . Also Ref. 48637 .
entries.reproduction: Benthic spawner.

entries.name: Bryaninops loki

Caught with nets and other types of artisanal gear.

entries.biology: A common deepwater dogfish of the outer continental shelves and upper slopes, commonest below 200 m ; usually benthic and epibenthic at depths from 50-1440 m with most records from 200-600 m (Compagno, pers. comm. 07/07). Solitary . Adults feed mainly on bony fishes such as hake, epigonids, lanternfish, herring, smelts, cods, rattails, squid and crustaceans . Males mature at about 105-118 cm TL . Ovoviviparous . This species is fished in Eastern Atlantic by bottom trawls, long lines, fixed bottom nets, hook and line and pelagic trawls; caught and discarded, or utilised from by-catch fisheries (IUCN discussion 07/07).
