entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 4 - 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 23; Anal soft rays : 16 - 21. First dorsal fin pale. A row of 4 pairs of sensory papillae between parallel bony ridges on dorsal surface of snout. Four sensory papillae between eyes arranged in semicircle (Ref 12850). Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.

entries.name: Chascanopsetta micrognatha
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 320 - 375 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Kyushu-Palau Ridge. Reported from the Philippines (Amaoka, pers. comm.).

entries.name: Chauliodus macouni
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; oceanodromous ; depth range 25 - 4390 m . Deep-water; 66°N - 23°N, 127°E - 106°W
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Navarin Canyon in the Bering Sea to Japan. Eastern Pacific: Gulf of Alaska to central Baja California  and the Gulf of California.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 5 - 7; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 9 - 14; Vertebrae : 56 - 62. First dorsal fin ray much produced in a long filament terminating in a minute flap; adipose fin large, placed well back over posterior part of anal, higher posteriorly; pelvic fins long and narrow . No true gill rakers . Dark brown to black in color . Branchiostegal rays: 16-21 . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Migrate upward at night . Adults feed on small planktonic crustaceans, arrow worms and fish . Photophores occur on belly arranged in a row . Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae . Also caught with bottom trawls.
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 35898 ).

entries.name: Chaunax apus
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 395 - 460 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Eastern Indian Ocean to Western Pacific: Bay of Bengal (Myanmar), Japan, Taiwan, the Philippines and the South China Sea.

entries.name: Chaunax penicillatus
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 343 - 658 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: widespread; including Kenya, South Africa, Madagascar, Japan, Taiwan, South China Sea, Australia and New Zealand.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 3; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 6 - 7. This species is characterized by the following: D III,11-12 (modally 12); A 6-7 (7); pectoral-fin rays 11-13; presence of a black and very deep illicial trough; extremely short illicium and esca with numerous stout black (anterior face) and white (posterior face) cirri; gill rakers: GRi = 13-14 (3-4+9-10); GRii = 8-10; GRiii = 8-11; GRiv = 7-8; lateral-line counts: AB = 10-12 (mainly 11); BB' =
entries.biology: A benthic species  found on the continental slopes .

entries.name: Cheilinus oxycephalus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 40 m . Tropical; 26°N - 28°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marquesan and Society islands, north to Taiwan, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef and the Austral Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9 - 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Brownish red, mottled with small whitish spots; dark brown spot anteriorly on each side of upper lip; 2 dark lines diverging from the eye; dark brown spot on 1st 2 dorsal membranes . Deep-bodied for genus, and snout pointed . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs at depths of 1 to over 40 m . A secretive species , rarely ventures more than a few centimeters from shelter . A shy species, usually found in pairs when adult . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cheilodipterus artus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 158 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Juveniles have a small black spot surrounded by a large gold blotch on the caudal peduncle ; characterized further by the following: mauve or pale grey color with eight reddish brown stripes; blackish to brown caudal fin base; adults capable of quick color change; greatest depth of body 3.2-4.0 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Occurs in sheltered bays and lagoon patch reefs from 5 to at least 20 m, forming small, loose aggregates in caves or just above branches of certain corals . Feeds on small fishes .
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cheilopogon spilonotopterus
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 20 m. Tropical; 20°N - 1°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific to Eastern Pacific: Widely distributed in tropical waters, including the Ryukyu Islands , Taiwan  and eastern Pacific .
entries.biology: Epipelagic in coastal and oceanic waters. May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface. Feeds on zooplankton and small fish .

entries.name: Cheilopogon spilopterus
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 20 m. Tropical
entries.distribution: Eastern Indian Ocean and Western Pacific: Andaman Sea to Samoa. Reported from the Ryukyu Islands .
entries.biology: Occurs in neritic surface waters. Feeds on zooplankton and small fish .

entries.name: Cheilopogon suttoni
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; oceanodromous ; depth range 0 - 20 m. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Gulf of Aden to 140°E , common in central and western Oceania.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 10 - 13. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Found in oceanic and neritic surface waters . Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding above the surface . Feeds mainly on planktonic organisms and small fish .

entries.name: Cheilopogon unicolor
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; oceanodromous; depth range 0 - 10 m . Tropical; 36°N - 29°S, 105°E - 143°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: southern Japan, Taiwan, Philippines, New Guinea, and eastern Australia up to Hawaiian Islands and Tahiti.
entries.biology: Neritic species.

entries.name: Chelidonichthys ischyrus
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: known only from Sagami Bay, Japan.

entries.name: Chelidonichthys kumu
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; demersal; depth range 1 - 200 m , usually 75 - 150 m . Subtropical; 34°N - 43°S, 15°E - 154°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Delagoa Bay, Mozambique to the Cape, South Africa; common in Australia and New Zealand and reported from Japan and Korea. Also reported from Hong Kong .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9 - 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 15 - 16; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16; Vertebrae : 33 - 35. Olive or brownish in color, becomes red when stressed; lower half of the inner part of pectoral fin with large black blotch surrounded by numerous pale spots . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Found from estuaries to edge of continental shelves over sand and sandy shell seabed . Reported to be often found in rivers . Juveniles may occur in bays . Benthic . Dorsal spine reported to be venomous . Neither anterolateral glandular grooves nor venom gland is present . Current information in the table (dangerous fish) do not match; needs verification. Excellent food fish . Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, microwaved and baked .

entries.name: Chelidoperca santosi
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range ? - 146 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan and the Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6; Vertebrae : 24. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D X,10; 40-45 serrae on preopercle; posttemporal with 5-7 spines on exposed portion at beginning of LL; 42-45 lateral-line tubed scales; 2.5-3.0 scales above lateral line to dorsal origin; body color pinkish without dark markings; snout with row of 4 small dark spots (2 in front of each eye); 2 dark spots on chin (one on each sid

entries.name: Chiasmodon pluriradiatus
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 230 - 1600 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Atlantic, Indian, Southest Pacific, tropical Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico, from 32°N-11°S, 20°W-77°W; in the western Indian from 12°S-32°S, 60°W-58°E; in the southern Pacific from 25°S-38°S, 167°W-179°E
entries.description: Vertebrae : 44 - 45. This species is distinguished from its congeners by the number of pectoral-fin rays 15-16 (vs. 12-14); fangs on premaxillary head 2 (vs. 1); with tiny dermal spinules on body of specimens larger than 48.7 mm present (vs. absent); it further differs from C. asper by supraorbital canal pores 8 (vs. 9) . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Found in the meso- to bathypelagic zones, with adults more frequently collected below 900 m .

entries.name: Chimaera jordani
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 750 - 1600 m . Deep-water; 36°N - 10°N
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: known only from the type locality, Sagami Sea (Japan). Eastern Atlantic: Western Sahara to about Guinea. Taxonomic status of the West African specimens is uncertain.
entries.biology: Oviparous . Eggs are encased in horny shells .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chlorurus bowersi
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 20 m . Tropical; 30°N - 9°S, 102°E - 163°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Philippines, Java (Indonesia), Ryukyu Islands, and Palau.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Males are easily recognized by the bright orange patch. Females are similar to males but lack orange . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Inhabits channel and lagoon reef slopes, in coral-rich areas . Occurs singly .

entries.name: Chlorurus japanensis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S, 102°E - 153°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Ryukyu Islands to Australia. Recently reported from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. This species is further distinguished by having the following characters: median predorsal scales 4; scale rows on cheek 2; conical teeth absent on side of lower dental plate, 0-2 on upper plate of initial phase and often 2 on terminal male; lips slightly covers the dental plates; caudal fin in subadult slightly rounded to truncate and slightly emarginate in terminal male. Colour of male distinctly bicol
entries.biology: Inhabits seaward coral  and rocky reefs ; inner reefs with rich coral habitat . Feeds on benthic algae . May occur in small groups of 1 TP with 1 to 3 IPs . Caught mainly with traps, nets and other types of artisanal gear. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chlorurus spilurus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Central Pacific: from southern Japan to Queensland, east to the Pitcairn and Hawaiian islands.
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Choerodon japonicus
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 95 - 120 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Japan to Shark Bay, Western Australia.

entries.name: Choeroichthys sculptus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 6 m . Tropical; 35°N - 25°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Line, Society , and Gambier islands, north to southern Japan, south to Tonga.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 27 - 34; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 4. Short-snouted; dark, blackish brown with small black spots and small white ocelli in parallel series along trunk, and some white speckles over the back . Males are characterized by vertical row of silver spots (Ref 1602). Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: angular.
entries.biology: Inhabits intertidal reef flats. Also found in seagrass habitats to few meters depth . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Males may be brooding at 4.6 cm SL . Seen in lagoons and seaward reefs in 0-6 m (Ref 90102).
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chrionema chryseres
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 335 - 490 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Japan and Hawaii. Recently reported from the Chesterfield Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16; Anal soft rays : 26. Maxilla without tentacle. Spinous dorsal fin never jet black (Ref 12932). Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Benthic on sand and rock .

entries.name: Chromis albicauda
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 25 - 70 m , usually ? - 30 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Indonesia and southern Japanese seas; distribution probably disjunct due to association with cool temperature regimes.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D XIII,12 (rarely 11); A II,12 (rarely 11); pectoral rays 18-20; spiniform caudal rays 3; tubed lateral-line scales 17-19; gill rakers 7-8 + 24-26, total rakers 24-26; body depth 1.8-1.9 in SL; edge of suborbital hidden by scales; 4-5 scale rows on anterior portion of preorbital; generally yellow in life, grading to brown on upper bac
entries.biology: Adults are commonly observed in areas of cool (18°-24°C) upwelling along the northern and western shores of Nusa Penida at about 25-50 m. They typically form aggregations, which feed high in the water column on zooplankton when currents are strong . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chromis alpha
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 11 - 110 m . Tropical; 16°N - 23°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean to the Society Islands, north to Mariana Islands, south to New Caledonia; throughout Micronesia. Replaced by Chromis nigroanalis in the west Indian Ocean .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults occur in clear lagoon and seaward reefs, usually seen singly or in loose aggregations near caves and ledges. Abundant over branching corals and leeward coasts . Feeds on planktons . Diurnal species . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chromis okamurai
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 135 - 175 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Known only from a single specimen dredged in 1979 in the Okinawa Trough, East China Sea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 12. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Chrysiptera parasema
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 16 m . Tropical; 30°N - 13°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: including Solomon Islands, northern Papua New Guinea, Philippines, and Ryukyu Islands. There is a doubtful record from the Great Barrier Reef off Cairns, Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 12; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit coral-rich areas of sheltered lagoon and inshore coral reefs . They occur in small groups on Acropora patches . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205 ). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhilabrus katherinae
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 10 - 50 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Miyake-jima, Izu Islands, Japan, Guam and the Mariana Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Juveniles and females nearly uniformly orange-red. Males develop elongate pelvic fins and have brilliant blue bands on dorsal and anal fins. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Known at depths ranging from 10 to at least 40 m at exposed outer reef areas than in lagoons or harbors. Occurs in aggregations. Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhilabrus lanceolatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 42 - 60 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan and the Philippines. Photographed from Palau.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Occurs along steep seaward reefs . Specimens collected at 42 and 60 m .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhilabrus lunatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 30 - 55 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Okinawa and the Ogasawara Islands. Also recorded from Taiwan ; Bali and Sangihe Islands in Indonesia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. In females, upper and middle part of body with several orange-red longitudinal stripes from snout to caudal peduncle; whitish on abdomen, thorax, and lower part of head . Young specimens with a black spot on upper part of caudal and 3 dark red stripes on upper part of body . Caudal fin rounded in female and young fish; strongly lunate in male . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Collected at depths ranging from 32 to 45 m on dead coral and rubble substratum.
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhilabrus melanomarginatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 6 - 40 m , usually 8 - 25 m . Tropical; 24°C - 28°C
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Malaysia (Layang Layang Atoll), Philippines (Palawan), Taiwan, and Japan (Ryukyu and Izu Islands).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Usually occurs over rocky bottoms.
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhilabrus rubrimarginatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 25 - 52 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: north to the Ryukyu Islands, through the Philippines, Palau, and Indonesia to Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Found in deep coastal to outer reef drop-offs and steep slopes. Occurs over rubble or sandy bottoms with small isolated patch reefs of low profile. Juveniles solitary among large rubble, usually in 2-30 m depth. Adults in loose aggregations in moderate depths, usually 40 m or more around patch reef .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Cirrhitichthys aureus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 5 - 20 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: India east to Sagami Bay, Japan and China. A new record was reported from southern Indonesia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6. Distinguished from C. aprinus by the bright yellow coloration when viewed underwater . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Occurs on rocky cliffs in deep water . Also inhabits muddy substrates in protected bays where wave action has no influence . Solitary (Ref 90102).
entries.reproduction: Bi-directional sex change has been confirmed for this species (Ref. 103751 ). Sexual pattern seem to be intermediate between simultaneous and sequential hermaphroditism: individuals, at least under conditions of captivity, have the capacity to change sex in either direction, from functional male to functional female, or vice versa (Ref. 31569 ).

entries.name: Cirrhitichthys oxycephalus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 40 m , usually 10 - 25 m . Tropical; 24°C - 28°C ; 30°N - 23°S, 180°W - 180°E
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea south to East London, South Africa  and east to the Marquesan Islands, north to the Mariana Islands, south to New Caledonia. Eastern Pacific: Gulf of California to Colombia and the Galapagos Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6. Highly variable in color from pale with grey to black blotches to pink with bright red blotches . Pale with horizontal rows of subquadrate dark brown spots; a row of smaller spots on LL between larger spots; small dark brown spots on head . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Inhabit areas of rich coral growth and clear water of lagoon, channel, or seaward reefs from below the surge zone to depths of at least 40 m. They rest on, in, or beneath hard or soft corals. Feed on crustaceans and small fishes . Males are territorial and haremic .
entries.reproduction: Pelagic spawner (Ref. 31569 ). Spawning ascents into the water column occurred over a distance of 0.3 to1.0 m (Ref. 26305 ).

entries.name: Cirrhitops fasciatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 1 - 52 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Madagascar, Réunion , Mauritius, Japan, and Hawaii.
entries.description: Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Occurs on seaward reefs, in areas of moderate to rich coral growth. Typically at the bases of coral heads on hard bottoms . Benthic . Feeds about equally on small fishes, shrimps and crabs; to a lesser extent, on sipunculids and zooplankton (larval shrimps, copepods, amphipods and larval gastropods) .

entries.name: Cirripectes imitator
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m. Tropical; 35°N - 20°N
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Shirahama, Japan and the Ogasawara Islands to Batan Islands, northern Philippines.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 15; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 14 - 16; Vertebrae : 30. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XII, 14, membrane attached to caudal fin, with deep notch above last spine, first spine almost same or slightly higher than second; anal fin II, 15; pectoral rays 15; pelvic fin I, 4; caudal fin procurrent rays 11-14. Vertebrae 10 + 20. LL, without scales and scalelike flaps; LL tubes 7-14, canal ends below posterior to 9th dorsal ray, usually on cau
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Adults inhabit shallow coral and rocky reefs . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ). Urogenital orifice of male genital papilla located basally between 2 widely separated slender filaments on a fleshy swelling behind anus; testes bulbous with length equal to its width (Ref. 529 ).

entries.name: Cirripectes quagga
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 19 m , usually 0 - 10 m . Tropical; 30°N - 35°S, 21°E - 129°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: South Africa to Tanzania, east to Henderson Island, Pitcairn and the Hawaiian Islands; north to China; south to the Great Barrier Reef.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 15 - 17; Vertebrae : 30 - 32. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XII, 15, membrane attached to caudal fin, with deep notch above last spine, first spine about equal to twice higher than second; anal fin II, 16; pectoral rays 15; pelvic fin I, 4; caudal fin procurrent rays 10-15. Vertebrae 10 + 21. LL, without scales and scalelike flaps; LL tubes 7-18 (usually 10-18), canal ends below 7th dorsal ray to caudal-
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Found in algal ridge and crests between surge channels of exposed seaward reefs . Usually taken in water less than 10 m deep, but has been collected at depths as great as 19 m . Feeds on benthic algae . Benthic . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ). Urogenital orifice of male genital papilla located behind a single slender filament on a fleshy swelling behind anus; elongated testes with width equals about about half its length (Ref. 529 ).

entries.name: Cirripectes stigmaticus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m , usually ? - 10 m . Tropical; 15°N - 30°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Kenya south to Mozambique and throughout the Indian Ocean and western central Pacific to the Marshall and Samoan islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11 - 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 15 - 17; Vertebrae : 30 - 32. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin XII, 15, membrane attached to caudal fin, with deep notch above last spine, first spine slightly higher than second; anal fin II, 16; pectoral rays 15; pelvic fin I, 4; caudal fin procurrent rays 10-14. Vertebrae 10 + 21. LL, without scales and scalelike flaps; LL tubes 1-10 (usually 3-8), canal ends below 7th dorsal ray to caudal-fin base. Lowe
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus ; Found solitary or forms small groups in the upper edge of seaward reef slopes, less than 10 m, but may be found up to 20 m deep . Adults inhabit coastal reef flats with rich coral and algae habitats ; also on rocky and coralline structures ; among Acropora and Pocillopora corals of surf-swept algal ridge. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ). Urogenital orifice of male genital papilla located basally between 2 widely separated slender filaments on a fleshy swelling behind anus; testes bulbous with length equal its width (Ref. 529 ).

entries.name: Cociella punctata
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 10 - 300 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: widespread, from the New Hebrides to Papua New Guinea, north to Taiwan, through Indonesia to Thailand, Pakistan, the Red Sea, and South Africa. Replaced by Cociella crocodilus from southern China to Japan and by Cociella hutchinsi in northern Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 12; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. Often seen in pairs. Uses its tubelike snout to ingest small crustaceans and plankton . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Monogamous and always in home-ranging pairs, that is they do not defend an exclusive territory .
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both obligate and genetic (Ref. 52884 ). Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

An active cleaner that shares crevices with shrimps, large mud crabs and sometimes moray eels . Solitary or in pairs near sponges and Diadema sea urchins (Ref 90102). Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Spawns from the end of May to September. Monogamous and always in home-ranging pairs, that is they do not defend an exclusive territory .
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both obligate and genetic (Ref. 52884 ). Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

They also socially mimic their swimming behavior and also of Pseudanthias huchtii and Lepidozygus tapeinosomoa . Reported to feed on zooplankton . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad

entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; amphidromous ; depth range 10 - 30 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Natal, South Africa, eastward to India and Lesser Sunda Island, Indonesia, north to Japan  and Taiwan, south to northern Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 19 - 20; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 15 - 17. Head and body silvery blue-green. Four or 5 faint dark blue bars often visible on body. Fins dusky. Body orbicular and strongly compressed, its depth more than twice length of head. Eye above horizontal axis through mouth. Mouth small, the maxilla not reaching past vertical at front edge of eye. Jaws with bands of slender, incisiform teeth with a single lanceolate cusp. No teeth on palatines o
entries.biology: Inhabits shallow water, over mud bottoms. Feeds on benthic invertebrates and fishes .

entries.name: Epinephelus bleekeri
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 30 - 105 m . Tropical; 36°N - 17°S, 48°E - 153°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Taiwan, Indonesia and the northern coast of Australia. Not known from Japan, but may occur here. It has not been found at any islands of Micronesia nor Polynesia.

Recognized by the bluish lower half of the caudal fin and the lack of spots there compared to the upper half ; characterized further by: generally brown color; head, body and fins with red to dark brown spots; body scales ctenoid, except cycloid scales on nape, thorax and ventrally on abdomen; body with auxiliary scales; elongate body, greatest depth 3.0-3.5 in SL; truncate to slightly rounded
entries.biology: Occur on shallow banks, but is not known from well-developed coral reefs  and adjacent soft substrate in depths of 30-105 m . Also found in silty coastal reefs and estuaries. Solitary (Ref 90102). Benthic . In Hong Kong live fish markets . Usually taken by trawling in 30-45 m or by hand-lining over rocky banks; not found from coral reefs .

entries.name: Epinephelus irroratus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 50 - ? m . Tropical; 30°N - 12°S, 144°E - 139°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: known only from the Marquesan Islands and one specimen from Minami Tori Shima, Marcus Islands, Japan (although this report may be erroneous).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Distinguished by the following characteristics: reddish brown color with white dot on each scale giving finely speckled appearance; dark reddish brown maxillary streak; prominent dark red margin on spinous dorsal fin; rear edges of median and pectoral fins with white line; body depth contained 2.7-3.3 times in SL; head length 2.4-2.6 times in SL; slightly convex interorbital area and dorsal head profile
entries.biology: Abundant in shallow water around fringing reefs. Nothing has been published on its biology.

entries.name: Epinephelus japonicus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan, and southern Taiwan, including Chinese coast of the South China Sea.

entries.name: Epinephelus morrhua

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the central Pacific. Epinephelus poecilonotus , Epinephelus radiatus , and Epinephelus tuamotoensis are sometimes referred to as this species.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 15; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7 - 8. Distinguished by the following characteristics: head and body tan, with dark brown bands: bifurcate band that begins at rear edge of eye, upper branch extending to a dark brown saddle blotch on the nape just in front of dorsal fin, lower branch running to lower opercular spine and continuing on body as midlateral band that bifurcates above the pectoral fin, upper branch of this band running to
entries.biology: Found in deep waters from 80-370 m on slopes of islands, sea mounts or continental shelves. Feeds on benthic fishes and large invertebrates . Considered rare in Tahiti but quite common in atolls . The species is easily confused with E. poecilonotus , E. radiatus , or E. tuamotuensis , three closely related deep-water groupers. Known to be ciguatoxic at Mauritius. Uncommon in local markets (probably due to it deep-water habitat).

entries.name: Epinephelus quoyanus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range ? - 50 m . Tropical; 35°N - 32°S, 110°E - 156°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan to Australia. Unknown from the Indian Ocean except for the Andaman Islands record (as Serranus merra ). Unreported from islands of Micronesia, Melanesia and central Pacific. Often misidentified as Epinephelus macrospilos or Epinephelus hexagonatus .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16 - 18; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Distinguished by the following characteristics: whitish color; head, body and fins with numerous large close-set hexagonal to roundish dark brown to blackish spots; ctenoid body scales except cycloid dorsoanteriorly above lateral line, on thorax and abdomen; body with auxiliary scales; greatest depth of body 2.7-3.2 in SL; rounded caudal fin; pelvic fins, 1.7-2.1 in head length ; head length 2.3-2.
entries.biology: Inhabits inshore silty reefs; there are no records from depths greater than 50 m. Feeds on shrimps, small fishes, worms and crabs . The enlarged fleshy pectoral fins appear to have resulted from its habit of sitting on the substrate. Solitary (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Epinephelus socialis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m , usually 0 - 3 m . Tropical; 30°N - 29°S, 139°E - 123°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: islands of Oceania; Ogasawara Islands, Marcus Islands, Mariana Islands, Marshall Islands, Phoenix Islands, American Samoa, Cook Islands, Line Islands, Society Islands, Rapa, Tuamoto Islands, and the Pitcairn Group. Unknown in Hawaii, the Marquesas, Caroline Islands, nor in any Melanesian islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 8. Preopercle rounded, finely serrate; upper edge of the operculum sinuous; nostril subequal; maxilla reaches past vertical at rear edge of the eye. Pectoral fins fleshy. Head and body whitish, with small close-set blackish-brown spots, those on the rear part of the body coalesced to form irregular longitudinal bands. Four dark blotches usually at the base of the dorsal fin and a fifth forming a dark
entries.biology: This shallow-water species is more common on atolls than high islands, and usually found in exposed outer-reef areas. Not dependent on coral cover . Juveniles and occasionally adults are collected from tide pools. Feeds on crustaceans (mainly grapsid crabs), octopi, and fishes.

entries.name: Epinephelus suborbitalis
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 360 - 570 m . Deep-water; 27°N - 23°N, 133°E - 137°E
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: known only from a single specimen taken from the Minami-Koto Seamount which lies on the Kyushu-Palau Ridge.

Upper edge of operculum convex; posterior nostril of large adults broadly oval, its diameter about 3 times that of the anterior nostril; ventral edge of the maxilla with a step-like expansion distally. Color is uniformly grayish brown, the fins darker. entries.name: Eptatretus moki
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; non-migratory; depth range ? - 100 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.
entries.description: Six pairs of gill pouches (GP) and apertures (GA); GA closely spaced (not crowded) in a nearly straight line. Fused cusps 3/2, total cusps 38-43. Prebranchial slime pores 18-21; total pores 75-82. Ventral finfold well developed with wide pale margin. Eyespots faint or absent . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.

entries.name: Etelis carbunculus

This species is distinguished by having the following characters: body relatively elongate, laterally compressed. Nostrils on each side of snout close together; lower jaw protruding slightly; premaxillae protrusible and maxilla extending to below middle of eye; both upper and lower jaws with conical teeth; 1 to several enlarged canines on each side of both jaws; vomer and palatines with teeth, those on
entries.biology: Adults inhabit rocky bottoms . Benthopelagic . Feed on fishes and larger invertebrates such as squids, shrimps and crabs; also takes planktonic organisms, including pelagic urochordates. An important food fish in some areas. Marketed fresh or frozen .

This species is distinguished by the following characters: body relatively elongate and laterally compressed; nostrils on each side of snout close together; lower jaw protruding and premaxillae protrusible, maxilla extending to vertical near posterior margin of orbit; small conical teeth in jaws, a few anterior ones in each jaw enlarged, sometimes into canine-like teeth; with teeth on palatine and vomer
entries.biology: Adults inhabit rocky bottoms. Feed mainly on fishes. Marketed fresh.

entries.name: Etmopterus brachyurus

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Kyushu-Palau Ridge.

Patchy external pigment in the distal 1/3 of the large specimen. Axis of filament unpigmented. External chevron-shaped or roundish striated areas on stem unpigmented. Middorsal paired spots

A single, simple or bifurcate, short terminal filament 5.1-1.6% SL, decreasing relatively with growth. Proximal end of bulb almost flat, with a solid black cap. Most of the barbel stem unpigmented between branch and terminal bulb . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.

Dendritic side filaments off main branch, usually with elongate ovoids or bulblets, growing wee distal to branch origin. The distal, unpigmented part of the bulb laterally flattened . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.

New Caledonia, and across to the Tuamotus and Pitcairn Islands.

entries.biology: Inhabits rocky caverns or coral heads on sand seen most frequently at depths of about 8-15 m on either live coral (frequently faviids) or on rocky surfaces covered with coralline algae patches .

entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Papua New Guinea (Trobriand Islands), New Caledonia, Fiji (widely distributed but not in the S.E. Lau Grp), Tonga, Australia (Great Barrier Reef), and throughout Micronesia to Kiribati.

Body shape ( shape gui

entries.reproduction: Benthic spawner.

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Seychelles, Mauritius (Cargados Carajos Shoals) and Western Australia; Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Palau, across Micronesia through islands of Oceania to French Polynesia (Rapa) and Pitcairn Islands. Apparently not occurring in Indonesia, Philippines, and New Guinea.

Characterized by dark purplish brown body color with three white spots anteriorly on middle of side; presence of series of small white spots beginning on nape, continuing along base of dorsal fin and ending on dorsal surface of caudal peduncle; caudal fin base with red-edged black spot; iris reddish; first four dorsal spines elongate or filamentous in male; all pectoral rays unbranched; longitudin

entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated. Temperate

Characterized by semi-transparent, greenish-brown body with about six faint, internal dark bars; scale margins narrow orange-brown; short brown bars across top of head and along upper back; presence of dark internal blotches above anal fin and lower edge of caudal peduncle; upper portion of caudal peduncle with large black spot; eleventh to fifteenth pectoral rays usually branched; ctenoid scales, abs

This species has dorsal to anal fin-ray formula 8/8; unbranched pectoral-fin rays; when alive or fresh, there is a distinct black stripe along the backbone and when preserved, with a strong black pigment along scale pockets on the ventral half of the sides . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: oval.

Characterized by 5 subcutaneous spots from anal base to caudal base ; translucent greenish color with 6-7 internal brown bars; scale margins reddish brown; head with red-brown spots/bands; upper half of caudal peduncle with large black spot; prolonged and filamentous first dorsal spine in male; longitudinal scale series 23-25; ctenoid scales, absent on head, nape, breast and pectoral fin base; se

This species is distinguished from its congeners by the following set of characters: dorsal/anal fin-ray formula usually 8/8, sometimes 8/7 or 9/8; pectoral fin rays 16-17 (usually 16), all unbranched; cephalic sensory-pore system pattern IV (lacking pores PITO and IT, AITO enlarged, engulfing the PITO); fifth segmented pelvic-fin ray variable, absent to 18% of fourth ray; non-fimbriate genital pa

Characterized by semi-translucent body with irregular, internal reddish midlateral stripe; white stripe along spinal column interrupted by reddish bars that extend ventrally; row of small reddish spots along dorsal midline; usually with narrow reddish bars above anal fin; often prolonged and filamentous first four dorsal spines of male and first three of female; unbranched pectoral rays; longitud
entries.biology: Adults live for 59 days at the most, with larvae spending three weeks in the open ocean and maturing within two weeks of settling on a reef, leaving the adults (which are 1 to 2 centimeters long) just three weeks to reproduce. This strategy of 'live fast, die young' is perceived to be a response to intense predation. Daily mortality rate, from tag-recapture data, might be as high as 8% . Occur at depths less than 4 to between 17 and 21 m on sandy bottoms of lagoon reefs .  Spawning appears to be repeated on a regular cycle, semilunar or every 14 days .

entries.name: Grammonus yunokawai

This species has the following characters: Dorsal-fin rays 83; anal-fin rays 64; caudal fin rays 9; pectoral 23-24; vertebrae 12 + 29; anterior anal fin ray is placed below 23rd dorsal fin ray; maximum depth of head is 32.0% SL; predorsal length 41.5% SL; interorbital width 10.5% SL; height of posterior margin of maxilla 8.4% SL .
entries.biology: Known only from one female specimen with ovaries containing eggs up to about 0.5 mm in diameter and apparently with no embryos. It was caught by hand in the back of the cave in absolute darkness. The head and lateral line pore systems are well developed, also the sensory papillae on the head and body, indicating adaptation to the lightless environment Also observed and caught were a shrimp Parhippolyte misticia and the fishes Pseudamia hayashii and Apogon evermanni .

entries.name: Gunnellichthys curiosus

entries.name: Gymnapogon japonicus

entries.biology: Sometimes taken by trawl net, and found in the open sea .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

The species is also found in the eastern Indian Ocean at Christmas I., the Cocos-Keeling Is. (in addition to the paratypes from this locality, 1 nontyp

Colour of male (female similar) greyish on upper back, white or pale yellow on ventral part; a broad brown stripe on side at eye level. with several white spots along lower edge of this stripe, mainly on posterior half; upper pectoral-fin base with a small black spot; middle of dorsal fin with a pale-edged

Stripes on male body blue-green and orangish in life, becoming salmon pink and green anteriorly; a dark spot behind eye contained within a brown band that bifurcates posteriorly. Females with a small black spot on 1st interspinous membrane of dorsal fin, another between 2nd-3rd soft rays; a spot at the upper base of caudal fin. Anterior lateral line scales with 1-4 pores (usual

Distinguished by the following characters: 5-8 symphyseal mandibular sensory pores; second dorsal fin spines XIII-XIV; last pleural ribs on vertebral centrum 11, vertebrae 11+ 26 = 37; nape naked ; black lower half of head; bright blue stripe extending from anterior part of upper lip to preopercular margin through ventral margin of orbit; dorsal fins black distally; central pa
entries.biology: Adults are found among rocky boulders and in surge channels to a depth of about 6 m . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters .

entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 32 m , usually ? - 10 m . Tropical

entries.name: Helcogramma ellioti
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 2 - 10 m , usually 2 - 5 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: widely distributed. The species complex is being revised by J.T. Williams.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 16; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 18 - 20; Vertebrae : 34 - 35. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin III + XIII+ 9-10, second fin same height of first; anal fin I + 18; pectoral rays 16 (1+8+7); pelvic fin I, 2, spine short and hidden, segmented rays simple, partially united by membrane. Vertebrae 10 + 24-25. LL total lateral scales 36-38, pored series 33-37 (21) scales; nape, belly, and anal-fin base scaleless, caudal fin base with only 1 row of sca
entries.biology: Adults inhabit rocky boulders from depths of 2 to 5 m, common at depths less than 10 m . They live in small groups, each comprising a male and several females  on rock surfaces and under ledges and tidepools . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters .

entries.name: Helcogramma fuscopinna

entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 16 - 18; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 12; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 19 - 21; Vertebrae : 36 - 38. Diagnosis: Dorsal fin III + XIV+ 11, 1st fin 4/5 height of 2nd fin, 1 free pterygiophore between 2nd and 3rd fin; anal fin I + 21; pectoral rays 17 (1+9+7); pelvic fin I, 2, spine short and hidden, segmented rays simple, partially united by membrane. Vertebrae 10 + 27. LL total lateral scales 39-40; tubed 22-30 scales, ends below anterior half of 3rd dorsal fin; nape
entries.biology: Adults live on rock surfaces and under ledges; common at depths less than 10 m . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters .

entries.name: Helcogramma rhinoceros
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 6 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Widespread in the area, from the Philippines, Viet Nam, Indonesia (Borneo) to the Solomon Islands . Recently collected from Fiji and Tonga (Williams pers. comm.). New locality records from Thailand and the Andaman Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 17 - 18; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 20; Vertebrae : 37. Trunk without longitudinal stripes; symphyseal dentary pores 1; upper lip with proboscis-like extension on males, head with horizontal yellowish or bluish white line from the upper rim of upper jaw to opercle . Males are easily recognized by the extended nose and change color to display to females with an electric blue line below the eye, shaded by black below . Also Ref. 9410
entries.biology: Adults inhabit clear coastal reefs with algae covered rocky boulders, usually in small groups . They occur in very shallow depths on rock surfaces and under ledges . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters . Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 58018 .

entries.name: Helcogramma striata
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 30 m , usually 0 - 10 m. Tropical; 36°N - 25°S, 92°E - 157°W
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Japan to the Philippines, Australia, and the Solomon Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 16 - 18; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 12; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 19 - 21; Vertebrae : 35 - 38. Identified by trunk having several longitudinal stripes . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit clear coastal reefs with moderate currents . Usually in small groups on sponges or reef outcrops. They feed on zooplankton . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters . Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 13227 .

entries.name: Hemibarbus maculatus
entries.environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 7.0 - ? ; dH range: 20 - ?. Temperate; 10°C - 24°C
entries.distribution: Asia: China, Korea, Japan and Amur River basin. At least one country reports adverse ecological impact after introduction.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 42 - 44. Both sides of the body with 7-11 large and blackish spots. Deep body with clearly convex dorsal profile. Head length shorter than body depth. Snout length shorter or equal to postorbital head length. Lips not developed, lateral lobes of lower lip narrow, without folds, the median process large and marked. Barbel length slightly thick, 1/2-2/3 of eye diameter. Dorsal spine strong, equal to HL. Origin of dorsal fin nearer the tip of snout than the caudal base . Anal fin with 6
entries.biology: Adults usually found in streams and creeks with moderate flow and sandy bottom . Feed mainly on insects and mollusks in summer and on crustaceans in winter
entries.reproduction: Mature at 3 years of age. Spawns from May to June, with water temperatures from 19-25 C°. Eggs are pasted at underwater plants. Egg diameter about 2mm. Development time about 4 days. Larvae live pelagic for the first 6 days.

entries.name: Heminodus philippinus
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 200 - 500 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-Western Pacific: Philippines, Japan and Indonesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6 - 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 21; Anal soft rays : 18 - 19. This species is characterized by the following: fusiform body covered with bony plates with head large and depressed; broad snout, with short, triangular rostral projection on each side, nearly parallel to each other; interorbital region concave and with no distinct ridges; head with supraocular, parietal, posttemporal, opercular, and preopercular spines; large and inferior mouth with posterior tip of uppe
entries.biology: Deep benthic species of limited commercial value inhabiting warm tropical seas along continental shelf edge and slope. Bony scutes reduce commercial value .

entries.name: Hemiramphus lutkei
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 0 - ? m. Tropical
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: ranging eastward to the Gilbert Islands and Samoa, north to southern Japan. Confused with Hemiramphus archipelagicus under the name Hemiramphus marginatus by many authors .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 15; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 10 - 13; Vertebrae : 52 - 57. Greatly prolonged, beak-like lower jaw; upper jaw short, triangular and without scales; preorbital ridge absent; total number of gill rakers on first gill arch 33-46; pectoral fins long, reaching beyond anterior margin of nasal pit when folded forward; no spots or vertical bars on sides. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal waters rich in vegetation . Found more offshore than other species of Hemiramphus in the western central Pacific; juveniles and immature individuals are relatively common far from shore, usually among floating plants . Caught by set-net.

entries.name: Hemitriakis complicofasciata
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Ryukyu Is. (Japan) and Taiwan.
entries.description: This species is distinguished by the following characters: monospondylous vertebrae 46-52; precaudal total vertebrae 124-131; posterior nasal flap developed; first dorsal fin origin anterior to free rear tips of pectoral fin; snout length short with snout tip to oral length 55581 ). Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Claspers of most males are almost fully elongate and calcified at about 76 cm TL; while females are mature and pregnant at about 76 cm TL. Embryos less than 22 cm TL with only external yolk, most that are more than 22 cm TL with substantial internal yolk. Litter size from 5-8 with 2-4 embryos per uterus. Five pregnant specimens contained a total of 29 embryos (9 females and 20 males) and each embryo were covered separately by embryonic membrane .

entries.name: Hemitrygon laevigata
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range ? - 60 m . Subtropical; 35°N - 20°N, 116°E - 135°E
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Taiwan to southern Japan.
entries.biology: A demersal species, inshore on continental shelf over soft bottoms to ca. 60 m. In the summer, juveniles are found in estuaries and coastal shallows . Ovoviviparous .
entries.reproduction: Exhibit ovoviparity (aplacental viviparity), with embryos feeding initially on yolk, then receiving additional nourishment from the mother by indirect absorption of uterine fluid enriched with mucus, fat or protein through specialised structures (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Heteroconger polyzona
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 1 - 10 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Ryukyu Islands, Philippines, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 437 - 444; Anal soft rays : 293 - 324; Vertebrae : 153 - 159. Body with zebra-like barring; body diameter about 15 mm . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Occurs in shallow water. Burrows of individuals are in pairs, approximately 8 inches apart; with neighboring pairs at least 3-4 times greater apart from each other. Usually in moderate sized aggregations that appear during current runs . Usually in colonies on sand bottoms near reefs, sheltered bays and coastal sand slopes (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Heterophotus ophistoma
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 790 - 1420 m . Deep-water; 55°N - 40°S, 85°W - 125°W
entries.distribution: Eastern Atlantic: Western Sahara south to Namibia, not recorded close to the coast. Western Atlantic: Bermuda south to Brazil including Caribbean Sea and the southern Subtropical Convergence. Also, Indian and Pacific Oceans.

Teeth on jaws very short, spine-like; photopores of ventral row excluding AC series arranged in discontinuous, close-set groups of 1 to 5 . Barbel shorter than head, dark stem, flattened and tapering tip . Black in color . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Meso- and bathypelagic .

entries.biology: Often photographed or collected from shallow water not deeper than 100 meters .

entries.name: Heterotilapia buettikoferi
entries.environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.5 - 7.0; dH range: 15 - ?; non-migratory . Tropical; 23°C - 25°C ; 14°N - 4°N
entries.distribution: Africa: lower reaches of coastal rivers from Guinea-Bissau (Geba and Corubal Rivers) to west Liberia (St. John River).
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13 - 15; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 10 - 11. Diagnosis: lower pharyngeal bone about as long as broad, and with anterior lamella shorter than toothed area; median pharyngeal teeth broadened when compared to the lateral teeth; 5-6 series of scales on cheeks; 4.5-6 scales between first dorsal fin spine and upper lateral line; dark vertical bars broader than lighter inter-spaces . Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults occur only in larger rivers with rocky substrates, not found in smaller creeks; not specialized, but prefer a herbivorous diet; pair-bonding, biparental open substratum spawners holding very large territories; might spawn throughout the year .

entries.name: Himantolophus borealis
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 1210 - ? m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific.

Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.

entries.name: Hippichthys cyanospilos
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Persian Gulf , northern Red Sea and East Africa  to Fiji.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 20 - 28; Anal soft rays : 2 - 3. Variable pale yellow to nearly black . Venter and side of trunk without dark bars; dorsal fin with 3-4 prominent brown spots on each ray . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Adults occur in estuaries, lower reaches of coastal rivers and streams  and mangroves . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Males may be brooding at 6.5-7.5 SL.
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Hippichthys heptagonus
entries.environment: Freshwater; brackish; demersal. Tropical; 29°N - 12°S
entries.distribution: Africa, Asia and Oceania: South Africa and Kenya to the Solomon Islands and in some Philippine lakes .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 22 - 30. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Common in the lower reaches of rivers and streams, and in estuarine habitats. Ovoviviparous . Occurs in mangrove estuaries and tidal creeks . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Male matures at 7.5-8.0 cm SL.
entries.reproduction: Female deposits eggs on the ventral surface of the male's trunk or tail, where they are incubated for several weeks (Ref. 2847 ).

entries.name: Hippichthys penicillus
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; non-migratory . Tropical; 34°N - 34°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: western Persian Gulf (Kuwait, Saudi Arabia), north central Indian Ocean, and eastward to Japan and Queensland, Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 23 - 31. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit lower reaches of streams and rivers, also seagrass beds in estuaries and other shallow inshore habitats . Occur in mangrove estuaries and tidal creeks . Males exhibit parental care by incubating and guarding the eggs in their brood pouch . Ovoviviparous . Monogamous and always in home-ranging pairs, that is they do not defend an exclusive territory .
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both obligate and genetic (Ref. 52884 ). Female deposits eggs on the ventral surface of the male's tail, where they are incubated for several weeks (Ref. 2847 ).

entries.name: Hippichthys spicifer
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; pH range: 7.5 - 8.2; dH range: 20 - 30; amphidromous ; depth range 0 - 3 m . Tropical; 23°C - 28°C ; 33°N - 15°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Sri Lanka and Samoa . Recorded upstream in freshwater of the Mekong, but this record may represent another species of this genus or another genus among the 15 genera of pipefishes expected in Mekong estuary and plume .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 25 - 30. Brownish, mottled or with prominent dark bars crossing lower half of side and venter of trunk; bars absent or obscured by dark ground color in some adults; dorsal rays without rows of distinct brown spots . Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Adults occur in shallow coastal and estuarine waters, sometimes among mangroves. Also found regularly in freshwater in the lower reaches of rivers  and tidal creeks . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Males maybe brooding at about 9.8 SL.
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Hippocampus bargibanti
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 40 m . Tropical; 3°N - 23°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Indonesia and eastward to Vanuatu; north to Japan; south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 15. Description based on 4 specimens: Adult height, less than 2.0 cm. Rings, 11-12 + 31-34. Snout length is greater than 4.0 in head length. Dorsal fin rays, 13-15 covering 1+1 rings. Pectoral fin rays, 10. Coronet, a rounded knob. Spine, as irregular bulbous tubercles scattered over body and tail; a single prominent rounded eye spine; a single low rounded cheek spine. Other distinctive characters: head and body very fleshy, mostly without
entries.biology: Only known to occur on gorgonian corals of the genus Muricella , with up to 28 pairs on a single gorgonian. The tubercles and truncated snout of this species match the color and shape of the polyps of the host gorgonian, while its body matches the gorgonian stem. So extreme is this camouflage that the original specimens were only noticed after their host gorgonian had been collected and observed in an aquarium. Post-pelagic young settle on various hosts, but to breed, they appear to prefer the red polyp Muricella spp. That usually grow in depths over 20 m . Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812
entries.reproduction: Possibly monogamous in the wild (Ref. 30915 ). Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Hippocampus kuda
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 68 m , usually 0 - 8 m . Tropical; 39°N - 28°S, 32°E - 154°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: southern Africa, the Red Sea to Hawaii and French Polynesia; north to Japan, south to Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 17 - 18; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 4. Body shape ( shape guide ): other; Cross section: angular.
entries.biology: Inhabit seagrass and marine algae areas of estuaries and seaward reefs; also on steep mud slopes. Found in open water and attached to drifting Sargassum up to 20 km from shore. Adults in pairs . Benthic to pelagic . Feeds on zooplankton . Ovoviviparous . The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Not shown to be monogamous in the laboratory . Very popular aquarium fish. Highly valued species in traditional Chinese medicine . Has been reared in captivity .
entries.reproduction: There are 20 - 1000 larvae in incubating sacks; time of development is 20-28 days. The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Hippocampus pontohi
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; non-migratory; depth range 3 - 25 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Indonesia to the Solomon Is. and Fiji ; north to Japan .
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 12. This species is distinguished from its congeners by the following set of characters: 4 subdorsal rings; 2 pairs of bilaterally wing-like protrusions formed by a pair of large truncate spines projecting laterad on both first and second superior trunk ridges; flat laterodorsal surface on the third and fourth trunk rings; 28 tail rings 28; 14 dorsal-fin rays; 10 pectoral-fin rays . Body shape ( shape guide ): other; Cross section: angular.
entries.biology: Hippocampus pontohi has been observed on the coralline algae Halimeda , as well as on the hydroid Aglaephenia cupressina (Müller and Severns, pers. comm.). Severns noted it particularly in areas where Halimeda is growing on reef walls. It has been recorded at a number of areas in Indonesia (Bunaken, Cape Sri, Sorong, Wakatobi, Lembeh Straits), at depths of between 11-25 m particularly on vertical walls or in rock fissures on current-swept walls where it will tend to occur on the side of the fissure that faces away from the current, but in all cases where there is some upward current (Müller, pers. comm.) and has been seen swimming over a fungiid coral (Hardt, pers. comm.). entries.biology: Adults are reported to occur on rocky slope area and small individuals are known to occur around sea urchins. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . They lay eggs in a nest, using holes made by invertebrates on massive corals. The well-developed eggs are taken into the mouth and squeezed by the males and the newly hatched larvae swim out of its mouth. Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Spawning season extends from the middle of May to the beginning of October in Kinko Bay, Japan .

It is syntopically distributed together with L. echigonia in the Yura and Kako rivers, although L. echigonia has a tendency to inhabit more lentic waters in swampy streams and ditches .

entries.biology: Adults mainly inhabit coral and rocky reefs . They sometimes form small aggregations around rocky outcrops and coral heads during daylight hours. Feed on fishes and crustaceans .

Juveniles often intertidal ; over sand, silt, or coral rubble bottoms, occasionally in mangrove-lined streams and estuaries  They may enter freshwater to feed ; on small fish and invertebrates . This is a small species commonly utilized in subsistence fisheries and also seen in markets. Caught mainly with handlines, traps, and gill nets and are marketed mostly fresh .

entries.biology: Adults are found solitary or in pairs  in lagoon and seaward reefs below the surge zone to 30 m depth . A common species, often seen along slopes and drop-offs, adults sometimes in small groups . Feed on zooplankton and also on small benthic invertebrates. Inoffensive, but immune from predation . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Mimicked by Ecsenius bicolor and Plagiotremus laudanus .

entries.biology: Found in coastal waters, over sandy or muddy areas of lagoons, reef flats and tide pools; enters harbors . Schooling species, swim at various depths along reefs, to about 20 meters but usually much shallower. Feed on detritus containing algae and microscopic animals, by scooping up the upper layer of sand or mud and filtering through the gills . Omnivorous . Form large schools before spawning, at the beginning of the ebb tide (in June), over shallow, open areas of the lagoon slope . Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive . Spawning occurs in large aggregations after dark. Marketed fresh . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874 .

entries.reproduction: Copulatory organ absent. The gonads of hagfishes are situated in the peritoneal cavity. The ovary is found in the anterior portion of the gonad, and the testis is found in the posterior part. The animal becomes female if the cranial part of the gonad develops or male if the caudal part undergoes differentiation. If none develops, then the animal becomes sterile. entries.description: Subtrapezoidal disc, a uniform purplish-brown, brown, or tan dorsal coloration (devoid of any other markings), and wide, broadly rounded tooth bands . Body shape ( shape guide ): other.
entries.biology: Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore . Occurs over soft bottoms; feeds on bottom-living organisms; possesses electric organs . Biology little known . Gravid females produces 2-3 pups during each gestation. Males mature at ca. 14 cm TL; born at ca. 6 cm TL .

entries.biology: An epibenthic species found in sandy and muddy bottoms on the steep slope. Adults form epibenthic schools, comprising 10-300 individuals (in Kagoshima Bay) .

entries.name: Nealotus tripes

entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 20 - 21; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16 - 19; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 15 - 19; Vertebrae : 36 - 38. Body greatly elongated and compressed. Mouth large with fang-like teeth. Tips of both jaws with dermal processes. Color is blackish brown; dorsal and anal fins pale brown; buccal and branchial cavities and peritoneum black. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic , migrating to the surface at night . Feeds on myctophids and other small fishes, squid and crustaceans . Matures at 15 cm SL .

entries.name: Nectamia fusca
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 20 m . Tropical; 27°N - 27°S, 28°E - 133°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: known from the Red Sea, Indian Ocean (except the Seychelles, Chagos Archipelago, Cargados Carajos, Mauritius and Rodrigues), north to Japan and south to Australia; throughout the West Pacific to the Tonga Islands, Samoa, Phoenix and Marshall Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Common in reef flats and shallow lagoons, but hiding by day within Acropora thickets and other corals, as well as in holes and crevices and emerging at night to forage on free-swimming invertebrates . Also found in sheltered seaward slopes in 1-20 m (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fishes and benthic invertebrates (e.g. shrimps - alpheids and penaieds; isopods, copepods, crab larvae, polychaete worms); relatively close to cover, within about 1-2 m .
entries.reproduction: Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Neenchelys similis
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 1500 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan, Taiwan, New Guinea and Banda Sea.

entries.name: Nematalosa nasus

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Gulf of Aden north to the Persian Gulf, then eastward to the Andaman Sea, South China Sea and the Philippines, and north to southern tip of Korea. Also reported from Durban Bay in South Africa based on a single juvenile .

entries.biology: Known from estuaries and coastal areas, occasionally ascending into the upper reaches of the tidal zone . A filter-feeder. Marketed fresh, dried-salted or boiled. Made into fish balls. Very bony.

entries.name: Nemipterus aurora
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 56 - 90 m . Tropical; 31°N - 8°S, 98°E - 132°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands to southeastern Indonesia.

Body pinkish above, shading through pale mauve to silvery on ventral half with 4 or 5 longitudinal, upward-curved silvery-white stripes along the middle of each scale row below lateral line. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabit sand and muddy bottoms .

entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Strait of Malacca and Gulf of Thailand to southern Japan. This species has been previously misidentified as Nemipterus marginatus by most authors .

Dorsal fin origin about 3-7 scale rows from imaginary line projected upward from posterior edge of suborbital to dorsal profile. Pectoral and pelvic fins long, reaching to or just short of level of anal-fin origin. Closely resembles N. bathybius Snyder, but has no ye
entries.biology: Found on sand or mud bottoms.

entries.name: Neobathyclupea japanotaiwana
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-oceanic; depth range 483 - 677 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan and Taiwan.

This species is distinguished by the following characters: bicolor pattern of the oral cavity, with large areas of dark pigment on light background; head length 2.9-3.1 times in SL; maximum body height 22.4-24.2% SL, preanal distance 44.1-49.8% (51.2%); A 29-31 rays; developed gill rakers on first arch 16-17, the longest 9.1-12.3% (usually less than 12%) of head length; pectoral fin light . Cross section: compressed.

entries.name: Neobythites stigmosus

Operculum with a sharp strong spine and preoperculum with 2 spinules at the lower angle . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: oval.

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Chinese, Korean and Japanese waters.

Scales from head posteriorly to behind the eye but none on cheek; lobate supraorbital tentacle; body coloration white; yellow or orange on scale edges; 6 uneven, oblique, dark brown bands bifurcating ventrally; uneven brown bar below eye with white posterior border; females with thin, oblique, red and white bands on second and third dorsal fins; dull orange in males. entries.biology: Adults are found in coral reefs and intertidal pools . Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites . Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters .

entries.name: Notoscopelus caudispinosus

entries.biology: High-oceanic, mesopelagic species . Occurs deeper than 1,000 m during the day and nyctoepipelagic at the surface and down to 175 m . Probably spawns in autumn-winter in the western North Atlantic .

entries.name: Novaculichthys taeniourus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 25 m , usually ? - 14 m . Tropical; 24°C - 28°C ; 30°N - 30°S, 32°E - 77°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea to South Africa  and the Tuamoto Islands, north to Ryukyu and Hawaiian islands, south to Lord Howe Island. Excluding Persian Gulf . Eastern Pacific: Gulf of California to Panama and the Galapagos Islands .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 12 - 13. Juveniles have long extended dorsal fin spines . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Inhabit semi-exposed reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs . Common in areas of mixed sand, and rubble that are subject to mild surge . Benthopelagic . Juveniles shallow on rubble amongst large bommies or protected open patches on reef crests and swim as if were a leaf floating along the bottom; large adults move along over large reef section, usually in pairs and typically turn or shift large pieces of rubble or debris that they grab and pull with their mouth or push over with their snout. Often, while one works the piece, the other grabs exposed prey. They are sometimes called rock-mover wrasse, but they don't move real rocks . Highly territorial . Feed on mollusks, sea urchins, brittle
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa  to New Guinea, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Lord Howe Island.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 12 - 14. A slender species, usually bright green. Juveniles vary from brown to green, usually with a blotched pattern . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found solitary or in small groups  in seagrass beds and sandy algal flats of lagoons and mangrove channels. Secretive amongst the vegetation and well-camouflaged .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).
