entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 177 - 300 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Mariana Islands, Taiwan and southern Japan.

entries.name: Okamejei acutispina
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 25 - 150 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan to the East China Sea.
entries.biology: Sublittoral on sandy mud bottoms . Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07). Feed on invertebrates and bony fishes . Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsules are 4.9-5.4 cm long and 2.5-2.9 cm wide .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 9908 ). Paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Okamejei boesemani
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 20 - 175 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific; Korea to Vietnam, including Taiwan and southern Japan.
entries.biology: Occur in the sublittoral zone, 70-90 m on sandy mud bottoms . Oviparous. Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother . Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats . Egg capsules measure 6.1 cm long and 3.7 cm wide . Utilization details sketchy . Very rarely caught by demersal longline fisheries off Java. Utilized for its meat .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 9908 ). Paired eggs are laid. Embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ). Distinct pairing with embrace. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Omobranchus punctatus
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; benthopelagic. Tropical; 35°N - 37°S, 20°E - 178°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Fiji and north to Japan; and from Delagoa Bay, Mozambique and Suez Canal on the African coast. Introduced in Trinidad and Panama Canal near Atlantic end.

Horizontal stripes on body distinct in male, but somewhat obscure in female. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Adults occur in coastal and brackish waters among rocks and mangroves . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Highly tolerant to adverse environmental conditions, self-reproducing population living between rocks in natural oil seeps in Venezuela .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.biology: Landlocked populations are found in rivers .
entries.reproduction: Reproductive strategy: synchronous ovarian organization, determinate fecundity (Ref. 51846 ).

entries.distribution: Southeast Indian Ocean and central Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 6; Anal soft rays : 4. Belonging to the Oneirodes schmidti -group. Lacking an anterior escal apparatus. Escal morphology: a pair of simple, elongate, anterolateral escal appendages, without internal pigmentation; a pair of simple, elongate, medial escal appendages, each divided distally into three or more short, slender filaments; a simple, elongate, and anteroposteriorly compress posterior escal appendage, slightly expanded distally; all appendages without pigmentation

entries.name: Oryzias sinensis
entries.environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic. Tropical
entries.distribution: Asia: Mekong, Irrawaddy, Salween, Red River and Nanpangjiang basins . Introduced in Kazakhstan where it is now abundant; established in lower Kuban drainage; spreading in Azov basin, discovered in River Obitochnaya, Ukraine in 2003 .
entries.description: Anal soft rays : 18 - 20. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Adults occur in swamps, marshes, rice fields, backwaters, stream stretches with stagnant water and dense vegetation . In Fuxian Lake, China, they are found in upper and middle layers of shallow coastal waters . Adults feed mainly on filamentous algae and zooplankton . They mature in 3 months time. Spawning occurs between April and September when temperature rises above 26°C. Can tolerate temperatures from 0 to 42°C, surviving winter under ice .
entries.reproduction: A cluster of eggs, about 15-50, are spawned every few days in the morning and females carry them for a few hours, until the eggs are entangled into aquatic vegetation by the filaments which cover them. Eggs hatch in 10-12 days at 24°C (Ref. 59043 ).

entries.name: Osmerus mordax
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; pelagic-oceanic; anadromous ; depth range 0 - 425 m , usually ? - 150 m . Temperate; 6°C - 18°C ; 73°N - 41°N, 167°W - 53°W
entries.distribution: North Atlantic: Atlantic drainages from Lake Melville in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada to Delaware River in Pennsylvania, USA and west through Great lakes. Arctic and Pacific drainages from Bathurst Inlet, Northwest Territories to Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada. Also Pacific drainages of Asia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 12 - 16; Vertebrae : 58 - 70. Body elongate, laterally compressed, greatest depth at anterior of dorsal fin origin. Head moderate; eye moderately large; snout elongate, pointed. Mouth large; lower jaw protruding, maxillary extending to middle of eye or beyond, well toothed on vomer, palatine, pterygoid, basibranchial, dentary, maxillary, and tongue. Teeth specially enlarged on tongue and front of vomer. Body
entries.biology: Nerito-pelagic . Inhabits cool clear lakes, medium to large rivers, and coastal waters . A schooling species that occurs in midwater of lakes or inshore coastal waters ; at temperatures ranging from 7.2-15.6°C. Coastal population are anadromous (Ref, 86798 ). Migrates up to 1,000 km upstream in rivers . Occurs possibly to 425 m . Feeds on invertebrates such as amphipods, ostracods, aquatic insect larvae and aquatic worms ; food also include copepods, euphausiids, mysids and small fishes (silversides, mummichogs and herring) . Headed, gutted, sold fresh, frozen and precooked. Eaten sautéed and fried .
entries.reproduction: Spawning runs occur when temperature is between 8.9-18.3°C, may last for 3 weeks, peak for 1 week. Lengths of both sexes decrease as spawning progress. Two or more tuberculated males maintain position against a female in swift water, eggs released in clusters and presumably milt released simultaneously. Spawning usually takes place at night, spawners move downstream to the lake during daytime.

Decays rapidly, but well liked when fresh.

entries.biology: Specimens are photographed hovering over a dark soft substrate. One individual at Lovina Beach, Bali, appears to be at the entrance of a large burrow (made by another organism).

entries.biology: This species is found in the tidal zone within or around mangroves in estuaries, and where four of the seven specimens were found hovering in small tidepools around the roots of mangrove trees [ Bruguiera gymnorhiza (L.) Savigny] within the forest at night. The substrate of the tidepool was mud, and a thalassinid mud lobster, Thalassina anomala (Herbst, 1804) made a burrow system around the tidepool. Other fish species observed in that tidepool include Bostrychus sinensis, Eleotris melanosoma, Mugilogobius chulae , and Pisodonophis boro ). Characterized by semi-transparent body with fine dark speckling; side of snout with brown stripe; internal brown, dash-like markings with white or yellow pigment along dorsal edge of vertebral column; longitudinal scale series 24-27; scaled head and nape; restricted gill opening to pectoral fin base; depth of body at anus 5.0-7.7 in SL . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal slopes, usually on barrel sponges in 10-30 meters depth . Often in groups (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Plotosus canius
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical; 27°N - 20°S, 72°E - 177°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: west and south coasts of India and off Sri Lanka eastward along the coasts of Bangladesh and Myanmar, through the Indo-Australian Archipelago and the Philippines as far as Papua New Guinea.
entries.description: A plain dusky-brown species with a black dorsal fin tip. Shows banded pattern at night. Distinguished from adult Plotosus lineatus by its long barbels on the nostrils that can reach pass the eyes. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Adults found mostly in estuaries and lagoons, and sometimes up rivers in nearly fresh waters. They occur in the lower parts of rivers in freshwater or brackish water and in coastal seas . It is reported to have an extended breeding season and likely spawns in brackish water, based on optimal sperm survival at 0.9 % salinity; produces relatively few large eggs, consistent with parental care and it is possible that male fish construct nests and guard their fry , Maximum length of 150 cm TL is without actual specimen . Juveniles may occur in dense aggregations . Feed on crustaceans, mollusks and fishes. Spines associated with anterior fins have potent venom. Marketed mostly fresh.

entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 12; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 22 - 30. Dark dorsum, flanks silver . Slender body, longer anal fin and tail set . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: An oceanic and mesopelagic species, adults and juveniles usually found at 200-500 m by day and the majority of them migrate into upper 100-200 m at night. Feeds mainly on small crustaceans. Dioecious with peak spawning during summer. Adult photophore complement attained at about 25-27 mm SL .

entries.name: Polydactylus sexfilis

entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: mainly around oceanic islands. Known from Mauritius, Seychelles, Kenya and many islands of the northern Indian Ocean; then from Indonesia north to the Ryukyu, Ogasawara and Yaeyama islands and east to the Hawaiian Islands, French Polynesia and Pitcairn. Has not been collected in Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 11. Body uniformly golden silver; occasionally with several faint dark stripes along longitudinal scale rows above and below lateral line. Pectoral filaments 6 with tip of uppermost filament reaching to or slightly beyond level of posterior tip of upper part of pectoral fin . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: This schooling species occurs along sandy and rocky shorelines and over sandy lagoon bottoms, often in zones of turbulence . Benthopelagic . Often encountered in river mouths or brackish mangrove estuaries. Feeds mainly on crustaceans (shrimps and crabs), polychaete worms, other benthic invertebrates; also on teleosts . A lunar spawning rhythm occurs close to shore . Sexual maturity in males occurs at 12 to 15 cm . Subsequently undergoes sex reversal passing through a hermaphroditic stage, and become female between 18 and 24 cm . The potential of this species for aquaculture has been studied .

Feed on zooplankton and benthic algae . Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding . Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs .

Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate . Males guard and aerate the eggs . Diurnal species .

This species resembles P. macracanthus with a long and narrow preopercular spine, but has less body depth,

entries.biology: Uncommon species found in outer reef slopes and deep lagoon pinnacles from 8 to at least 80 m. In small aggregations, sometimes schools in oceanic locations . Also found under ledges or hovering next to coral heads during day (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fish, crustaceans, and other small invertebrates . Occasionally taken in moderate numbers in trawls and by hook-and-line . Generally marketed fresh, may be salted or dried . Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .

Adults developing a pronounced protuberance anteriorly on snout (Ref 9808). Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.

They feed on small fishes, shrimps, crabs, amphipods, ascidians and salps. Marketed fresh . Caught mainly with bottom longlines and deep handlines, marketed main fresh and a good quality food fish .

entries.biology: A secretive species that inhabits seaward reefs, among live coral or rubble . Benthic and benthopelagic . Often observed hiding around the base of small heads of live coral, especially Pocillopora meandrina . Stomach contents of specimens taken from Oahu and Johnston I. consisted of demersal eggs, copepods, amphipods, alpheid shrimp, crab megalops, larval shrimp and gastropod. However, it is likely that the copepods and larval food items are from demersal plankton because this species is never seen more than a few centimeters off the bottom .

Adults are solitary and feed on algae and small invertebrates. Juveniles have been observed 'cleaning' other fishes. Because of its dentition, it is regarded as a close relative to the parrotfishes (Scaridae), although it behaves like the species of Anampses .

A single, continuous dorsal fin with spinous part lower than soft portion. Chin with fleshy protuberance narrowing to a thin low, medi
entries.biology: Adults live in reef habitats from shallow coastal slopes to outer reef lagoons and slopes below drop-offs to 50 meters, among rubble . They occur in pairs and their burrows may be situated in coral rock or sand. Monogamous . Adults feed on zooplankton . They tend to form large, though diffuse, colonies; may be due to a propensity to aggregate or may be a result of the ecological requirements for the species (for which type of substratum, current pattern, and water depth among the most important) which restrict the areas of settlement of the postlarvae.
entries.reproduction: Monogamous mating is observed as both obligate and social (Ref. 52884 ).

entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Mozambique Channel, Saya de Malha Bank, Maldives Islands, India, Sri Lanka, Arafura and Java seas, Makassar Strait, northwestern and northeastern Australia and southern Japan . Also recorded from New Caledonia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 19 - 20; Dorsal soft rays (total): 14 - 16; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 11 - 13; Vertebrae : 34. Spinescent gill rakers with 3 or 4 cusps. Lateral line branching from below the 5th to before the 6th spine of the first dorsal fin; the upper lateral line reaching at least to the end of the soft dorsal fin base. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Matures at about 10 cm standard length. A squid was found in the stomach of one specimen .

entries.name: Rexea nakamurai
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 340 - 370 m . Deep-water; 34°N - 18°S, 53°E - 154°W
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Nazareth Bank and off Sumatra in the Indian Ocean and Kyushu-Palau Ridge, Japan and off Oahu, Hawaii.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 19 - 20; Dorsal soft rays (total): 15 - 18; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 12 - 13; Vertebrae : 34. Pectoral fin is represented by a single spine in small specimens or entirely absent in individuals over 25 cm SL. Lateral line branching below the 5th to 6th spine of the first dorsal fin. The upper line reaches to the base of the first dorsal finlet, the lower line runs sub laterally. Most of the body is naked except for a large rectangular stripe of squamation extending
entries.biology: Mesobenthopelagic . Matures at about 25 cm standard length .

entries.name: Rhabdoblennius nitidus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 2 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Western Pacific Ocean: southern Japan to Taiwan, Philippines and Malaysia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 22; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 19 - 23. Teeth on jaws immovable, fewer than 40 in each jaw. Terminal anal fin ray connected by membrane to caudal peduncle. Nasal and supraorbital cirri simple, nuchal cirri absent. Both sexes with occipital crest. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing ; Adults are usually found on the outer reef front of surge channels and pools, exposed to heavy surf. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Rhinecanthus abyssus
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range ? - 150 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific. Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 3; Dorsal soft rays (total): 23 - 26; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 21 - 23. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.

entries.name: Rhinochimaera africana
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 549 - 1450 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Southeast Atlantic: southern Africa and Mozambique Channel. Pacific Ocean: Japan (off Hokkaido and northern Honshu) to the east China Sea, including Taiwan; Costa Rica and Peru.
entries.description: This species is distinguished by the following characters: elongate body with an elongate, broad and paddle-shaped pointed snout extending anterior to head (SNL 47.7% HDL), tapering to a slender tail; the junction of supraorbital and infraorbital canals on ventral side of snout is closer to the tip of the snout than to the nasal canal; ONC/TIO is greater than 1.4 (ONC/TIO= 1.64); TIO/SWF is less than 1.5 (TIO/SWF= 1.47); TIO/LNC is less than 3.0 (TIO/LNC= 2.75); tooth-plates are nearly smooth; e
entries.biology: Rare . Oviparous . Eggs are encased in horny shells .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Rhinoliparis barbulifer
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 28 - 2189 m . Deep-water; 66°N - 32°N
entries.distribution: North Pacific: Sea of Okhotsk, Pacific Ocean off northern Honshu and Hokkaido to Kuril Islands and southeastern Kamchatka, Commander Islands, eastern Aleutian Islands, and southern California, USA.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 63 - 65; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 58; Vertebrae : 68. Pectoral fin deeply notched; caudal fin very slender .

entries.name: Rhinopias eschmeyeri
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 18 - 55 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: A popular aquarium fish, together with Rhinopias frondosa , are collected from Southeast Asian waters, imported to Japan where these are traded separately as different morphotypes . Found in coral reefs and ruble bottoms in 18-55 m (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Rhizoprionodon oligolinx
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 36 m . Tropical; 30°N - 18°S
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf east to Thailand, Indonesia, China, and Japan. Recorded from the Gulf of Carpentaria  and Palau . This species is very close to Rhizoprionodon taylori , but is geographically separated from it .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Anal spines : 0. Position of anal fin origin well in front of second dorsal fin origin, long labial furrows, and short pectoral fins . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: A little known inshore and offshore shark found on continental and insular shelves . Found to depths of at least 36 m . Probably feeds on fishes, cephalopods, and crustaceans . Viviparous . Commonly caught by inshore demersal gillnet fisheries, especially off Java . Utilized fresh and probably dried salted for human consumption . Also used for fishmeal  and fins .
entries.reproduction: Viviparous, placental (Ref. 50449 ). With 3 to 5 young per litter (Ref. 244 , 37816 ). Size at birth 20-30 cm TL (Ref. 9997 , 37816 ). Distinct pairing with embrace (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Rhynchocypris oxycephala
entries.environment: Freshwater; demersal. Temperate; 10°C - 20°C
entries.distribution: Asia: rivers of Pacific basin from Amur southward to Yangtze drainages; in Korea in Yellow Sea basin; southern Japan (Honshu, Kyushu, Shikoku); in Amur, middle reaches of Amur and Bureya River system downstream to lower reaches, Ussuri River but not present in Khanka Lake basin.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 3; Dorsal soft rays (total): 7 - 8; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabits rivers. Predatory fish which feeds on fry, insects and other animal food .

entries.name: Rogadius patriciae
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; non-migratory; depth range 14 - 100 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands  to northern Australia (including Western Australia) and New Caledonia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 12; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 11 - 12. Infraorbital ridges bearing many fine serrations. Lower side of head unicarinate. Dorsal fin rays usually 12; anal fin rays usually 11. Iris lappet bilobed. Caudal fin white with several dark blotches along upper edge and 2 or 3 elongate black bars below. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Taken by trawl on coastal shelves at depths of 14-100 m . Also occurs on sand or rubble bottoms near reefs (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Rudarius excelsus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 8 - 25 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: northern Australia to southern Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 2; Dorsal soft rays (total): 22 - 24; Anal soft rays : 20 - 22; Vertebrae : 20. Diagnosis: Extremely small size at maturity (1.5 cm SL). Prominently elevated dorsal and ventral profiles. Extremely long bristles on caudal peduncle of male, projecting posteriorly to behind middle of caudal fin. Low fin ray counts (D.22 to 24; A.20 to 22; P.10) . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Inhabits sheltered coastal habitats, usually in areas with mixed low reef and sparse seagrass .

entries.name: Salarias alboguttatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 8 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Sri Lanka to Samoa, north to southern Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 16; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 18. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing ; Adults are found in shallow lagoon reefs, on algal covered rocks and rubble . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Salarias guttatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific.
entries.description: Identified by the large yellowish or pink breast spot and series of dusky to pink spots along base of dorsal fin . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Facultative air-breathing ; Adults are found in the intertidal areas and shallow coastal reefs . They inhabit rubble and algae reefs . Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive , and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal . Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters . Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 90102 .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Samariscus triocellatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 30 m . Tropical; 28°N - 18°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian and Society islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 64 - 70; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 51 - 47; Vertebrae : 40 - 41. Body mottled brown with irregular dark and pale markings; 2-3 dark-edged ocelli along lateral line pectorals blackish distally; dorsal and anal fins with minute black dots; caudal fin with black spots . Gill rakers rudimentary . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: Inhabits coral heads of lagoon and seaward reefs; common in shallow caves or under ledges and can lie flat against vertical rock surfaces . Found in rubble slopes in sand or fine-rubble patches . Benthic . Comes out at dusk and hunts on low reef. It has low profile and crawls along like a flatworm, but activity waves its black pectoral fin as it goes . Feeds on small benthic animals .

entries.name: Sargocentron borodinoensis
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range 100 - 190 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Central Pacific: Philippine Sea, Borodino submarine.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13; Anal spines : 4; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 27. This species is distinguished by the following characters: D IX,13; A IV,9; lateral line scales 46, above lateral line 3½ scale rows; gill rakers on first gill arch 12 = 5 + 1 + 9 (vs. 17 to 22 in congeners) ; big pointed spines on posterior operculum edge 2, with lower spine longer than upper spine; nasal fossa edges or on nasale surface without spine . Cross section: compressed.

entries.name: Sargocentron melanospilos
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 5 - 90 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea , Zanzibar (Tanzania), Aldabra and Seychelles to the Marshall Islands and American Samoa, north to Taiwan, southern Japan and the Ogasawara Islands, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef and the Chesterfield Islands. Replaced by Sargocentron marisrubri in the Red Sea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 14; Anal spines : 4; Anal soft rays : 9 - 10. Body with red and white stripes following the scale rows; black blotch at base of soft dorsal, anal, and caudal fins, but may be faint or absent in caudal and anal fins . Uniformly small ctenii on posterior margin of scales of body. Inferior mouth due to hypertrophy of median part of upper lip (front of upper lip thickened and slightly protruding) . Five oblique scale rows on cheek; body depth
entries.biology: A relatively uncommon inhabitant of rocky reefs and coral-rich areas. Spine of preopercle venomous. Usually seen solitary , but sometimes forms schools in deep water in oceanic locations . Found in seaward slopes in 5-90 m .

entries.name: Sargocentron praslin
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 20 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa south to Mozambique (but not the Red Sea) and east to the Marshall, except the northern Marshalls  and Society islands. Recorded from the Mediterranean as a Lessepsian migrant .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 11; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 4; Anal soft rays : 8 - 9. Body with dark brown to brownish red stripes, alternating with silvery white stripes. The upper 2 dark stripes often ending in an elongate dark brown spot at the base of the soft portion of the dorsal fin; the third curving downward to end at mid-base of caudal fin; the 4th ending just before the caudal peduncle; the 5th and 6th stripes converging posteriorly on lower edge of caudal peduncle; 7
entries.biology: Inhabits reef flats and shallow protected reefs, often in dead reef areas . Secretive during the day .

entries.name: Satyrichthys laticeps
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 58 - 300 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Arabian Sea, Saya de Malha Bank, off Indian coast of southern Africa (including Sri lanka and the Andaman Sea); south to Japan, Taiwan, East China Sea, to Sulu Sea, South China Sea, and Indonesia.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 17; Anal soft rays : 14 - 17. This species is distinguished by the following characters: barbels 4 (rarely 3 or 5) lip and 2-5 on the chin; presence of antrose spines on upper lateral bony plates of caudal peduncle; parietal bones unequal in size on midline; dusky spots on dorsal fin absent . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: angular.

entries.name: Satyrichthys rieffeli
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 65 - 600 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan, Taiwan, Sea of Japan, southern Pohai Sea, East China Sea, South China Sea, Indonesia and Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 17; Anal soft rays : 17. This species is distinguished by the following characters: barbels, 2 on lip and 2 (rarely 1) on the chin; head and body with scattered dusky small spots; upper lateral bony plates of caudal peduncle with antrose spines . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: angular.
entries.biology: Inhabits warm tropical seas along the continental shelf edge and slope and insular areas . Benthic .

entries.name: Saurida eso
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwestern Pacific: widespread; from Russia (Peter the Great Bay) to the South China Sea, including Japan, South Korea, China (Yellow Sea to Hainan Island), Taiwan, and Vietnam.
entries.description: Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 13; Anal soft rays : 9 - 12. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits shallow waters with sandy-muddy bottoms .

entries.name: Saurida nebulosa
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 100 m , usually 2 - 60 m . Tropical; 28°N - 28°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Mauritius to the Society Islands, north to the Hawaiian Islands, south to Sydney Harbor, New South Wales, Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 9 - 10. Saurida differs from all other lizardfishes by possessing several rows of villiform teeth extending outward onto the lips beyond the normal row of large canine, and 9 instead of 8 pelvic rays. The species is recognized by the large dark blotches below the dorsal fins . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: circular.
entries.biology: Benthic in sand, mud, rock and eel-grass habitats . Solitary on sand and silt bottoms (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fishes . Found primarily inshore, e.g. in mangroves and seagrass beds, also near streams and river mouths. Piscivorous. Caught with artisanal gear. Sold fresh in markets.

entries.name: Scalicus amiscus
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Deep-water
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: southern Japan and the East China Sea.

entries.name: Scalicus hians
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 275 - 858 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Japan, Taiwan and the South China Sea . Eastern Central Pacific: Hawaii.
entries.biology: Benthic on sand .

entries.name: Scarus chameleon
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 30 m . Tropical; 30°N - 32°S
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Christmas Island  and Western Australia in the eastern Indian Ocean to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Lord Howe Island.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Inhabits outer reef flats and exposed lagoon and seaward slopes from a depth of 3 to at least 30 m . Feeds mainly on algae . Females often in schools of mixed species when feeding, males usually seen separate .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Scarus fuscocaudalis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 20 - 45 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Ryukyu Islands, Philippines, and Guam. Records from Indonesia and Papua New Guinea are questionable and confirmation is needed.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 25. Presence of 4 median predorsal scales; 3 rows of scales on cheek, the upper row with 6-7 scales, the middle row with 6 scales, and the lower row with 1 or 2 scales; 1 or 2 laterally projecting canines posteriorly on side of dental plates of adults; lips covering more than 3/4 of dental plates; dorsal fin moderately high, the longest dorsal spine 2.1-2.6 in head length; caudal fin truncate
entries.biology: Found in coastal to outer reef crests and along drop-offs, usually in small groups ; occurs at depths greater than 20 m .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Scolecenchelys aoki
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 80 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: restricted to Japanese waters, excluding northern Hokkaido and Ryukyu Archipelago, and southern Korea .
entries.description: Vertebrae : 130 - 138. This elongate species of Scolecenchelys is distinguished by the following set of characters: head 7.6-10 % TL, tail 51-57 % TL; infraorbital pores 3 at postorbital area; median groove present ventrally on snout, extending anteriorly beyond level of anterior margin of tubular anterior-nostril base; acute snout; rictus of mouth slightly posterior to a vertical line through posterior margin of eye; conical and pointed teeth on upper jaw and vomer forming uniserial or biserial
entries.biology: Occurs in shallow tide pools to a depth of 80 m .

entries.name: Scolecenchelys fuscapenis
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 112 - 269 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.
entries.biology: The largest specimen was a ripe male .

entries.name: Scoliodon macrorhynchos
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Central Pacific: W Indonesia, Malaysia, Gulf of Thailand, Singapore, Borneo, Philippines, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan; exceptions, E Indonesia, New Guinea, northern Australia, and remainder of the Oceania region.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 149 - 171. This small carcharhinid species is distinguished by the following set of characters: snout long and extremely flattened; slender body and tail; smooth-edged teeth with slender, strongly oblique, blade-like cusps and no cusplets; anterior teeth strongly sexually dimorphic, for adult males greatly elongate and flexuous; total tooth row counts 25-28/23-28 rows or 48-56 total rows; second dorsal-fin origin well posterior of anal-fin origin, about opposite posterior third of an
entries.biology: Adults are found in shallow, inshore waters, most abundant near large freshwater outflows, e.g. Pearl River estuary (Hong Kong) and the large Borneo drainage systems .

entries.name: Scolopsis affinis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 3 - 60 m . Tropical; 32°N - 21°S, 96°E - 166°E
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Andaman Sea in the eastern Indian Ocean to Indonesia, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to northeastern Australia and the Solomon Islands. This species has been incorrectly referred to as Scolopsis personatus (a junior synonym of Scolopsis auratus ) by some authors.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7. Lower limb of preopercle scaly. Antrorse (forward-directed) suborbital spine absent. Pelvic fins long, reaching to or beyond level of anus. Larger specimens with upper and lower lobes falcate. Presence of indistinct bluish stripe between eyes and a narrow white stripe from middle of upper lip to below eye. Juveniles with dusky brown stripe on either side of dorsal midline, and dusky brown midlateral stri
entries.biology: Inhabits sheltered lagoons on sandy or muddy bottoms close to reefs. Occurs singly or in small aggregations. Adults mainly in depths over 15 m; juveniles solitary and in sheltered coastal habitats .

entries.name: Scopelosaurus adleri
entries.environment: Marine; bathypelagic; depth range 102 - 1440 m . Deep-water; 60°N - 20°N
entries.distribution: North Pacific: off Taiwan, waters of Kamchatka, Japan, and Kuril Islands, Sea of Okhotsk, Bering Sea, off British Columbia, California and Alaska Bay.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 17 - 20; Vertebrae : 58 - 61. Pyloric caeca, 16-26. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Individuals of 20-22 cm SL, feeds on various types of plankton, almost exclusively deep-sea copepods of Pareuchaeta . Larger specimens also feed on squid, shrimp, and fish .

entries.name: Scorpaena hatizyoensis
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Hachijôjima, Japan.

entries.name: Scorpaena izensis
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 80 - 200 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific.
entries.description: Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Found on the continental shelf; in sandy mud bottom . Benthic .

entries.name: Scorpaenodes albaiensis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa to the western Pacific . Recently recorded from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13 - 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Rare species . Very secretive in coastal coral reefs and rarely seen by divers, even at night . Solitary (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Scorpaenodes guamensis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 20 m , usually 0 - 5 m . Tropical; 35°N - 40°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea east to the Society Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13 - 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 7 - 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Thie species is distinguished by the following set of characters: pectoral-fin rays 17-20 (mode 18), some rays branched in specimens over ca. 40 mm SL; dorsal-fin soft rays 7-9 (8); scale rows in longitudinal series 40-46 (43); underside of lower jaw scaleless; gill rakers 11-15 (13); with nasal spine; lateral lacrimal spine is usually present; suborbital spines 2, first spine below eye, second
entries.biology: Found in rock crevices in reef flats, shallow lagoons, and channels. Feeds mainly at night on small shrimps, crabs, and polychaetes. Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland . Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Scorpaenodes hirsutus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 8 - 54 m . Tropical; 35°N - 25°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Marquesan and Pitcairn islands, north to Ryukyu and Hawaiian islands, south to Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5 - 6. Covered with short hairlike filaments . With vertical scale rows about 30; usually with 4 spines on suborbital ridge, first on lateral face of lachrymal bone; usually 1 additional spine below suborbital ridge at level between second and third spines; presence of interorbital spines; absence of small spines at midline between tympanic spines . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 40 m . Benthic in coral reefs . Venomous spines .

entries.name: Scorpaenodes quadrispinosus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 12 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific : Christmas Island to Fiji and the Marshall Islands northward to Ryukyu Islands southward to Papua New Guinea. Also recorded in Australia .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10 - 11; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5 - 6. Distinguished from all other Scorpaenodes species by having the first two spines on the suborbital ridge extending dorsally above the lower orbit margin; no distinct dark spot on opercle, subopercle, or spinous dorsal fin; pectoral fin rays usually 17; vertical scale rows 39-43; head and upper body light cream overlaid by dark brown to black pigment pattern; lower half of body light cream to wh
entries.biology: Found in coral reefs in 0-12 m (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Scorpaenopsis macrochir
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 80 m . Tropical; 35°N - 25°S
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: northwest Australia, Moluccas, and Philippines to the Marquesan and Society islands, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to Rowley Shoals, Western Australia, and Tonga; Mariana and Caroline Islands in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Submarginal black band on inner pectoral fin surface complete; eyes relatively large; snout relatively short; hump on back less obvious as in S. diabolus ; SL to 10.4 cm. No black spot nearly as large as eye on inner surface of pectoral fins. A narrow triangular black mark inside mouth at front of upper jaw behind teeth. Ascending process of premaxilla broad, its maximum width 1.4-1.8 in orbit diameter.
entries.biology: A rare inhabitant of mixed sand and rubble areas of reef flats and shallow lagoons. Feeds on fishes . Usually buries itself in the substrate when in sand or sits amongst rubble where it has good camouflage . Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland . Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Scorpaenopsis orientalis
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 8 - 20 m . Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 24. About one-half of eye projecting above dorsal profile of head; interorbital space V-shaped and deep, the maximum depth about 2.5 in orbit diameter; third dorsal spine usually longest (2.15-2.5 in head length); first dorsal spine 2.0-2.5 in second spine; snout length 2.8-3.05 in head length (Ref 42181). Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.

entries.name: Scorpaenopsis papuensis
entries.environment: Marine; brackish; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 40 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Indonesia and the Philippines to the Society Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and Fiji.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Snout length > orbit diameter. Has a dark purplish blotch on the rear of the spinous dorsal fin . Juveniles with large, forward pointing tentacles above the eyes . Space on opercle between opercular spines scaled; penultimate dorsal spine 1.9-2.2 in length of last spine; reaches 195 mm SL (rarely over 170 mm) (Ref 42181). Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Found in coral and rocky areas to depths over 40 m ; also in coastal and slopes, estuaries and lagoons, often in algae covered rubble zones . Feeds on fishes . Solitary and difficult to see due to camouflage colors (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Scorpaenopsis venosa
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 2 - 95 m , usually ? - 25 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: East Africa to Papua New Guinea, north to Taiwan  and the Philippines, south to the Great Barrier Reef . Also reported from the Saya de Malha Bank (76-95 meters) .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Adults are best recognized by the tiny light-blue ocelli scattered over the body, and dark triangle below the eye. Small juveniles have three distinctive white spots along the back . A deep quadrangular occipital pit, its anterior edge, as viewed dorsally, with a slight ridge. A low ridge on each side of pit between tympanic and parietal spines. Pectoral rays strongly modally at 17 (Ref 42181). Body shap
entries.biology: Inhabits coastal reefs ; usually taken by diving in protected areas of bays or lagoons, often where the fish can be well camouflaged in areas of algae, seagrass or sponge . Venomous spines. Occurs along continental margins or islands associated with continents, not at true oceanic islands (Ref 90102).

entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 40 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Indo-Pacific: South Africa and the Red Sea to Fr. Polynesia; north to Japan; south to Australia
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5; Vertebrae : 24. A broad dark band across soft portion of anal and pelvic fins. Maxilla extending posterior to a vertical at rear edge of orbit. Interorbital ridges low, flaring laterally to base of tympanic spines; no median interorbital ridge. Occipital pit shallow, its anterior edge inwardly curved. A small but deep suborbital pit. Suborbital ridge with 4 retrorse spines, the first on lacrimal; posteri
entries.biology: Inhabits coral reefs and areas with rubble bottom .

entries.name: Scuticaria okinawae
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: Mauritius to Hawaii and Tahiti, north to Japan.
entries.description: Vertebrae : 169 - 177. Color in alcohol uniform yellowish brown to chocolate brown. Easily identified by its very short tail (anus at 2/3 TL) and its uniform dark coloration . MVF 168-170-176. Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Benthic .

entries.name: Sebastapistes mauritiana
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m , usually 0 - 5 m . Tropical; 16°N - 28°S
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marquesan and Rapa islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and Samoa.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. Underside of head with weak dark bars; spinous dorsal normally with dark spot . Strong coronal ridges with spine; distinct occipital pit, deepening with age . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Inhabits outer intertidal reef flats and shallow lagoon reefs exposed to wave action. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

entries.name: Sebastapistes tinkhami
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 1 - 30 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 5. With dark spots, especially on rear of body and rear fins . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal.
entries.biology: Rare species. Inhabits deeper reefs. Solitary and cryptic, also found in seaward reefs, mainly at oceanic islands (Ref 90102).

entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Temperate
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan and South Korea.
entries.biology: Inhabit rocky coasts. Viviparous .

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: northern Japan.
entries.description: Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.

entries.name: Sebastes melanostictus
entries.environment: Marine; benthopelagic; depth range 84 - 1000 m , usually 350 - 450 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Pacific: from Japan (about 35°N), north through the Kuril Is., Aleutian Is., and the Bering Sea to 60.5°N; south to southern California on Coronado Bank, at 32.6°N.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 12 - 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 15; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7 - 8; Vertebrae : 26 - 27. Head spines, 8; infraorbital spines, 2 or more; body coloration generally dusky with faint mottling on dorsum; spinous dorsal-fin and rest of body often spotted; dorsal-fin spine 1 longer, 1.0 to 1.8 times into orbit length, 5.9-9.6% SL; dorsal-fin spine 4 longer, 12.0-18.4% SL; gill rakers longer, 3.9-7.1% SL and more numerous in comparison to S. aleutianus . Genetica

entries.name: Sebastes variabilis
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 6 - 675 m , usually 100 - 300 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: North Pacific: Japan, east coast of Kamchatka to Cape Ol'utorskii in western Bering Sea, along the Aleutian Islands to 60°N in the eastern Bering Sea, through the Gulf of Alaska south to Johnstone Strait, British Columbia and to central Oregon.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13 - 14; Dorsal soft rays (total): 13 - 16; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 7 - 9; Vertebrae : 28 - 29. This species is distinguished by the following characters: body light yellow to greenish brown to gray, typically greenish brown, with orange flecks present on sides, distinctly light ventrally above anal-fin base and on ventral pectoral-fin rays; peritoneum light gray to jet black; strong symphyseal knob; extrinsic swimbladder muscle with a single section of striated
entries.biology: Collection depth between 6-370 m, deepest recorded depth at 675 m. Large adults common along the edge of the continental shelf at 100-300 m where the species is targeted for commercial use. Captured in the offshore trawl fishery. Males and females captured by trawl surveys vary widely in maturity during the summer (May-July) .

entries.name: Sebastes zonatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 50 - 175 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: Japan  and South Korea .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 12 - 13; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 6 - 7; Vertebrae : 26.
entries.biology: Inhabits rocky reefs .

entries.name: Selar boops
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 35 - 500 m . Subtropical; 31°N - 23°S, 75°E - 134°W
entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Andaman Islands to Vanuatu, north to the Philippines, south to northern Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 23 - 25; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 19 - 21. Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Adults are found inshore and form large schools on day time. They disperse at night to feed on planktonic and benthic invertebrates such as crabs and shrimps. Eggs are pelagic .

entries.name: Setipinna tenuifilis
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; pelagic-neritic; amphidromous ; depth range 0 - 50 m . Tropical; 42°N - 17°S, 81°E - 147°E
entries.distribution: Eastern Indian Ocean: northern and eastern Bay of Bengal coasts, including the Andaman Islands; perhaps southward from the Godavari river. Western Pacific: northern coast of Australia, Arafura Sea , Gulf of Papua, Sarawak, presumably the Philippines and Hong Kong; China from Taiwan north to Yellow Sea and southern part of Sea of Japan.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 46 - 56. Belly with 18 to 20 (rarely 17 or 21) + 7 (sometimes 8) = 25 to 27 keeled scutes from isthmus to anus. Lower gill rakers with the serrae uneven, with slight or sometimes distinct clumps of larger serrae. Pectoral filament moderate, reaching back to base of 9th to 21st anal fin ray. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Presumably schooling and occurring mostly in coastal waters, but also entering estuaries  (e.g. the Hooghly and Godavari in India) and penetrating at least 20 km up the Godavari, tolerating salinities as low as 8.7 ppt. Feeds on prawn, copepods, crustacean larvae, mollusks and fishes. Fairly common .

entries.name: Sicyopterus longifilis
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical; 19°N - 6°S
entries.distribution: Asia: Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia; and Papua New Guinea.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10. This species is distinguished by the following characters: upper lip with no median cleft, but with a lateral cleft on each side of lip; margin of upper lip between lateral clefts minutely serrated; no tubercle behind median cleft; ridge beneath the upper lip only with feeble papillae; premaxillary teeth tricuspid; first dorsal-fin spines, especially second to fifth spines, are long and filamentous in males; posterior tip of first dorsal fi
entries.biology: Lives in coastal streams with moderate to fast flow . Usually found in small. clear creeks, often in rainforest within about 50 km of the sea .

entries.name: Sicyopterus macrostetholepis
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Tropical; 10°N - 10°S
entries.distribution: Philippines and Indonesia. Also Ryukyu Islands . May be present in Papua New Guinea  and Guam .

entries.name: Siganus lineatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 25 m , usually 0 - 20 m . Tropical; 25°C - 29°C ; 27°N - 30°S, 71°E - 171°E
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Maldives, Laccadive Archipelago, India, Sri Lanka, Ogasawara Islands (Japan), eastern Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Philippines; Palau and Yap in Micronesia. Records from Viet Nam  is probably Siganus guttatus .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 7; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 13. This species is distinguished by the following characters: body deep and compressed; greatest body depth 1.9-2.2 in SL; longest dorsal-fin spines 4th to 8th, a little longer (1.1-1.3 times) the last dorsal-fin spine. Colour blue dorsally, silvery below; horizontal golden bronze bands, some broken, running along single sides of trunk, breaking up into spots near bases of dorsal and anal f
entries.biology: Adults inhabit shallow areas, typically 5 m; juveniles common around estuarine areas including mangrove areas and seagrass flats; adults in protected waters such as lagoons and bays in the vicinity of rocky substrata or reefs (resting on rubble or sandy bottoms). Form schools that diminish with age, down to 10-25 fish by adult stage, although congregations may consist of several thousand fish during spawning period. Feed by scraping encrusting algae from beach rock or pavement areas of coral reefs or by browsing on larger coarse algae. Caught mainly with set nets and fixed traps; common in markets where it is sold fresh .
entries.reproduction: Smallest female to spawn was 23 cm, the largest 33 cm SL. Spawning apparently occurs not until the fish is 2 years old.

entries.name: Siganus punctatissimus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 12 - 30 m . Tropical; 30°N - 24°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Ryukyu Islands, Palau (Belau), Philippines, northern Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, northern Queensland and reefs off northwestern Western Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 13; Dorsal soft rays (total): 10; Anal spines : 7; Anal soft rays : 9; Vertebrae : 13. Head and body dark chocolate brown with purplish hue; iris pale rose-brown, white spotted. Spines stout, pungent, venomous. Preopercular angle 93°-109°. Cheeks completely scaled. Midline of thorax scaled; a row of scales absent along pelvic ridges. Anterior nostril with low rim; expanded posteriorly into a broad flap, reaching halfway to posterior nostril. Body shape ( shape guide ): sho
entries.biology: Inhabits lagoon and channel reefs , usually near steep slopes and harbours . Usually seen in pairs. Feeds on benthic seaweeds .

North Atlantic: 65°-30°N. Indo-Pacific: in tropical and subtropical waters. Eastern Pacific: found in California and Baja California , and Chile . Indian Ocean, tropical and subtropical waters . South China Sea and East Chin
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0; Dorsal soft rays (total): 11 - 15; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 27 - 32; Vertebrae : 39 - 41. Black in color, slightly silvery laterally; fins dusky and with small black spots; distal portion of pectorals and pelvic fins colorless . Dorsal adipose fin present. Branchiostegal rays: 12-13 . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Meso- to bathypelagic . Occur between 100-200 m and 500-800 m at night and 25-600 m and 1,250-1,500 m during the day . Feed on crustaceans and small fishes . Photophores develop in fishes over 6-22 mm SL . Protandric hermaphrodite, oviparous with planktonic eggs and larvae .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous (Ref. 35800 ).

entries.name: Siphamia argentea
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 23 - 50 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Western Australia, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Found in sand and mud bottoms in 23-50 m (Ref 90102).
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Siphamia fuscolineata
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 7 - 27 m . Tropical; 24°N - 6°S
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Sumatra, south Taiwan, and the Marshall Islands.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Plain dark brown to black, showing a lined pattern on occasion, and usually when caught or as juveniles. Black lines slightly broader in width to pale interspaces. Sometimes confused with the striped form of Siphamia tubifer or S. versicolor , that has narrower black lines . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep.
entries.biology: A rare species found in lagoons, among the spines of Acanthaster planci , in groups of up to 31  from depths of 7 m or more . Minimum depth taken from Ref. 57178 .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.distribution: Pacific Ocean: Japan

Body depth 2.3-2.7 in SL and body width 1.95-2.25 in the depth; eye diameter 2.65-3.1 in head length; first dorsal spine 2.3-10.3 in second spine; second dorsal spine 4.35-6.2, spine of second dorsal fin 3.5-4.4,and second anal spine 4.7-5.6, all in head lengt

This species is distinguished from its congeners by the following characters: a wider snout (11.7-13.1% of SL; 29.2-34.6% of HL); dorsal spines 4, the 1st and 2nd close to the tip of snout, 3rd and 4th completely contained within loose fold of skin which connects these 2 spines to the soft dorsal fin; with blunt, sturdy cranial spines; uniform brown coloration, lacking vermiculations or contrasti

entries.name: Solegnathus hardwickii
entries.environment: Marine; demersal. Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Indian Ocean: Mauritius. Western Pacific: South China Sea north to southern Japan, south to northern Australia.
entries.description: Body shape ( shape guide ): eel-like.
entries.biology: Found in the continental shelf. Ovoviviparous . The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail .
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Solenostomus armatus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; non-migratory; depth range 0 - 95 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: Southeast of Kyushu Islands, Japan to Arafura Sea, Indonesia and Australia; east tio Fiji. Also known from China.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 20 - 22; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 20 - 22; Vertebrae : 32 - 33. Total number of body plates is 33-35. Color and color patterns highly variable: most specimens in dark-color phase with dark red background overlaid with reticulated yellow to orange blotches; some in light-color phase of yellow to beige with few spots of darker pigment on body. Two large black spots present between first and third dorsal-fin spines . Long caudal peduncle
entries.biology: Adults occur over muddy bottom. Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch .
entries.reproduction: Pelvic fins of females are modified as brood pouch for the reception of the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Solenostomus leptosoma
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated, usually 15 - ? m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Mauritius, Japan, Indonesia and Australia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 21; Anal soft rays : 18 - 21. Body shape ( shape guide ): other; Cross section: flattened.
entries.biology: Found along the reef's edge, bordering on open sand substrates . Mostly pelagic until they settle on the substrate for breeding . Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch .
entries.reproduction: Pelvic fins of females are modified as brood pouch for the reception of the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Solenostomus paegnius
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 10 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from East Africa to Australia, north to Japan; confirmed East Indian records from Indonesia and Malaysia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 18 - 21; Anal soft rays : 18 - 21. This species usually with prominent filamentous appendages along the ventral surface of the snout and may also have shorter appendages along the dorsal surface. Some individuals have 'hairy' filamentous appendages covering head, body and fins. Body with variable shades of brown, red and green, often with white mottling .
entries.biology: Found in algal/rubble reefs and sandy bottoms, often at depths below 10 m . Mostly pelagic until they settle on the substrate for breeding .

entries.name: Solenostomus paradoxus
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 4 - 35 m . Tropical
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Fiji, north to southern Japan, south to southeast Australia and New Caledonia. Recently recorded from Tonga .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 5; Dorsal soft rays (total): 17 - 21; Anal spines : 0; Anal soft rays : 17 - 21; Vertebrae : 32 - 33. Post-pelagic are almost fully transparent and more slender compared to those established in the benthic phase. Variable in color from black to red and yellow, usually in a mix of bands and spots . Total body number of plates 31-35. Caudal fin truncate, rounded or lanceolate. Caudal fins of females modified into brood pouch . Body shape ( shape guide ): other; Cross section
entries.biology: Adults usually settle along reef edges in current-prone areas . Uncommon species found solitary or paired, among branches of gorgonians, floating weeds, or crinoids . They feed mostly on mysids but also target small benthic shrimps . Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch .
entries.reproduction: Pelvic fins of females are modified as brood pouch for the reception of the eggs (Ref. 205 ).

entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 274 - 550 m . Deep-water
entries.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: widespread, off South Africa, New Caledonia, Taiwan and Japan, Hawaii.

Centers of scales flecked with black around bases of apical spines . Tubercles on dorsal surface of disk with simple spines, elsewhere on body with multi-spined tubercles, especially prominent on principal tubercles of tail; fins without tubercles. Rostrum with a large multifold median spine protruding beyond its neighbors, termi
entries.biology: Bathymetric range possibly up to 900 m . Benthic .

entries.name: Sphaeramia orbicularis
entries.environment: Marine; reef-associated; depth range 0 - 5 m . Tropical; 31°N - 27°S, 32°E - 173°W
entries.distribution: Indo-Pacific: East Africa to Kiribati, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia; Belau to eastern Caroline and Mariana Islands in Micronesia.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 8; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 9. Greenish grey, with dark vertical bar from origin of spiny dorsal to just in front of anus; scattered spots on body, head and 1st dorsal membrane; pelvic fins dark . Body shape ( shape guide ): short and / or deep; Cross section: compressed.
entries.biology: Restricted to coastal waters, forming small aggregations among mangroves, rocks, debris, or piers of shallow sheltered shorelines. Feeds at night (early evening and just before day break), primarily on planktonic crustaceans. Courtship and spawning occur fortnightly (shortly before new moons and full moons). Eggs are incubated by the male for about 8 days. Larval phase pelagic. Sexual maturity is attained at 7 cm by males and at 6 cm by females .
entries.reproduction: Courtship and spawning occur on a semi-lunar cycle, shortly before full and new moons (Ref. 37816 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ). Are mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Males incubate up to 12,000 eggs for a period of about 8 days (Ref. 37816 ). After the pelagic larval phase, juveniles settle and grow at a rate of 3 to 6 mm per month (Ref. 37816 ).

Senou believes that it occurs from the Philippines to north-eastern Australia . The exact range is uncertain because of confusion of this species with Sphyraena helleri .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6; Dorsal soft rays (total): 8 - 9; Anal spines : 2; Anal soft rays : 8. Body with a narrow dark stripe on the lower flank; a dark marking on body near pelvic fin base; caudal fin darkish . Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs . Also found in bays . Schooling species. Nocturnally active .

Posterior tip of maxilla nor or just reaching to below anterior nostril. Posterior tip of opercle obtuse just above level of pectoral-fin base. A single row of scales in the suborbital groove not covered with skin. Two distinct longitudinal stripes on the side of the body with fresh (upper stripe usually lost in preserved specimens); lower stripe especially distinct, running from t
entries.biology: A shallow coastal water inhabitant .

entries.name: Squalus brevirostris
entries.environment: Marine; pelagic-neritic; depth range ? - 130 m . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Western Pacific: southern Japan  to the South China Sea.
entries.biology: Known from the continental shelves, sometimes at depths greater than 130 m . Ovoviviparous .
entries.reproduction: Distinct pairing with embrace (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Squatina formosa
entries.environment: Marine; bathydemersal; depth range 183 - 220 m . Deep-water; 24°N - 22°N, 120°E - 121°E
entries.distribution: North Western Pacific: East coast of Taiwan and Ryuku Islands to SE Japan to Izu Peninsula ; misidentifiction of S. caillieti in the Philippines .
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 0. Taiwan angelshark Squatina formosa has broad pectoral fins with outer corner more obtuse and free rear tips narrowly subangular; nasal barbels apparently simple, narrow and tapered. Anterior nasal flaps smooth to weakly fringed; dermal folds on sides of head possibly with a triangular lobe. Rear tip of inner margin of pelvic fins reaching little beyond origin of first dorsal. Very short hypocercal tail. Rows of small spines on midline of back and tail, and on snout and
entries.biology: A little-known angelshark found on the outer continental shelf. Possibly larger. Ovoviviparous .
entries.reproduction: Ovoviviparous, embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449 ).

entries.name: Stenogobius ophthalmoporus
entries.environment: Freshwater; brackish; demersal. Tropical
entries.distribution: Asia: Japan, Taiwan, Viet Nam, Philippines and Indonesia.

Predorsal midline fully scaled, usually 19-21; cheek almost always naked; opercle scaled; pectoral base scaled; belly scaled anteriorly near pelvic base; breast always with exposed or embedded scales; basal half of first dorsal fin with two black bands, lower band may originate behind first or second spine; sexual dichromatism not well developed . Body shape ( shape guide ): fusiform / normal; Cross
entries.biology: Known from estuaries to lowland rivers and streams in fresh water.

entries.distribution: Northwest Pacific: southern Kuril Islands, southwestern Okhotsk Sea, Tatar Strait to Peter the Great Bay and Moneron Island, Japan Sea.
entries.biology: Occurs in coastal waters . Inhabits sandy bottoms with coarse and silted sand, seagrass beds and rarely in rocky slopes with sand .

entries.biology: Adults and juveniles inhabit freshwater streams, usually in pools. Often form shoals with conspecific individuals and the congeners Stiphodon percnopterygionus and Stiphodon atropurpureus , and occasionally with Stiphodon imperiorientis .

entries.name: Stiphodon elegans

entries.distribution: Asia. Oceania and Pacific Ocean.
entries.biology: Inhabits clear, relatively swift rainforest streams, close to the coast . Feeds on algae .

entries.biology: The species was observed in a small pool less than 1 m deep and a rapid just below the pool, located 1.5 km from the stream mouth, no major barrier to upstream migration between the stream mouth and this site. The individuals were often shoaled with the abundant S. percnopterygionus and observed scratching on the rock surface for feeding with them. Single individuals of S. atropurpureus and S. multisquamus were also observed at the same site. Other abundant fishes found on the site were amphidromous gobies, such as Sicyopterus japonicus (Tanaka 1909), Awaous melanocephalus (Bleeker 1849), Rhinogobius nagoyae Jordan and Seale 1906, and Tridentiger kuroiwae Jordan and Tanaka 1927, amphidromous

entries.name: Stiphodon percnopterygionus
entries.environment: Marine; freshwater; brackish; demersal; amphidromous . Subtropical
entries.distribution: Asia: Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan. Oceania: Guam, Mariana Islands and Babelthuap, Palau.
entries.description: Dorsal spines (total): 6 - 7; Dorsal soft rays (total): 9 - 10; Anal spines : 1; Anal soft rays : 10 - 11. Body shape ( shape guide ): elongated.
entries.biology: Adults inhabit small, clear streams with rocky bottoms usually covered with dense mats or clumps of algae . This species produces small pyriform eggs, laid on the undersurfaces of stones in freshwater streams. Newly hatched larvae are small (0.12-0.13 cm in notochord length) and poorly developed. These migrate downstream to the sea shortly after hatching at dusk, where they develop as pelagic larvae for 2.5-5 months. Pelagic larvae may potentially disperse to distant islands before migrating to freshwater streams when they reach 1.3-1.4 cm standard length (SL) where they grow further and reproduce .

No dermal flap or small tentacle dorsally on eye. One large pore in interorbital space on each side close to the edge of the orbit; a small median pore posteriorly in interorbital space. Tubular an

entries.biology: Only two specimens were collected from the deep waters, but It is expected to have wider distributions, horizontally and vertically. Stomach contents include small crustaceans, snails and bivalves. Little else is known about the biology of this species .

entries.biology: Occur in protected coastal shallows over or among algae, seagrasses , or floating weeds . Juveniles occasionally found near the surface . Ovoviviparous . The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail . Used in Chinese medicine to extract Hailong, one of the important drugs . Has been reared in captivity .
entries.reproduction: Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205 ).

entries.reproduction: Generally solitary, but up to four males may have been observed courting a single larger female. A courting male may station itself atop a female and puff out its opercula and spread its fins in a display of aggression towards other males (Ref. 37816 ).

entries.biology: Inhabits deep lagoon and seaward reefs to depths over 40 m ; sometimes found on sandy bottoms concealing itself in the sand. Prefers to rest on hard surfaces and frequently occurs in pairs . Benthic . Feeds on small fishes by seizing these from passing schools, also shrimps . Caught with various types of artisanal gear; sold fresh or dried salted in markets. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797 .

Nocturnal species .
entries.reproduction: Are mouthbrooders (Ref. 240 ). Distinct pairing during courtship and spawning (Ref. 205 ).

entries.name: Tetronarce californica
entries.environment: Marine; demersal; depth range 0 - 906 m , usually 3 - 200 m . Temperate; 48°N - 23°N, 126°W - 110°W

entries.biology: Found on the outer continental shelf, around rocks, in kelp beds, over fine sand bottoms or buried in sand. Solitary, nomadic, and can remain suspended in the water with minimal swimming . Feeds on bony fishes, mainly herrings and halibuts. Ovoviviparous . Produces litters of up to 17 pups. Males reaches maturity at ca. 65 cm TL, females at ca. 73 cm TL . Attacks their prey from the substratum by day and actively forage at night with the aid of its electric organ discharge or EOD . The EOD of a large individual was measured at 50 V; with a low internal organ resistance the power output exceeded 1 kW . Aggressive when provoked but no human has yet been injured by the electric shock . Does not
entries.reproduction: Exhibit ovoviparity (aplacental viviparity), with embryos feeding initially on yolk, then receiving additional nourishment from the mother by indirect absorption of uterine fluid enriched with mucus, fat or protein through specialised structures (Ref. 50449 ). Reproductive cycle appears to be annual in males and biannual in females (Ref. 48844 ). No defined birthing season (Ref. 48844 ).

Also occurs in surge-swept reef flats, reef margins, and clear rocky shorelines, but may venture to deeper waters up to 10 m . Benthopelagic . Feeds on crustaceans (especially crabs), mollusks, and ophiuroids (brittle stars) .
entries.reproduction: Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205 ).

If this is the species being referred to in Ref. 6841 , then the principal food of the young would be prawns and copepods, supplemented by polychaetes and amphipods. Minimum depth range from Ref. 137633 .

Often appearing a rich deep yellow with wide dark brown bands, and red/orange fin margins; mature adults are very dark with prominent black stripes and a patch of scarlet scales behind the head . entries.biology: Adults are found in widely diverse habitat ; they favor areas where plant cover exists along the edges of rivers, lakes or swamps , but tend to be confined to shallow weedy areas, so ithey do not build up large populations in deep lakes . They are reported to be cold-confined . Adults are omnivorous, feeding on animal and plant matter , preferentially on filamentous algae, aquatic macrophytes and vegetable matter of terrestrial origin like leaves, plants, etc. . Juveniles feed on small crustaceans and midge larvae . It is forage fish for bass . A substrate spawner . Male and female form pairs to rear the young . It undertakes seasonal upstream migration and breeds before and during these mig
entries.reproduction: A substrate spawner (Ref. 118638 ). Male spreads his milt over the cluster of eggs which are deposited on the bottom or even attached to the branches of aquatic weeds; parents guard the eggs; eggs and fry may be moved into the mouth to alternative sites during hatching operations but there is no evidence of actual mouth brooding (Ref. 13337 ).

entries.name: Toxotes jaculatrix

entries.biology: Occurs primarily in brackish mangrove estuaries, but also penetrates rivers and small streams . Reported to occur near overhanging vegetation on reefs . Usually in small aggregations . Feeds at the surface during daytime on floating debris which includes insects and vegetable matter. It is renowned for its ability to 'shoot down' insect prey by expelling beads of water from its mouth with considerable force and for its remarkable ability to compensate for visual refraction when aiming its shoots; shooting range is about 150 cm . Sold fresh in markets.
